categories_symptomes.guide: Each STI: signs, testing and patterns
intro: STIs are passed on during sex (vaginal, anal or oral), and sometimes through blood or from mother to baby. Many cause no symptoms at all: only a test can tell you.

Where to get tested: at a sexual health clinic (free CeGIDD centers in France), anonymously if you like, with your doctor, a midwife or at a sexual health center. At a lab, without a prescription (in France: “Mon test IST”): the HIV test is free for everyone, and tests for chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis and hepatitis B are also free if you are under 26.
Condoms protect against most STIs. Vaccines exist against hepatitis B, hepatitis A, papillomavirus (HPV) and mpox.
Chinese medicine does not cure an STI. The patterns shown support your body's underlying balance and your comfort (itching, burning, fatigue), always alongside medical treatment.
For any question about STIs, call a helpline (in France: Sida Info Service, 0 800 840 800, free and anonymous, 7 days a week from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m.).
precautions: Sex without a condom, or a condom that broke: go to the emergency room right away (or to a sexual health clinic (free CeGIDD centers in France) during the day) to assess the risk of HIV; emergency treatment (PEP) works best within 4 hours and must be started within 48 hours at the latest. If there is a risk of pregnancy, get emergency contraception at a pharmacy (free and without a prescription in France). Then get tested for STIs.
During an infection, avoid sex until your treatment is finished, and tell your partners so they can get tested.
Don't massage an area with a sore, blisters or warts, and wash your hands after touching it.
rappel: Don't massage an area with a sore, blisters or warts, and wash your hands after touching it.

Hashimoto's or Graves' disease: no iodine supplements and no seaweed (kelp, bladderwrack) without medical advice.

categories_symptomes.note: Rheumatoid arthritis is treated by a rheumatologist, as early as possible. The patterns help with pain, stiffness and fatigue, alongside treatment.
categories_symptomes.guide: Rheumatoid arthritis: key facts and patterns
intro: Rheumatoid arthritis is the most common inflammatory rheumatic disease. It mostly affects women, often between the ages of 40 and 60.
The earlier disease-modifying treatment starts, the better your joints are protected. Physical therapy, occupational therapy and gentle physical activity help a lot.

Chinese medicine looks at the phase you are in: during a flare (heat, swelling), you cool and drain; when things are calm, you warm, get things moving and nourish the Liver and Kidney. Also choose your current signs to find the right pattern.
Patient association (in France: AFPric, Association française des polyarthritiques et des rhumatismes inflammatoires chroniques).
precautions: Flare (red, hot, swollen joints): no heat and no moxa on the joint, only gentle pressure around it.
On methotrexate or a biologic: if you get a fever, a cough or an infection, see a doctor quickly; no herbs and no supplements without your rheumatologist's advice.
A very hot, very painful joint with fever: see a doctor the same day.

categories_symptomes.note: Multiple sclerosis is treated by a neurologist. The patterns show the underlying imbalance often seen with it, to help with fatigue, walking, sleep and mood, alongside treatment.
intro: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a disease of the central nervous system: the immune system damages the sheath around the nerves of the brain and spinal cord. It often begins between the ages of 20 and 40, and more often in women.
Disease-modifying treatments, physical therapy and adapted physical activity are the foundation. The routines in this app can help with fatigue, sleep, digestion and mood.
Patient association (in France: Ligue française contre la sclérose en plaques).
precautions: A new problem (vision, strength, sensation, balance) lasting more than 24 hours: tell your neurologist, it may be a relapse.
Sudden weakness on one side, trouble speaking, loss of vision: call emergency services (15 or 112 in France).
No prolonged heat if it makes your symptoms worse; never a hot-water bottle or moxa on an area with reduced sensation.
No herbs and no supplements without your neurologist's advice.

categories_symptomes.note: Chinese medicine does not cure cancer. It can help you cope better with treatment (fatigue, nausea, sleep, digestion, mood), always with your care team's agreement.
categories_symptomes.guide: Each cancer: treatment side effects and patterns
intro: Cancer is treated with surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, immunotherapy or targeted therapies. Nothing here replaces or delays these treatments.
In Chinese medicine, there is no single “cancer pattern”: we look at the person's underlying balance and at the side effects of treatment. That is what the matches below show.

What often helps, for your comfort and alongside your prescribed medicines: gentle self-massage of PC 6 (on the wrist) for nausea and of ST 36 (below the knee) for fatigue, warm, cooked meals that are easy to digest, rest, and gentle activity such as walking or qi gong.

Supportive care exists and is often free: psychologist, dietitian, adapted physical activity, beauty and wellbeing care. Ask your care team. (In France: Cancer info, 0 805 123 124, free service and call.)
precautions: Tell your oncologist about any herb, herbal tea, supplement or mushroom you take: some change how treatments work (St John's wort, grapefruit, Chinese angelica or dang gui, astragalus, high doses of turmeric or ginseng…).

During and after treatment, use only gentle pressure (tonification), never strong pressure. Skip any point on the tumor, on an area that has been operated on or irradiated, on a stoma, near an implanted port, on the belly after pelvic radiation therapy, or on a swollen arm or leg (lymphedema).
No moxa or hot-water bottle on an irradiated area or an area with reduced sensation, and no moxa (flame, smoke) if you are short of breath or use oxygen at home.
Low white blood cells: avoid raw foods (oysters and shellfish, raw fish, undercooked eggs, raw milk). Low platelets: very gentle pressure only; stop if you bruise.
Fever of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher during chemotherapy: call your care team right away, or emergency services (15 or 112 in France).
rappel: Gentle pressure only, never strong. Skip points on an area that has been operated on or irradiated, a stoma, the belly after pelvic radiation therapy, or a swollen arm or leg.
No moxa on an irradiated area or an area with reduced sensation, and none if you are short of breath or on oxygen.

Recipes: ask your care team before using Chinese angelica (dang gui), astragalus, ginseng or large amounts of turmeric. Low white blood cells: nothing raw (oysters, shellfish, raw fish, undercooked eggs).
Fever of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher during chemotherapy: call your care team or emergency services (15 or 112 in France).

fiches.note: If the tip of your tongue turns red or your sleep gets worse, shorten the moxa on ST 36.

items.loc: Above the kneecap, in the hollow at the middle of its upper edge.
items.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the knee, eases pain and stiffness.

items.loc: Outer side of the leg, in the hollow in front of and below the head of the fibula.
items.act: Hui-Meeting point of the tendons: relaxes the tendons, soothes the knee, moves Liver Qi.

tech: Moxa 2–3 cm (about an inch) from the skin, slow circles above both hollows. Pull it away as soon as it stings.
items.loc: Knee bent, the two hollows on either side of the kneecap tendon: Du Bi on the outside, Nei Xi Yan on the inside.
items.act: Expels Cold-Damp from the knee, gets things moving, calms pain.

tech: Pecking moxa (bring it close, then away, again and again), until you feel a pleasant warmth and slight redness.
items.loc: 3 cun below ST 35, 1 finger-width outside the crest of the shinbone.
items.act: Warms and tonifies the Spleen and Stomach, transforms Dampness at its source, strengthens the knee.

tech: Circular rubbing around the kneecap, until absorbed.
items.loc: Wait 2 to 3 minutes after the moxa. All around the knee, focusing on the “eyes” of the knee and the hollow behind the knee.
items.act: Moves Qi and Blood, calms pain. On days without moxa, use red tiger balm instead.

produits.texte: First choice when warmth relieves the knee. Air out the room, keep a bowl for the ash, and put the stick out by smothering it.
At the end of the session, for massage. Moves Qi and Blood, calms pain.
On days without moxa, rubbed into the knee. Warming.
A neutral base for massaging longer, or for diluting an essential oil.
Only as an extra, always diluted: 2 to 3 drops in a teaspoon of oil. Never with moxa. Avoid if you take blood thinners or are allergic to aspirin.

fiches.regle: Never put heat on a product you have just applied: moxa first, product after.

fiches.contexte: Sugarcane soothes and moistens the Stomach, and a touch of ginger calms and warms it. A juice to sip for nausea, motion sickness and morning sickness in pregnancy.
fiches.precautions: Very sweet: avoid it if you have diabetes. Drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold, and go easy on it if you have a cold belly or soft stools. If you are pregnant and vomit several times a day or can't keep anything down, see your midwife or doctor quickly.

ingredients.nom: plain sugarcane juice, at room temperature
ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores: fresh, bottled or frozen (let it thaw in the fridge). Choose one with no added sugar.

ingredients.nom: fresh ginger (a piece about 3 cm long)

etapes.texte: Peel the ginger ({gingembre}) with the edge of a spoon and grate it finely.
Put the pulp in a square of clean cloth and squeeze it hard over a bowl: you should get about a teaspoon of juice.
Pour the sugarcane juice ({canne}) over the ginger juice and stir. Taste it: add a few more drops of ginger if you want it spicier.
Drink it in small amounts, one or two sips at a time, spread over the day or the journey.
Run the ginger ({gingembre}) through the juicer. With a blender: slice it and blend it with a third of the sugarcane juice ({canne}), then strain through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp well.
Add the rest of the sugarcane juice and stir.
Drink it in small amounts, spread over the day or the journey.

notes: Fresh sugarcane juice turns quickly: keep it in the fridge for 24 hours at most and take it out a little while before drinking.
When traveling, make it in the morning in a small bottle.

fiches.contexte: Celery calms the Liver and cools: a juice for irritability, a chest tight with stress or rising blood pressure. If you have high blood pressure, it goes alongside your medical care and never replaces it.
fiches.precautions: Cooling: drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold, and go easy on it if you have a cold belly, soft stools or low blood pressure. Never change your blood pressure treatment without talking to your doctor. Avoid it if you are allergic to celery.

etapes.texte: Wash the celery ({celeri}) well and cut it into 3 cm pieces.
Run it through the juicer. With a blender: blend it very finely with the water ({eau}).
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp well with the back of a spoon.
Add a pinch of salt ({sel}) if you like. Drink a small glass in the morning and another in the afternoon, away from meals.
Wash the celery ({celeri}), cut it into pieces and drop it into a pot of boiling water.
Drain it and let it cool down a little.
Blend it finely with the water ({eau}), then strain, pressing the pulp well.
Add a little salt ({sel}) if you like. Drink it in two servings over the day, warm or at room temperature.

notes: Blanched celery makes a milder juice that is easier on a sensitive stomach.
Make it the same day: the juice oxidizes quickly.

fiches.contexte: Gently heated and sweetened with honey, celery juice clears the Liver while sparing the Spleen and Stomach. For irritability; with hepatitis, it goes alongside your medical care and never replaces it.

principe.fr: Clear the Liver, strengthen the Spleen

fiches.precautions: Diabetes: use less honey or leave it out. No honey for babies under one year old. Hepatitis: never replace your treatment, and talk to your doctor about it.

ingredients.nom: celery, washed and cut into pieces

etapes.texte: Run the celery ({celeri}) through the juicer. With a blender: blend it finely with the water ({eau}) and strain, pressing the pulp well.
Pour the juice into a small pot and warm it over very low heat, without letting it boil.
Off the heat, let it cool slightly, then stir in the honey ({miel}).
Drink it warm but not scalding, once a day, ideally in the morning.
Run the celery ({celeri}) through the juicer. With a blender: blend it finely with the water ({eau}) and strain, pressing the pulp well.
Pour the juice into a heatproof bowl and cover it with a plate. Set it in a steamer basket or in a pot of simmering water, with the water halfway up the bowl.
Take the bowl out, let it cool slightly, then stir in the honey ({miel}).
Drink it warm but not scalding, once a day.

notes: Honey keeps its qualities better when added to warm juice rather than boiling juice.
You can drink it every day for several weeks: it is a food, not a medicine.

fiches.contexte: For nausea that comes on or gets worse with stress and emotions: Chinese chives get the Qi moving again and a little ginger calms the Stomach.

principe.fr: Move the Qi, harmonize the Stomach

fiches.precautions: Pungent and warming: avoid it if you have mouth ulcers, a dry mouth, heartburn or a stomach ulcer. Drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold. If the nausea lasts more than a few days or you vomit often, see a doctor.

ingredients.note: Sold in bunches in Asian grocery stores: long flat leaves with a mild garlic taste. Don't mix them up with regular chives.

ingredients.nom: fresh ginger (a piece about 3 cm long)

etapes.texte: Wash the chives ({ciboule}) and cut them into pieces. Peel the ginger ({gingembre}) and cut it into thin slices.
Run them through the juicer, then add the water ({eau}). With a blender: blend them with the water until you get a smooth purée.
Strain through a fine sieve or a clean cloth, pressing the pulp well.
Add a little sugar ({sucre}) and stir. Drink half in the morning and the rest in the afternoon, in small sips; add a little water if it is too strong.
Chop the chives ({ciboule}) very finely. Peel the ginger ({gingembre}) and grate it finely.
Put everything in a clean cloth and squeeze it hard over a bowl to collect all the juice. Add the water ({eau}).
Add a little sugar ({sucre}), stir and drink it in two servings over the day, in small sips.

notes: The original recipe uses a large amount of ginger juice: a small dose is enough and makes the juice much easier to drink.
Make it the same day: it quickly loses its strength.

fiches.contexte: Chinese hawthorn berries help you digest fatty meals, get the Blood moving and ease a tight chest. For excess weight or high blood fats, alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Sour: avoid it if you have an acid stomach, heartburn or an ulcer, and don't drink it on an empty stomach. Not during pregnancy: hawthorn moves the Blood. If you take medication for your heart, blood pressure or cholesterol, or a blood thinner, ask your doctor first.

ingredients.nom: dried Chinese hawthorn berries (shan zha), sliced
ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops: small dried red slices with their seeds. They are the berries of the Chinese hawthorn tree.

etapes.texte: Rinse the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) and let them soak in the cold water ({eau}), right in the pot.
Heat over medium heat until it boils.
Lower the heat, cover and let it simmer gently.
Strain, add the whole cane sugar ({sucre}) and stir. Drink it hot or warm, in several cups over the day, after meals.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Rinse the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}), put them in a teapot or a large bowl and pour the boiling water ({eau}) over them. Cover.
Strain, add the whole cane sugar ({sucre}) and drink warm, after the meal. You can top up the same berries with hot water once.

notes: The teapot version is lighter: handy at the office after a big meal.
Avoid store-bought hawthorn candies and flakes, which are very sugary.

fiches.titre: Hawthorn, tangerine peel, ginger and jujube decoction
fiches.contexte: For a heavy, bloated or aching stomach after eating too much or eating badly, sometimes with soft stools. Hawthorn aids digestion, tangerine peel and ginger get the Qi moving, and jujubes protect the Stomach.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have an acid stomach, heartburn or an ulcer. If you are pregnant, ask for advice first: hawthorn moves the Blood. If the pain is strong or lasting, or if the diarrhea comes with fever or blood, see a doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops, as small red slices.
In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops. You can also air-dry the peel of unwaxed organic tangerines for a few days.

etapes.texte: Rinse the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) and tangerine peel ({mandarine}). Slice the ginger ({gingembre}) and slit the jujubes ({dattes}) with a knife.
Put everything in a pot with the cold water ({eau}) and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover and let it simmer gently.
Strain and drink it hot, in two servings, after meals. You can eat the jujubes.

notes: Keep it hot in a thermos to drink over the day.

fiches.titre: Hawthorn and honey drink for sleep
fiches.contexte: For restless nights after a big or late dinner: toasted hawthorn berries aid digestion, the Stomach settles and sleep comes more easily.

principe.py: Xiāo shí hé wèi ān shén
principe.fr: Aid digestion, harmonize the Stomach, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have an acid stomach, heartburn or an ulcer, and during pregnancy. Diabetes: use less honey. If the insomnia lasts more than a few weeks, talk to your doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops, as small red slices.

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) in a frying pan over low heat, stirring, until they turn lightly golden and smell good.
Put them in a heatproof bowl, add the honey ({miel}), stir, then pour in the water ({eau}).
Cover the bowl with a plate and set it in a steamer basket or in a pot of simmering water.
Strain and drink the cup warm, about 30 minutes before going to bed.
Dry-toast the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) in a small pot over low heat, stirring, until they turn lightly golden and smell good.
Pour in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil, then cover and let it simmer over low heat.
Strain, let it cool slightly, then stir in the honey ({miel}).
Drink the cup warm, about 30 minutes before going to bed.

notes: Toast a larger batch of berries at once and keep them in a tightly closed jar.
The original recipe uses far more: this amount for one cup is enough and stays gentle on the stomach.

fiches.contexte: Fresh cilantro and Chinese cardamom (sha ren) wake up the Stomach and help a meal go down. A tea to sip slowly for nausea, including morning sickness in pregnancy.

principe.fr: Wake up the Stomach, ease nausea

fiches.precautions: A little warming: avoid it if you have a dry mouth, thirst and a feeling of heat. If you are pregnant and vomit several times a day, lose weight or can't keep liquids down, see your midwife or doctor quickly.

ingredients.nom: fresh cilantro (a small handful of sprigs)

ingredients.note: In Chinese herbal shops or Asian grocery stores. If you can't find it, use 3 or 4 green cardamom pods, cracked open; they are more fragrant.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Rinse the cilantro ({coriandre}) and chop it roughly, stems included. Lightly crush the cardamom ({cardamome}) with the flat of a knife or in a mortar.
Put them in a bowl or teapot, pour the boiling water ({eau}) over them and cover.
Strain. If the smell bothers you, let it cool for a few minutes, then sip it slowly as soon as it seems pleasant to you.

notes: Make it in the morning in a thermos and take a few sips as soon as a wave of nausea comes.

fiches.contexte: Wood ear mushrooms support the Qi, nourish the Blood and get it moving. For scanty, painful periods toward the end of the cycle, and for constipation: you eat the mushrooms and drink the broth.

principe.fr: Nourish the Blood and get it moving

fiches.precautions: They move the Blood: avoid this drink during pregnancy and if your periods are heavy, and ask your doctor first if you take a blood thinner. Never leave the mushrooms soaking for more than a few hours at room temperature: beyond that, put them in the fridge.

ingredients.note: Sold in bags in Asian grocery stores. They swell a lot: 6 g is a small handful.

etapes.texte: Soak the mushrooms ({champignons}) in a bowl of lukewarm water until they are soft.
Rinse them carefully, remove the small hard base and cut them into strips.
Put them in a pot with the water ({eau}) and the whole cane sugar ({sucre}), then bring to a boil.
Lower to medium-low heat, cover and cook until they are tender.
Eat the mushrooms and drink the hot broth.

notes: For periods, drink it mainly in the days before they start and toward the end of your period.
Throw away the soaking water: it holds the impurities.

fiches.titre: Chrysanthemum, hawthorn and cassia seed tea
fiches.contexte: A drink to have instead of tea, which gets the Blood moving and helps the body clear excess fats. For excess weight and high cholesterol, alongside your medical care, never instead of it.

principe.fr: Move the Blood, clear turbidity (excess fats)

fiches.precautions: Cassia seeds are cooling and mildly laxative: avoid this drink if you have soft stools, diarrhea or low blood pressure. Not during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Also avoid it if you have an acid stomach or an ulcer. If you take medication for cholesterol or blood pressure, or a blood thinner, ask your doctor first. Take breaks: a few weeks on, then one week off.

ingredients.nom: dried Chinese hawthorn berries (shan zha), sliced

ingredients.note: In Chinese herbal shops or Asian grocery stores: small, shiny brown seeds. Nothing to do with Chinese cinnamon, which is also sometimes called cassia.

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the cassia seeds ({cassia}) in a frying pan over low heat, stirring, until they smell toasted.
Let them cool for a moment, then crush them in a mortar, or in a bag with a rolling pin.
Put them in a pot with the hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) and the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then cover and let it simmer.
Off the heat, add the chrysanthemum flowers ({chrysantheme}), cover and let them steep.
Strain and drink it hot or warm, in several cups over the day, instead of tea.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the cassia seeds ({cassia}) in a frying pan over low heat, stirring, until they smell toasted.
Let them cool for a moment, then crush them in a mortar, or in a bag with a rolling pin.
Put the seeds, hawthorn berries ({shanzha}) and flowers ({chrysantheme}) in a large teapot or a thermos. Pour in the boiling water ({eau}) and close.
Drink it warm throughout the day; you can top it up with hot water once.

notes: The original recipe doesn't toast the cassia seeds: toasting makes them gentler on the belly and more fragrant.
Toast a larger batch of seeds ahead of time and keep them in a closed jar.

fiches.titre: Chrysanthemum, sweet apricot kernel and mulberry leaf tea
fiches.contexte: At the start of a cold with a sore throat and cough, when you feel rather hot. Chrysanthemum and mulberry leaves drive out Wind and Heat, and the sweet apricot kernel calms the cough and helps loosen phlegm.

principe.py: Shū fēng qīng rè zhǐ ké
principe.fr: Disperse Wind, clear Heat, calm the cough

fiches.precautions: Only SWEET apricot kernels, never bitter apricot kernels (toxic), and no more than the amount given. Not for young children; if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, ask for advice first. Licorice raises blood pressure: leave it out if you have high blood pressure, swelling (edema) or treatment for your heart or kidneys. A little cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly. High fever, difficulty breathing or a cough lasting more than a week: see a doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops, sold as nan xing ren or "sweet apricot kernels": large, flat and pale. Never buy bitter apricot kernels (bei xing ren, ku xing ren), which are smaller and pointed.
In Chinese herbal shops.
Optional: see the cautions.

etapes.texte: Crush the apricot kernels ({amandons}) in a mortar or with the flat of a knife.
Put them in a pot with the licorice ({reglisse}) and the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then cover and let it simmer.
Off the heat, add the mulberry leaves ({murier}) and the chrysanthemum flowers ({chrysantheme}). Cover and let them steep.
Strain and drink it warm, in small sips, several times over the day.

notes: The traditional recipe uses bitter apricot kernel, a medicinal herb reserved for practitioners: here it is replaced by the sweet kernel, which is safer.
The original recipe steeps everything in boiling water: simmering the kernels first makes them easier to digest.

fiches.contexte: Watermelon cools, quenches thirst and helps you urinate: the juice for heat-wave days, when you feel hot, thirsty and restless. Mint adds freshness.
fiches.precautions: Watermelon is very cooling: drink this juice at room temperature, never ice-cold, and go easy on it if you have a cold belly, soft stools or during your period. Diabetes: one small glass only.

etapes.texte: Cut the watermelon ({pasteque}) into cubes and remove the black seeds.
Blend it with the mint leaves ({menthe}) until very smooth.
Strain it if you prefer a juice without pulp. Drink it right away, at room temperature.
Cut the watermelon ({pasteque}) into pieces, remove the seeds and mash it with a potato masher or a fork in a large bowl.
Pass it through a sieve, pressing the pulp well.
Crush the mint leaves ({menthe}) between your fingers, add them to the juice and let them steep.
Remove the mint and drink the juice at room temperature.

notes: If your watermelon comes straight from the fridge, let the juice come back to room temperature before drinking it.

fiches.contexte: A flavored water that quenches thirst and gently cools you on hot days. Cucumber clears Heat and moistens, and mint brings freshness.
fiches.precautions: Cooling: drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold, and go easy on it if you have a cold belly or soft stools.

etapes.texte: Wash the cucumber ({concombre}) and cut it into thin slices, skin on if it is organic.
Lightly crush the mint leaves ({menthe}) between your fingers to release their scent.
Put everything in a pitcher, pour in the water ({eau}) and let it steep.
Drink it within the day, at room temperature. If it is very hot, keep the pitcher in the fridge, but take it out 30 minutes before drinking.

notes: You can top up the same cucumber with water once.
After one day, throw it all away: the cucumber goes soft.

fiches.contexte: For a dry cough and a scratchy throat, especially in autumn or in dry weather. Pear moistens the Lung, and daikon soothes the cough and helps loosen phlegm.

principe.fr: Moisten the Lung, calm the cough

fiches.precautions: Cooling: drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold, and go easy on it if you have a cold belly, soft stools or a cough with lots of white phlegm. No honey for babies under one year old. A cough lasting more than 3 weeks, fever, blood in your phlegm or shortness of breath: see a doctor.

etapes.texte: Wash the pears ({poire}), core them and cut them into pieces. Dice the daikon ({radis}).
Run them through the juicer. With a blender: blend them with the water ({eau}), then strain, pressing the pulp well.
Add the honey ({miel}) if you like and drink it in two servings over the day, at room temperature.
Finely grate the cored pears ({poire}), then the daikon ({radis}).
Put the grated mixture in a clean cloth and squeeze it hard over a bowl. Thin it with the water ({eau}) if the radish taste is too strong.
Add the honey ({miel}) if you like and drink it in two servings over the day, at room temperature.

notes: If your stomach is delicate, warm the juice for a few minutes in a small pot before drinking it.

fiches.contexte: A mild, nourishing juice that supports the Spleen and Stomach, for small appetites and sluggish digestion. A slice of ginger makes it easier to digest.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, harmonize the Stomach

fiches.precautions: Drink it at room temperature, never ice-cold, preferably mid-morning rather than with meals. Cold belly or soft stools: keep the ginger and stick to a small glass. Diabetes: choose whole fruit instead.

etapes.texte: Wash the apples ({pomme}) and carrots ({carotte}). Core the apples and cut everything into pieces, along with the ginger ({gingembre}).
Run them through the juicer. With a blender: blend them with the water ({eau}), then strain, pressing the pulp well.
Stir and drink right away, in small sips, at room temperature.
Finely grate the cored apples ({pomme}), the peeled carrots ({carotte}) and the ginger ({gingembre}).
Squeeze the grated mixture in a clean cloth over a bowl, then thin it with the water ({eau}).
Stir and drink right away, in small sips, at room temperature.

notes: Drink it right away: it darkens and loses its qualities within a few hours.

fiches.contexte: A hot, caffeine-free drink that tastes of toasted bread. It helps digestion after a heavy or fatty meal and quenches thirst without chilling the Stomach.

principe.fr: Aid digestion, harmonize the Center (Spleen and Stomach)

fiches.precautions: Barley contains gluten: avoid it if you have celiac disease. Breastfeeding: don't drink much of it, as barley is said to reduce milk supply.

ingredients.note: In organic food stores or with the dried beans and grains. Asian grocery stores also sell barley already roasted for tea.

etapes.texte: Dry-roast the barley ({orge}) in a frying pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, until it is golden brown and smells like toasted bread.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil, add the roasted barley, then cover and let it simmer.
Strain and drink hot or warm, after meals or throughout the day.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Dry-roast the barley ({orge}) in a frying pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, until it is golden brown and smells like toasted bread.
Put the roasted barley in a large teapot, pour in the boiling water ({eau}) and cover.
Strain and drink hot or warm. You can top up the same barley with hot water once.

notes: Roast a larger batch ahead of time: it keeps for several weeks in a closed jar.
In summer, you can also drink it at room temperature.

fiches.titre: Honeyed sweet apricot kernels and walnuts
fiches.contexte: A small treat to keep in a jar for a lingering cough in someone who is run-down: sweet apricot kernels moisten the Lung, walnuts strengthen the Kidney, and honey soothes the throat.

principe.py: Bǔ fèi yì shèn zhǐ ké
principe.fr: Tonify the Lung and Kidney, calm the cough

fiches.precautions: Only use sweet apricot kernels (nan xing ren): bitter apricot kernels (bei xing ren or ku xing ren) are toxic and are never used in cooking. Avoid if you are allergic to tree nuts. Rich and sweet: 1 to 2 spoonfuls a day at most, and go easy on it if you have diabetes, soft stools or diarrhea. No honey for babies under one year old. A cough that lasts more than three weeks needs a doctor's opinion.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops, labeled 南杏仁 ("southern apricot kernels", large and flat). Check the label: never 北杏仁 or 苦杏仁, which are the bitter ones.

etapes.texte: Drop the kernels ({amandons}) into a small pot of boiling water, then drain them.
Pinch each kernel between two fingers: the thin brown skin slips right off. If you bought them already peeled, skip this step.
Put the kernels back in the pot with the water ({eau}), bring to a simmer and cook gently, uncovered.
Add the walnuts ({noix}) and keep cooking over low heat, stirring, until there is hardly any liquid left in the bottom.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for a few minutes (honey should not boil), then stir in the honey ({miel}) to coat the nuts well.
Let it cool completely and spoon it into a clean jar. Take one tablespoon in the morning, and another in the evening if needed.

notes: The traditional recipe uses much more honey and family-size amounts: here the quantities are reduced to last about a week.
Keeps for 1 week in the fridge in a tightly closed jar. Take it out a little ahead so you eat it at room temperature.

fiches.contexte: For constipation with dry, hard stools, common in older people, after giving birth or after surgery. Banana moistens the intestines and black sesame nourishes Yin.

principe.fr: Moisten the intestines, ease bowel movements

fiches.precautions: Banana is cold in nature: if you have a cold belly or soft stools, choose the steamed version, and avoid it if you have diarrhea. Use very ripe bananas (green ones are constipating). Diabetes: ripe bananas are sweet, so have just one at a time. Sesame allergy: avoid. Constipation that lasts, pain or blood in the stools: see your doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or organic food stores.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Put the black sesame ({sesame}) in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until it crackles and smells nutty: it should be lightly toasted, not burnt.
Tip it onto a plate right away, or it will keep cooking. You can crush it roughly in a mortar: it is easier to digest.
Peel the bananas ({bananes}), cut them into chunks and roll them in the sesame. Eat right away, as a snack.
Toast the black sesame ({sesame}) in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until it crackles. Tip it onto a plate right away.
Peel the bananas ({bananes}), cut them into chunks, lay them on a plate in the steamer basket and steam until hot and soft.
Sprinkle with sesame and eat warm: cooking makes the banana less cold for the belly.

notes: You can eat this up to three times a day for a few days, while drinking enough warm water.
Toast a small jar of sesame ahead of time: it keeps for 2 weeks, tightly closed.

fiches.contexte: A very simple sweet soup for a dry cough that lingers: peanuts moisten the Lung and bring back a little strength, and rock sugar soothes the throat.

principe.fr: Moisten the Lung, calm the cough

fiches.precautions: Peanut allergy: avoid completely. Peanuts are rich: go easy on them if you digest slowly, or have soft stools or diarrhea. Diabetes: reduce the rock sugar or leave it out. A cough that lasts more than three weeks needs a doctor's opinion.

ingredients.nom: raw shelled peanuts, with their red skins
ingredients.note: Raw and unsalted, from Asian grocery stores or organic food stores (not roasted snack peanuts).
In Asian grocery stores (large white or yellow crystals). If you can't find it, stir in 1 tablespoon of honey off the heat.

etapes.texte: Rinse the peanuts ({cacahuetes}) and soak them in a bowl of cold water: they will cook faster and turn out more tender.
Drain them and put them in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, until they are tender to the bite.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and stir until it melts.
Serve warm in a bowl: eat the peanuts and drink the broth.
Rinse the peanuts ({cacahuetes}) and soak them in a bowl of cold water.
Put the drained peanuts and the water ({eau}) in the pressure cooker. Close it and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Let the pressure drop, open, add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and let it melt over low heat, stirring.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Rinse the peanuts ({cacahuetes}) and soak them in a bowl of cold water.
Put the drained peanuts and the water ({eau}) in the inner pot.
Soup or Slow Cook program.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}), stir and leave for 5 minutes on Keep Warm.

notes: Have it once a day, as a snack, while the cough lasts.
You can add 4 jujubes (Chinese red dates), slit open, at the start of cooking for a sweeter, more nourishing broth.

fiches.contexte: For tiredness with slow digestion and constipation where you push without result: carrot strengthens the Spleen and honey moistens the intestines.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, moisten the intestines

fiches.precautions: Diabetes: halve the honey or replace it with a drizzle of sesame oil. No honey for babies under one year old.

etapes.texte: Peel the carrots ({carottes}) and cut them into half-inch rounds or sticks.
Drop them into the boiling water ({eau}) and cook until the tip of a knife slides through with no resistance.
Drain them and let them cool a little before adding the honey ({miel}), which should not be cooked. Eat warm.
Peel the carrots ({carottes}) and cut them into half-inch rounds or sticks.
Lay them in the steamer basket over the simmering water ({eau}) and steam until very tender.
Let them cool a little before adding the honey ({miel}), which should not be cooked. Eat warm.

notes: Traditionally, this is eaten twice a day, as a snack, for one to two weeks.
Steaming keeps more of the carrot's natural sweetness: you can then use even less honey.

fiches.titre: Cherry and longan compote with goji
fiches.contexte: A warm compote that tonifies Qi and nourishes Blood: for tiredness with a pale complexion, light sleep, eyesight that fades at dusk, or aching joints from lack of Blood. If you have been diagnosed with anemia, it goes alongside your medical care and never replaces it.
fiches.precautions: Longans and cherries are slightly warming: go easy on them if you often feel hot or have a dry mouth or mouth ulcers. Diabetes: no added sugar, and a small portion.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, in bags (龙眼肉). Or 30 g of fresh longans, peeled and pitted.
Out of season, frozen pitted cherries work well.

etapes.texte: Wash the cherries ({cerises}), remove the stems and take out the pits with a small knife or a cherry pitter.
Put the longans ({longanes}) and goji ({goji}) in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a simmer and cook gently until they are nicely plump.
Add the cherries and cook over low heat, just until they soften.
Taste: the fruit is already sweet, so only add the sugar ({sucre}) if needed. Serve warm, with the juice.

notes: This uses more cherries than the traditional recipe, to make a real compote.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge: warm it up gently before eating.

fiches.contexte: A soft steamed cake with walnuts, chestnuts, Chinese yam, longans and goji. It nourishes the Blood and the Yin of the Liver and Kidney and gently warms the Kidney: for a weak or aching lower back and knees, and eyesight that fades at dusk.
fiches.precautions: Contains walnuts and eggs: watch out for allergies (you can replace the walnuts with pumpkin seeds). Sweet and high in flour: a small slice if you have diabetes. Rich and a little sticky: go easy on it if you digest slowly or have a bloated belly.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, in bags (龙眼肉).
Peel it wearing gloves: its sap makes your skin itch. If you can't find it, use sweet potato (the effect on the Kidney is weaker).

ingredients.nom: cooked, peeled chestnuts (vacuum-packed or in a jar)

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores (糯米粉). It gives the cake its soft, slightly springy texture.

etapes.texte: Put the longans ({longanes}) and goji ({goji}) to soak in the lukewarm water ({eau}): they plump up while you prepare the rest.
Peel the yam ({igname}), cut it into chunks and steam until it mashes easily.
Mash the yam while still hot with the chestnuts ({chataignes}), using a fork or a potato masher, until smooth. Let it cool a little.
Beat the eggs ({oeufs}) with the sugar ({sucre}) and add them to the purée. Stir in the glutinous rice flour ({farine}): the batter should be thick and sticky.
Drain the longans and goji. Mix the longans, half the goji and three quarters of the walnuts ({noix}) into the batter.

Oil ({huile}) a 7-inch round pan or a heatproof bowl. Pour in the batter, smooth the top with a wet spoon and sprinkle with the rest of the goji and walnuts. Cover with a sheet of parchment paper so drops of steam don't fall on it.
Set the pan in the steamer basket over rapidly simmering water, lid on. The cake is done when a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let it cool a little before turning it out and cutting it into slices: it firms up as it cools.

notes: Keep the slices for 3 days in the fridge and reheat them for 5 minutes in the steamer.
A wok with a rack and a lid works just as well as a steamer.

fiches.titre: Steamed Chinese yam cake with dried fruit
fiches.contexte: A steamed Chinese yam cake topped with dried fruit and a light glaze, which nourishes Yin and tonifies the Kidney. For tiredness; if you have diabetes, it goes alongside your medical care without replacing it, and only as a small slice.
fiches.precautions: Diabetes: flour, dried fruit and honey raise blood sugar; have a small slice, with your doctor's approval, and leave the honey out of the glaze. Contains wheat (gluten) and walnuts: watch out for allergies. No honey for babies under one year old.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores. Peel it wearing gloves: its sap makes your skin itch.
Coconut oil gives a mild flavor and a more tender dough.
In organic food stores or the baking aisle.

etapes.texte: Peel the yam ({igname}), dice it and steam until very tender.
Mash the hot yam with one tablespoon of the oil ({huile}). Add the flour ({farine}) little by little and mix until you have a soft dough that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Cut the jujubes ({dattes}) into strips, roughly chop the walnuts ({noix}), and rinse the raisins ({raisins}) and goji ({goji}).
Oil a deep plate or an 8-inch pan with the rest of the oil. Spread the dough about 3/4 inch thick and press the topping lightly into the surface.
Steam in the steamer basket, lid on, over rapidly simmering water.
In a small pot, stir the agar-agar ({agar}) into the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil and let it boil, stirring, so it dissolves completely.
Off the heat, wait one minute, then stir the honey ({miel}) into the glaze.
Right away, pour the glaze in a thin layer over the still-warm cake and let it set before cutting it into slices.

notes: Vary the dried fruit with what you have: dried apricots, figs, pumpkin seeds.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge; take it out a while ahead so you eat it at room temperature.

fiches.contexte: A raw, peppery, refreshing salad for the start of a Wind-Heat cold: sore throat, cough with yellowish phlegm, headache or red eyes. Daikon helps clear Phlegm and brings Qi downward.

principe.py: Shū fēng huà tán jiàng qì
principe.fr: Disperse Wind, transform Phlegm, bring Qi down

fiches.precautions: Raw and cooling: limit it if your digestion is weak, or if you have a cold belly or soft stools. High fever, a very sore throat, a sticky eye or a cough that lingers: see your doctor.

ingredients.note: At the market or in Asian grocery stores, sometimes sold as Chinese white radish or mooli.

etapes.texte: Wash and peel the daikon ({radis}). Grate it coarsely, or slice it thinly and then into matchsticks.
Toss it with the salt ({sel}) and let it rest: it releases its water and loses some of its bite.
Squeeze it between your hands over the sink to remove the released water. Taste: if it's too salty, rinse it quickly and squeeze again.
Drizzle with sesame oil ({huile}), toss and serve as a starter or with the meal, at room temperature.

notes: Add a sliced spring onion or a few cilantro leaves if you like.
Keeps for a day in the fridge; take it out 30 minutes before eating.

fiches.contexte: A cooling salad for a cough with thick yellow phlegm, sometimes with wheezing: bamboo shoots and kombu clear Heat, transform Phlegm and bring Qi downward.
fiches.precautions: Very cooling: avoid it if you have a cold belly, soft stools or weak digestion. Kombu is very high in iodine: once or twice a week at most, and ask your doctor if you have a thyroid problem or are pregnant. Soy sauce is salty: go easy on it if you have high blood pressure. Shortness of breath or an asthma attack: see your doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores (海带, hai dai) or organic food stores. The white powder on the surface is normal: don't scrub it off.

ingredients.nom: precooked bamboo shoots (canned or vacuum-packed), drained

etapes.texte: Rinse the kombu ({algues}) and soak it in a large bowl of cold water: it swells and softens.
Drain the kombu and cut it into thin strips. Slice the bamboo shoots ({bambou}) thinly.
Drop the kombu strips into the boiling water ({eau}) and cook until tender.
Add the bamboo shoots to the pot for the last few minutes: this removes the canned taste.
Drain everything and let it cool to lukewarm in the colander.
Arrange on a plate, drizzle with soy sauce ({soja}) and sesame oil ({huile}), toss and serve at room temperature.

notes: You can add a little fresh ginger, cut into fine threads, to soften the cooling effect of the dish.

fiches.contexte: The great classic of Chinese summer salads: cucumber cools and quenches thirst, while garlic and vinegar wake up the appetite and temper its coolness. Ideal in hot weather, when you are thirsty and not very hungry.
fiches.precautions: Raw and cooling: limit it if your digestion is weak, or if you have a cold belly or soft stools. Raw garlic: go easy on it if you have heartburn.

etapes.texte: Wash the cucumber ({concombre}) and lay it on the cutting board. Smash it with one sharp blow of the flat of a large knife or a rolling pin, then cut it into rough chunks.
Salt it ({sel}) and let it release its water, then pour the water off.
Finely chop the garlic ({ail}) and mix it with the vinegar ({vinaigre}), soy sauce ({soja}), sugar ({sucre}) and sesame oil ({huile}).
Pour the dressing over the cucumber, toss and let it rest a little so it soaks up the flavors.

notes: Smashed rather than sliced, the cucumber soaks up the dressing much better.
A little chopped fresh cilantro goes very well with it.

fiches.contexte: A crunchy, tangy salad that cools, opens the appetite and helps you digest a rich meal. Ginger and spring onion temper the cabbage's coolness.
fiches.precautions: Raw and cooling: limit it if your digestion is weak, or if you have a cold belly or soft stools. Vinegar: go easy on it if you have heartburn.

ingredients.nom: Chinese cabbage (napa) heart, the inner leaves
piece of fresh ginger, about 1 inch

etapes.texte: Cut the cabbage ({chou}) crosswise into thin strips. Peel the carrot ({carotte}) and cut it into fine julienne.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the salt ({sel}) and let them rest, then squeeze lightly to remove the released water.
Peel the ginger ({gingembre}) and cut it into fine threads. Slice the spring onion ({cebette}). Mix the vinegar ({vinaigre}), sugar ({sucre}) and sesame oil ({huile}).
Pour the dressing over the vegetables, add the ginger and spring onion, toss and let it rest a little before serving.

notes: Save the tougher outer cabbage leaves for a soup or a stir-fry.

fiches.contexte: A small salad with a taste of the sea: wakame, salty and cooling, helps transform Phlegm and clear excess water; ginger protects the Stomach and black sesame nourishes.
fiches.precautions: Cooling: limit it if your digestion is weak, or if you have a cold belly or soft stools. Seaweed is high in iodine: no more than twice a week, and ask your doctor if you have a thyroid problem or are pregnant. Sesame allergy: avoid.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or organic food stores. It swells enormously: 10 g is enough for two.

etapes.texte: Soak the wakame ({wakame}) in the cold water ({eau}): it unfolds and swells.
Drain it, squeeze it gently and cut any pieces that are too long. Remove any tough ribs.
Mix the ginger ({gingembre}), vinegar ({vinaigre}), soy sauce ({soja}), sugar ({sucre}) and sesame oil ({huile}).
Pour the dressing over the seaweed, toss, sprinkle with black sesame ({sesame}) and let it rest a little before serving.

notes: Add cucumber slices or strips of daikon for a heartier salad.

fiches.contexte: A very simple classic: tofu cools and hydrates, while spring onion brings a little warmth and helps you digest it. Perfect in summer, when you feel hot and have a dry mouth.
fiches.precautions: Cooling: limit it if your digestion is weak, or if you have a cold belly or soft stools, and then choose the blanched version, served warm. Soy allergy: avoid.

etapes.texte: Cut the tofu ({tofu}) into 3/4-inch cubes. Drop them into the lightly salted simmering water ({eau}): this removes the raw soy taste and makes it less cold.
Lift the cubes out gently with a slotted spoon and let them drain and cool slightly.
Finely slice the spring onions ({cebette}), both green and white parts.
Sprinkle the tofu with the spring onion and salt ({sel}), drizzle with soy sauce ({soja}) and sesame oil ({huile}). Toss gently and serve.
Drain the tofu ({tofu}), pat it dry with paper towels and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes.
Finely slice the spring onions ({cebette}), both green and white parts.
Sprinkle the tofu with the spring onion and salt ({sel}), drizzle with soy sauce ({soja}) and sesame oil ({huile}). Toss gently and serve.

notes: Silken tofu is meltingly soft, firm tofu holds its shape better: choose according to your taste.

fiches.titre: Sweet adzuki bean soup with tangerine peel
fiches.contexte: A very common Chinese sweet soup: adzuki beans drain Dampness and help reduce swelling, while tangerine peel moves Qi and eases digestion. For a heavy body, swollen legs and sluggish digestion.
fiches.precautions: Diabetes: reduce the sugar or leave it out (the soup is also good barely sweetened). Adzuki beans make you urinate: go easy on them if you already urinate a lot or are very dry (dry mouth and skin).

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops (陈皮). If you can't find it, use the zest of an organic tangerine, dried for a few days.
Chinese recipes often use twice as much: adjust to your taste.

etapes.texte: Rinse the adzuki beans ({azuki}), cover them generously with cold water and let them soak overnight.
Drain them and put them in a pot with the water ({eau}) and the tangerine peel ({chenpi}). Bring to a boil, then simmer with the lid ajar.
Stir now and then and add a little water if needed: the beans should crush easily between your fingers and the soup should thicken.
Remove the peel, add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and salt ({sel}), and let it melt over low heat.
Rinse the adzuki beans ({azuki}), cover them generously with cold water and let them soak overnight.
Put the drained beans, the water ({eau}) and the tangerine peel ({chenpi}) in the pressure cooker. Close it and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own: the beans finish softening.
Remove the peel, add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and salt ({sel}), and let it melt over low heat.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Rinse the adzuki beans ({azuki}), cover them generously with cold water and let them soak overnight.
Put the drained beans, the water ({eau}) and the tangerine peel ({chenpi}) in the inner pot.
Soup or Slow Cook program.
Remove the peel, add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and salt ({sel}), stir and leave for 5 minutes on Keep Warm.

notes: Eat it hot in winter and warm in summer. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
For a more nourishing version, add 4 jujubes (Chinese red dates) or a handful of lotus seeds with the beans.

fiches.contexte: A summer dessert that cools and quenches thirst: watermelon clears Heat, calms the thirst and restlessness of heat-wave days, and makes you urinate.
fiches.precautions: Watermelon and agar-agar are cold in nature: avoid if you have a cold belly, soft stools, or painful periods relieved by warmth. Eat it at room temperature, never ice-cold. Diabetes: watermelon raises blood sugar quickly, so have a small portion.

ingredients.note: In organic food stores or the baking aisle of supermarkets.

etapes.texte: Remove the seeds from the watermelon ({pasteque}), blend the flesh, then strain it through a fine sieve: you should get about 450 ml of juice.
In a small pot, stir the agar-agar ({agar}) into the water ({eau}), bring to a boil and let it boil, stirring.
Pour the watermelon juice into the pot, whisking quickly, then leave it over low heat without boiling, just so the mixture stays fully liquid.
Pour right away into 4 small glasses or ramekins.
Let it set at room temperature, without putting it in the fridge.
Top each glass with a mint leaf ({menthe}) and serve.

notes: No need for sugar: a really ripe watermelon is sweet enough. A squeeze of lime juice brightens it nicely.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge, well covered; take it out half an hour before eating.

fiches.contexte: Daikon helps the Spleen clear out excess water and Phlegm, and beef strengthens it. A light, complete dish when you tend to feel puffy, retain water or put on weight.

principe.py: Jiàn pí lì shuǐ huà tán
principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, drain Water, transform Phlegm

fiches.precautions: Daikon makes Qi descend: avoid eating it on the same day as a ginseng-based tonic.

ingredients.note: Put it in the freezer for 15 minutes: it slices much more thinly.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Cut the beef ({boeuf}) into thin strips, against the grain: it will stay tender.
Mix it with the soy sauce ({soja}), starch ({fecule}) and a pinch of salt ({sel}). Let it rest while you prepare the daikon.
Peel the daikon ({radis}) and cut it into thin sticks, like very thin fries.
Heat half the oil ({huile}) in the wok over high heat. Stir-fry the daikon with a pinch of salt, stirring often, until it turns translucent and tender. Set it aside on a plate.
Pour the rest of the oil into the hot wok and stir-fry the beef just until it is no longer red.
Return the daikon, stir, pour in the water ({eau}), cover and cook over medium heat.
Scatter the cilantro ({coriandre}) on top at the last moment and serve with rice.

notes: You'll find daikon in Asian grocery stores and often in the produce section of supermarkets. Choose one that feels heavy, firm and smooth.

fiches.titre: Grilled lamb heart skewers with rose
fiches.contexte: Rose soothes the Liver and eases tension, and lamb heart nourishes the Heart. For restless nights full of dreams or nightmares, when you feel on edge during the day.

principe.py: Shū gān yǎng xīn ān shén
principe.fr: Soothe the Liver, nourish the Heart, calm the spirit

fiches.precautions: Avoid during pregnancy (rose moves the Blood). Heart is an organ meat: avoid it if you have gout. If your insomnia lasts more than a few weeks, talk to a doctor.

ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores or herbalists. Never use florist roses: they are sprayed.
Ask your butcher; halal butchers often have it without ordering ahead.

etapes.texte: Put the rosebuds ({rose}) in a small saucepan with the water ({eau}) and salt ({sel}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer gently.
Meanwhile, cut the heart ({coeur}) open. Remove the fat, the white membranes and the small tubes, then rinse it in cold water. Cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Strain the rose water and let it cool until warm. Soak the cubes in it so they absorb the flavor. Keep the rose water for cooking.
Thread the cubes onto skewers (wooden ones soaked in water for 10 minutes so they don't burn) and brush them with oil ({huile}).

Turn on the broiler. Place the skewers on the rack, about 10 cm from the heating element. Halfway through, dip them in the rose water and turn them over. The heart should be browned outside and barely pink in the center, or it turns tough.
Serve right away with rice and a green vegetable, ideally at dinner.

variantes.nom: In a grill pan or on a griddle

etapes.texte: Put the rosebuds ({rose}) in a small saucepan with the water ({eau}) and salt ({sel}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer gently.
Meanwhile, cut the heart ({coeur}) open. Remove the fat, the white membranes and the small tubes, then rinse it in cold water. Cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Strain the rose water and let it cool until warm. Soak the cubes in it so they absorb the flavor. Keep the rose water for cooking.
Thread the cubes onto skewers and brush them with oil ({huile}).
Heat a grill pan or griddle over high heat. Grill the skewers, turning them often, and brush them with rose water two or three times as they cook.
Serve right away with rice and a green vegetable, ideally at dinner.

notes: With fresh unsprayed roses (from your garden, for example), use 30 g of petals for the same amount of water.

fiches.contexte: Lotus leaf helps clear Dampness and fat, and duck strengthens without weighing you down. For excess weight and cellulite; if your cholesterol or triglycerides are high, this dish supports your medical care, it does not replace it.
fiches.precautions: Duck and lotus leaf are rather cooling: if you often have a cold belly and soft stools, don't leave out the ginger and pepper. Glutinous rice is a little heavy: eat slowly.

ingredients.note: Ask your butcher to bone them. Skinless duck breasts work too.
From Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbalists, sold as large folded discs.

etapes.texte: Break the star anise ({badiane}) into pieces. Toast it with the glutinous rice ({riz}) in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the rice turns golden and smells toasty.
Let it cool a little, then grind everything in a coffee grinder or blender into a fairly fine powder. A few bigger bits are normal.

Cut the duck ({canard}) into 3 cm pieces. Mix it with the soy sauce ({soja}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), pepper ({poivre}) and water ({eau}). Cover and refrigerate (1 hour minimum). Meanwhile, soak the lotus leaf ({lotus}) in a large basin of hot water.
Lightly salt the duck ({sel}), add the rice powder and mix to coat each piece well.

Drain and wipe the lotus leaf, then cut it into 4. Divide the duck among the pieces, placing it in the center, and fold the edges over to make tightly closed parcels. Set them seam side down in a deep plate.
Put the plate in the steamer basket over boiling water, cover and steam over medium heat. Check the water level every 30 minutes and top up with boiling water.
Open the parcels at the table and serve with rice or a green vegetable. The leaf flavors the meat but is not eaten.

Let it cool a little, then grind everything in a coffee grinder or blender into a fairly fine powder. A few bigger bits are normal.

Cut the duck ({canard}) into 3 cm pieces. Mix it with the soy sauce ({soja}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), pepper ({poivre}) and water ({eau}). Cover and refrigerate (1 hour minimum). Meanwhile, soak the lotus leaf ({lotus}) in a large basin of hot water.
Lightly salt the duck ({sel}), add the rice powder and mix to coat each piece well.

Drain and wipe the lotus leaf, then cut it into 4. Divide the duck among the pieces, placing it in the center, and fold the edges over to make tightly closed parcels. Set them seam side down in a deep plate.
Pour 500 ml of water into the pressure cooker and set the steamer basket with the plate of parcels on top. Close it and start timing once the valve starts hissing, over low heat.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own before opening.
Open the parcels at the table and serve with rice or a green vegetable. The leaf flavors the meat but is not eaten.

notes: Without a lotus leaf, wrap the duck in parchment paper: the dish is still good, but it loses the leaf's aroma and draining effect.
You can make one big parcel with the whole leaf: add 15 minutes of cooking time.

fiches.contexte: Green tea is cooling, and carp strengthens the body without heating it. Tradition makes this dish when thirst is intense and the mouth is dry. If you have diabetes, this dish supports your medical care: it replaces neither your treatment nor your blood sugar checks.

principe.py: Qīng rè bǔ xū zhǐ kě
principe.fr: Clear Heat, tonify Deficiency, relieve thirst

fiches.precautions: Green tea is cooling: go easy on this dish if you have a cold belly and soft stools. Carp has many small bones: be careful with children.

ingredients.nom: whole carp (600 to 800 g), gutted and scaled
ingredients.note: From the fishmonger; very common in eastern France. Otherwise: a sea bass or sea bream.

etapes.texte: Rinse the carp ({carpe}) in cold water, inside and out. Remove the thin black lining inside the belly: that's what gives the muddy taste. Pat it dry and make 2 or 3 slashes on each side.
Sprinkle the green tea ({the}) with 2 tablespoons of hot water so the leaves unfurl.
Tuck the tea leaves into the belly and the slashes. Lay the carp in a deep plate that fits in your steamer basket (remove the head if needed).
Once the water is at a rolling boil, put the plate in the basket, cover and steam over high heat. The flesh should come away easily from the backbone.
Remove the tea leaves and eat the flesh plain, with no sauce or spices, with rice. Watch out for bones.
Rinse the carp ({carpe}) in cold water, inside and out. Remove the thin black lining inside the belly: that's what gives the muddy taste. Pat it dry and make 2 or 3 slashes on each side.
Sprinkle the green tea ({the}) with 2 tablespoons of hot water so the leaves unfurl. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
Lay the carp on a large sheet of parchment paper. Tuck the tea leaves into the belly and the slashes, then fold into a tightly sealed parcel.
Bake on the middle rack. The flesh should come away easily from the backbone.
Remove the tea leaves and eat the flesh plain, with no sauce or spices, with rice. Watch out for bones.

notes: Plain, the flavor is very mild. A dash of soy sauce at the table is fine, but tradition eats it unseasoned.

fiches.contexte: Winter melon is cooling and helps clear excess water, and shiitake mushrooms support the Spleen. A light side dish when you feel puffy, retain water or want to lose weight.
fiches.precautions: A cooling dish: if you have a cold belly and soft stools, keep the ginger and eat it piping hot.

ingredients.nom: winter melon (dong gua), peeled and seeded
ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores, often sold by the slice. Otherwise: zucchini (shorter cooking time).

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Soak the shiitake ({shiitake}) in the lukewarm water ({eau}) until soft.
Cut the winter melon ({courge}) into 1.5 cm cubes. Drain the shiitake, keeping the soaking water, remove the tough stems and slice the caps.
Heat the oil ({huile}) in the wok, let the ginger ({gingembre}) sizzle for a few seconds, then add the melon and mushrooms. Stir-fry over high heat.
Pour in the soaking water, leaving the grit at the bottom of the bowl. Cover and cook over medium heat until the melon turns translucent.
Add salt ({sel}) and the soy sauce ({soja}), and let the liquid reduce uncovered, stirring. Serve with rice.

notes: With fresh shiitake: 150 g, sliced, no soaking, and 100 ml of water instead of the soaking water.

fiches.contexte: Winter melon strengthens the Spleen and moves Water: a gentle remedy when your legs, ankles or face swell and you retain water. Eaten without salt, it drains better.

principe.py: Jiàn pí lì shuǐ xiāo zhǒng
principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, drain Water, reduce swelling

fiches.precautions: Swelling (edema) should be checked by a doctor: it can come from the heart, the kidneys or the circulation. This dish supports your medical care, it does not replace it. A cooling dish: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools.

ingredients.nom: winter melon (dong gua), with its skin and seeds
ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores, often sold by the slice.

etapes.texte: Scrub the skin of the melon ({courge}) well under running water. Without peeling it, cut it into 3 to 4 cm chunks. Keep the seeds: together with the skin, they are the most draining parts.
Put the chunks in a bowl with the ginger ({gingembre}) and set it in the steamer basket over boiling water. Cover. The flesh should be translucent and tender when pierced with a knife.
Eat it hot, without salt, with rice, and drink the juice left in the bowl. Leave the skin, too tough to eat, on the side of your plate: it has already passed its benefits into the juice.
Scrub the skin of the melon ({courge}) well under running water. Without peeling it, cut it into 3 to 4 cm chunks. Keep the seeds: together with the skin, they are the most draining parts.
Start your rice as usual. For the last 20 minutes, set the steamer basket on top with the melon and ginger ({gingembre}) in a bowl, then close the lid.
Eat it hot, without salt, with the rice, and drink the juice left in the bowl. Leave the skin, too tough to eat, on the side of your plate: it has already passed its benefits into the juice.

notes: Tradition recommends it at every meal for a few days, always with rice and without salt.
If it tastes too bland, add a few drops of rice vinegar rather than salt.

fiches.titre: Stuffed flatbreads with daikon and tangerine peel
fiches.contexte: Daikon and tangerine peel move the Qi and help the Stomach digest. For slow digestion and a stomach that feels heavy, full or sore after meals.

principe.py: Lǐ qì jiàn wèi xiāo shí
principe.fr: Regulate Qi, strengthen the Stomach, aid digestion

fiches.precautions: Tangerine peel is slightly drying: go easy on it if you have a dry mouth or a dry cough. Frequent or severe stomach pain should be checked by a doctor.

ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbalists.

ingredients.nom: ground chicken (or chicken breast finely chopped with a knife)
ingredients.note: Meat-free version: 150 g of crumbled firm tofu or chopped shiitake mushrooms.

etapes.texte: Put the tangerine peel ({mandarine}) in a small saucepan with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered.
Strain it: you should have about 150 ml of liquid left. Let it cool until warm. Finely chop half of the softened peel for the filling.
Mix the flour ({farine}) and a pinch of salt ({sel}) in a bowl. Gradually pour in the warm liquid while stirring, then knead until you have a soft dough that no longer sticks. Cover and let it rest.

Meanwhile, grate the daikon ({radis}) on the large holes of a grater. Stir-fry it in a spoonful of oil ({huile}) with a pinch of salt: it should stay a little crunchy. Let it cool, then squeeze it in your hands to remove the juice.
Mix the daikon with the chicken ({poulet}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), chopped peel, soy sauce ({soja}) and the rest of the salt.

Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a 12 cm disc. Put a heaped spoonful of filling in the center, bring the edges up to the middle in pleats and pinch to seal. Gently flatten into a round, seam side down.
Place the flatbreads on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, brush them with oil and bake at 200 °C (400 °F) until nicely golden.
Let them cool for 5 minutes before biting in: the filling is scalding. Serve with a broth or vegetables.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the flatbreads, cover and let them brown.
Flip them, cover again and brown the other side. The chicken must be cooked all the way through.
Let them cool for 5 minutes before biting in: the filling is scalding. Serve with a broth or vegetables.

notes: The flatbreads freeze well uncooked: cook them straight from frozen, adding 5 to 10 minutes.
You can dry your own peel from organic tangerines: a few weeks in the open air, somewhere dry.

fiches.contexte: Nutmeg and star anise warm the Kidney and Spleen, and kidneys strengthen the Kidney. For fatigue, lingering lower back pain and chronic diarrhea, especially the early-morning kind.

principe.py: Wēn shèn jiàn pí zhǐ xiè
principe.fr: Warm the Kidney, strengthen the Spleen, stop diarrhea

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: avoid it if you have Heat (thirst, dry mouth, fever) or burning diarrhea. Nutmeg: no more than the amount given, and not during pregnancy. Kidneys: avoid if you have gout. Diarrhea lasting more than 2 weeks should be checked by a doctor.

ingredients.note: From the butcher: choose very fresh, firm kidneys with no strong smell.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Put the star anise ({badiane}) in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil and simmer, covered.
Meanwhile, remove the thin membrane from the kidneys ({rognons}). Halve them horizontally and snip out the white core and tubes with scissors.
Put them in a bowl of cold water with the vinegar ({vinaigre}) and let them soak. Rinse them well afterward.
Score the rounded side of each half in a fine crisscross, without cutting through, then cut it in two: the pieces will open like flowers as they cook.
Remove the star anise and bring the liquid back to a boil. Drop in the kidneys and drain them as soon as they change color.
Heat the oil ({huile}) in the wok over medium heat with the Sichuan peppercorns ({sichuan}). Scoop out the peppercorns with a slotted spoon as soon as they darken.
Turn up the heat and stir-fry the kidneys briskly. They should stay tender: overcooked, they turn tough.
Grate the nutmeg ({muscade}) over them, add salt ({sel}), stir and take off the heat at once. Serve right away with rice.

notes: Veal kidneys work too: cut them into pieces of the same size.

fiches.titre: Lamb's liver with soy sauce and vinegar
fiches.contexte: Lamb's liver nourishes the Liver and Blood, which in turn nourish the eyes. Tradition uses it when you see poorly in the evening or in dim light; also have your eyes checked by an eye doctor, as this dish supports that care.

principe.fr: Nourish the Liver, brighten the eyes

fiches.precautions: Liver is very rich in vitamin A: not during pregnancy, and no more than once or twice a week, even though tradition recommends it daily. Avoid if you have gout.

ingredients.note: Choose it very fresh and glossy, from the butcher.

ingredients.nom: rice vinegar or Chinese black vinegar

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Remove the thin membrane and the vessels from the liver ({foie}). Rinse it, pat it dry and cut it into 5 mm slices.
Stir the starch ({fecule}) into the water ({eau}), add the slices and mix to coat them well.
In a bowl, mix the soy sauce ({soja}), vinegar ({vinaigre}) and sugar ({sucre}).
Heat the oil ({huile}) in the wok over high heat. Spread out the slices, let them sear without touching them, then flip them.
Add the ginger ({gingembre}) and spring onion ({cebette}), pour in the sauce and stir-fry until the liver is just cooked and still tender.
Serve right away with rice: liver turns tough if it waits.

notes: Chinese black vinegar gives the most authentic flavor; cider vinegar will do in a pinch.
Chicken livers can be cooked the same way.

fiches.titre: Lamb's liver stir-fried with Chinese chives
fiches.contexte: Chinese chives warm the Kidney, and lamb's liver nourishes the Liver and Blood. For lingering lower back pain, dizziness, blurred vision, cramps, and scanty or dully painful periods.

principe.fr: Warm and tonify the Liver and Kidney

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: avoid it if you have Heat (red eyes, bitter taste in the mouth, mouth ulcers). Liver is very rich in vitamin A: not during pregnancy, and better 2 or 3 times a week than every day. Dizziness or very irregular periods deserve a doctor's opinion.

ingredients.note: Sold in bunches in Asian grocery stores: flat leaves, mild garlicky taste. Otherwise, a young leek, very thinly sliced.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Remove the thin membrane and the vessels from the liver ({foie}), then cut it into thin slices. Wash the Chinese chives ({ciboule}), pat them dry and cut them into 4 cm lengths, keeping the firmer white ends separate.
Heat the oil ({huile}) in the wok over high heat. Stir-fry the liver until it is no longer red on the surface.
Add the white ends first, then the leaves. Stir-fry just until they wilt.
Add salt ({sel}) and the soy sauce ({soja}), stir and serve right away with rice.

notes: For period problems, eat it preferably in the week after your period, when the Blood is rebuilding.

fiches.contexte: Daikon helps the Stomach digest and dissolves Phlegm. A snack or side dish for a heavy stomach, bloating after meals and phlegm.

principe.py: Jiàn wèi xiāo shí huà tán
principe.fr: Strengthen the Stomach, aid digestion, transform Phlegm

fiches.precautions: Dried shrimp are salty: taste before adding salt, especially if you watch your blood pressure. Shellfish allergy: replace them with 2 extra shiitake mushrooms.

ingredients.note: Sold in bags in Asian grocery stores.
From Asian grocery stores or the gluten-free aisle.

etapes.texte: Soak the dried shrimp ({crevettes}) and the shiitake ({shiitake}) in two bowls of lukewarm water (on top of the water in the recipe).

Meanwhile, peel the daikon ({radis}) and grate it on the large holes of a grater. Put it in a saucepan with its juice and a third of the water ({eau}). Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, until translucent.
Drain the shrimp and mushrooms, remove the shiitake stems and roughly chop everything. Sauté in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}).

In a bowl, stir the rice flour ({farine}) and salt ({sel}) into the rest of the water. Add the hot daikon with its juice, the topping and the chives ({ciboulette}). Mix: the batter should be thick but still pourable.
Oil a 20 cm round pan, or a deep dish that fits in your steamer basket. Pour in the batter and smooth the top.
Steam over high heat, covered. Halfway through, top up the pot with boiling water. A chopstick inserted in the center should come out almost clean.
Let it cool completely: the cake firms up as it cools and then slices cleanly.
Unmold and cut into 1 cm slices. Reheat them by steaming, or brown them for 2 to 3 minutes per side in an oiled frying pan.
Soak the dried shrimp ({crevettes}) and the shiitake ({shiitake}) in two bowls of lukewarm water (on top of the water in the recipe).

Meanwhile, peel the daikon ({radis}) and grate it on the large holes of a grater. Put it in a saucepan with its juice and a third of the water ({eau}). Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, until translucent.
Drain the shrimp and mushrooms, remove the shiitake stems and roughly chop everything. Sauté in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}).

In a bowl, stir the rice flour ({farine}) and salt ({sel}) into the rest of the water. Add the hot daikon with its juice, the topping and the chives ({ciboulette}). Mix: the batter should be thick but still pourable.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Oil a 20 cm round pan, pour in the batter, smooth the top and cover with aluminum foil.
Set the pan in a large dish filled halfway up with hot water and put it in the oven. A knife inserted in the center should come out almost clean.
Let it cool completely: the cake firms up as it cools and then slices cleanly.
Unmold and cut into 1 cm slices. Reheat them by steaming, or brown them for 2 to 3 minutes per side in an oiled frying pan.

notes: The cake keeps for 4 days in the fridge, well wrapped, and freezes well in slices.

fiches.contexte: Chinese yam gently nourishes Yin and consolidates Essence. For menopause symptoms (hot flashes, night sweats) and, if you have diabetes, as support for your medical care, never in its place.
fiches.precautions: It is starchy: if you have diabetes, it replaces the rice or bread in your meal, it is not added on top. Avoid it if your belly is bloated and your digestion feels very clogged.

ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores: a long, beige, hairy root. African yam is a different plant.

etapes.texte: Scrub the yam ({igname}) under running water and cut it into 8 to 10 cm lengths without peeling: cooked in its skin, you won't have to touch its sap, which makes your skin itch.
Place the pieces in the steamer basket over boiling water. Cover and steam until a knife tip slides in with no resistance.
Let it cool for a moment, then remove the skin: it slips right off.
Slice it into rounds and add just a little salt ({sel}) if you like. Eat it in place of the rice or bread in your meal.
Scrub the yam ({igname}) under running water and cut it into 8 to 10 cm lengths without peeling: cooked in its skin, you won't have to touch its sap, which makes your skin itch.
Pour water into the inner pot as the manual says, put the yam in the steamer basket and start the Steam program.
Let it cool for a moment, then remove the skin: it slips right off.
Slice it into rounds and add just a little salt ({sel}) if you like. Eat it in place of the rice or bread in your meal.

notes: Tradition recommends it twice a day, in place of your usual starch.
It keeps for one to two weeks in the fridge, wrapped in newspaper.

fiches.contexte: Spinach is cooling and nourishes the Liver, and fish is light. For dizziness, irritability and pressure rising to the head; if you have high blood pressure, this dish supports your medical care, it does not replace it.

principe.py: Qīng rè chú fán píng gān
principe.fr: Clear Heat, calm agitation, settle the Liver

fiches.precautions: A cooling dish: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools. If you have high blood pressure, use very little salt. If you have kidney stones, don't eat spinach too often.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Trim the stems of the spinach ({epinards}), wash the leaves in plenty of water and cut the largest ones in half.
Plunge them into a large pot of boiling water just until they wilt. Drain and squeeze them gently.
Cut the fish ({poisson}) into 1 cm strips, salt them lightly ({sel}) and roll them in the starch ({fecule}).
Heat the oil ({huile}) in the wok over medium heat. Brown the garlic ({ail}), then add the ginger ({gingembre}) and onion ({oignon}). Stir until fragrant.
Turn up the heat, add the fish and water ({eau}). Turn the strips gently, without stirring too much so they don't break.
Add the spinach and stir gently, just to heat it through. Serve right away with rice.

notes: Blanching removes the spinach's bitterness and some of its oxalic acid.

fiches.contexte: Rabbit strengthens the Spleen and Stomach without weighing you down, black sesame moistens the intestines and cloves bring warmth. For fatigue, excess weight and dry stools.

principe.py: Jiàn pí hé wèi rùn cháng
principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, harmonize the Stomach, moisten the intestines

fiches.precautions: Black sesame moistens the intestines: use less if you have soft stools or diarrhea.

ingredients.nom: rabbit pieces (2 legs and a saddle)
ingredients.note: In the poultry section or from the butcher.

etapes.texte: Toast the black sesame seeds ({sesame}) in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring, until they crackle and smell nutty. Tip them into a bowl.
Put the rabbit pieces ({lapin}) in a large pot of cold water and bring to a boil. Let it boil, then discard the water and rinse the pieces.
