Return the rabbit to the pot with the water ({eau}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), cloves ({girofle}), soy sauce ({soja}) and salt ({sel}). Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat with the lid ajar, turning the pieces now and then.
Remove the lid and let it reduce until only a little syrupy liquid is left, 3 to 4 tablespoons. The meat should come away from the bone.
Arrange the rabbit on a platter. Strain the liquid, add the toasted sesame and the sesame oil ({huile-sesame}), then spoon it over the pieces. Serve with rice.
Toast the black sesame seeds ({sesame}) in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring, until they crackle and smell nutty. Tip them into a bowl.
Put the rabbit pieces ({lapin}) in the pressure cooker, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Let it boil, then discard the water and rinse the pieces.

Return the rabbit to the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), cloves ({girofle}), soy sauce ({soja}) and salt ({sel}). Close it and start timing once the valve starts hissing, over low heat.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own before opening.
Boil uncovered until only a little syrupy liquid is left, 3 to 4 tablespoons.
Arrange the rabbit on a platter. Strain the liquid, add the toasted sesame and the sesame oil ({huile-sesame}), then spoon it over the pieces. Serve with rice.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Toast the black sesame seeds ({sesame}) in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring, until they crackle and smell nutty. Tip them into a bowl.
Put the rabbit pieces ({lapin}) in a large pot of cold water and bring to a boil. Let it boil, then discard the water and rinse the pieces.
Put the rabbit in the inner pot with the water ({eau}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), cloves ({girofle}), soy sauce ({soja}) and salt ({sel}). Slow Cook or Soup program.
Take out the rabbit and keep it warm. Pour the liquid into a small saucepan (or use the appliance's Sauté mode) and boil it uncovered down to 3 or 4 tablespoons.
Arrange the rabbit on a platter. Strain the liquid, add the toasted sesame and the sesame oil ({huile-sesame}), then spoon it over the pieces. Serve with rice.

notes: Tradition suggests it twice a week, as a course lasting a few weeks: half at lunch, the other half at dinner.
Four cloves are enough for flavor: any more and the sauce turns bitter.

fiches.titre: Chicken stir-fry with carrots and tangerine peel
fiches.contexte: Tangerine peel moves the Qi, and carrot strengthens the Spleen. For a tight, bloated or sore stomach and difficult digestion, especially when stress is involved.
fiches.precautions: Tangerine peel is drying: go easy on it if you have a dry mouth or a dry cough. Frequent or severe stomach pain should be checked by a doctor.

ingredients.note: From Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbalists.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Soak the tangerine peel ({mandarine}) in a bowl of lukewarm water until soft.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken ({poulet}) into thin strips and mix it with the soy sauce ({soja}) and starch ({fecule}).

Cut the carrots ({carottes}) into matchsticks, or grate them on the large holes of a grater. Drain the peel, scrape off the white pith inside if it's thick, and cut it into thin strips. Thinly slice the spring onion ({cebette}).
Heat half the oil ({huile}) in the wok and stir-fry the carrots over high heat. Set them aside on a plate.
Pour in the rest of the oil and stir-fry the chicken with the strips of peel until it turns white.
Return the carrots, salt lightly ({sel}), pour in the water ({eau}), cover and cook over medium heat.
Scatter the spring onion on top and serve with rice.

notes: The older the tangerine peel, the mellower and more fragrant it is.
The same recipe works with strips of beef.

fiches.contexte: A classic recipe to settle the Heart and the mind: it tonifies Qi and nourishes Yin. For restless nights, nervousness, frayed emotions, and menopausal hot flashes with night sweats.

principe.fr: Nourish the Heart, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Licorice raises blood pressure and makes the body hold on to water: avoid this dish if you have high blood pressure, swollen legs (edema), heart or kidney disease, and during pregnancy. If you take any medication (diuretics, cortisone, heart medication), ask your doctor first. No more than 2 to 3 weeks in a row. Contains gluten.

ingredients.note: In organic stores, in the grains aisle (soft wheat or spelt berries).
From a Chinese herbal shop or a specialist pharmacy. The traditional recipe uses up to 15 g; 10 g is enough at home.

etapes.texte: The day before, rinse the wheat ({ble}) and leave it to soak overnight in a large bowl of cold water.
Put the licorice ({reglisse}) in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on.
Lift out the licorice slices with a slotted spoon, or strain the decoction and pour it back into the pot.

Drain the wheat and add it to the decoction with the jujubes ({dattes}). Cook over low heat with the lid ajar, stirring now and then: the grains should burst open and the broth thicken. Add a little hot water if it runs low.
Divide between two bowls: one in the morning, one in the evening, warm. Eat the grains and the jujubes (watch out for the pits).
The day before, rinse the wheat ({ble}) and leave it to soak overnight in a large bowl of cold water.
Put the licorice ({reglisse}) in the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}), without locking the lid. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Lift out the licorice slices with a slotted spoon.
Add the drained wheat and the jujubes ({dattes}). Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Let the pressure drop on its own, then open and stir: it should be creamy. Serve in two parts, morning and evening.

notes: You can make it in the evening for the next day: it keeps 2 days in the fridge. Reheat it with a little water.
It's usually taken for 1 to 2 weeks. If sleep problems persist, talk to a practitioner.

fiches.contexte: Oysters nourish Liver and Kidney Yin and help bring down the Yang that rises to the head: headaches, dizziness, irritability, night sweats. If you have high blood pressure, this broth goes alongside your medical care, it never replaces it.

principe.fr: Nourish Yin, bring the Yang back down

fiches.precautions: Seafood allergy: avoid. The oysters must be very fresh (tightly closed shells) and cooked. Slightly cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools. If you have high blood pressure, use very little salt and keep taking your treatment.

ingredients.note: Ask your fishmonger to open them and give you the shells separately. If you have no shells: 30 g of crushed oyster shell (mu li) from a Chinese herbal shop.

etapes.texte: Open the oysters ({huitres}) over a bowl to catch their liquor. Loosen the flesh and keep it in the fridge. Scrub the empty shells under cold water.
Put the shells in a large pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on, over low heat.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and discard the shells. Add the strained oyster liquor, the soy sauce ({soja}) and the salt ({sel}), then bring back to a simmer.
Drain the oysters and roll them in the starch ({fecule}): they'll stay tender.
Slip the oysters into the simmering broth with the ginger ({gingembre}). Don't let it boil hard: they're done when their edges curl.
Off the heat, add the chives ({ciboulette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.
Open the oysters ({huitres}) over a bowl to catch their liquor. Loosen the flesh and keep it in the fridge. Scrub the empty shells under cold water.
Put the shells in the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}). Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own.
Strain the broth and discard the shells. Add the strained oyster liquor, the soy sauce ({soja}) and the salt ({sel}), then bring back to a simmer with the lid off.
Drain the oysters and roll them in the starch ({fecule}).
Slip the oysters into the simmering broth with the ginger ({gingembre}), without letting it boil hard.
Off the heat, add the chives ({ciboulette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: The oyster liquor is already salty: taste before adding salt.
The shell broth keeps 2 days in the fridge: then you only need to poach the oysters at the last minute.

fiches.contexte: A gentle soup that nourishes Yin and replenishes body fluids: for a dry mouth, thirst and constipation with dry stools. If you have diabetes, it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly or soft stools. Spinach is rich in oxalates (limit it if you get kidney stones) and in vitamin K: if you take an anticoagulant, keep the amounts steady and talk to your doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, as pale golden balls in bags.

etapes.texte: Soak the tremella ({tremelle}) in a large bowl of warm water: it will swell and soften.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base of the tremella, then tear it into small pieces. Wash the spinach ({epinards}) in plenty of water and chop it roughly.
Put the tremella in the water ({eau}) with the ginger ({gingembre}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on: it should turn tender and slightly jelly-like.
Add the spinach and cook just until it wilts.
Add salt ({sel}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}), and serve hot, with rice or bread.
Soak the tremella ({tremelle}) in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard base of the tremella and tear it into small pieces. Wash the spinach ({epinards}) and chop it roughly.
Put the tremella, water ({eau}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the pressure cooker. Lock the lid and start timing once it reaches pressure, over low heat.
Let the pressure drop, open, add the spinach and let it simmer uncovered.
Add salt ({sel}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}), and serve hot.

notes: You can have it once or twice a day, for 3 to 4 weeks.
For a less astringent soup, blanch the spinach for 1 minute in another pot first.

fiches.contexte: A light soup that helps transform Phlegm (mucus) and clear Heat. It's also recommended for high cholesterol: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Seaweed is very rich in iodine: if you have a thyroid problem (nodule, goiter, thyroid medication), ask your doctor before eating it often. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools.

ingredients.note: The sheets used for sushi rolls (Asian aisle of supermarkets), or about 5 g of zicai seaweed cakes from Asian grocery stores.
Optional: the soup is just as good without chicken.

etapes.texte: Cut the tofu ({tofu}) into cubes and the chicken ({poulet}) into thin strips. Tear the nori ({nori}) into pieces.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the ginger ({gingembre}).
Slide the tofu into the broth and wait for it to come back to a boil. Add the chicken strips, separating them, and simmer until they're white all the way through.
Add the nori at the very end: it unfurls in a few seconds.
Add salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and drizzle with a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: Plant-based version: leave out the chicken, or replace it with a few sliced shiitake mushrooms added at the same time as the tofu.

fiches.titre: Capillary wormwood, sprouted barley and jujube soup
fiches.contexte: Capillary wormwood clears Heat and drains Dampness from the Liver; sprouted barley and jujubes look after the Spleen and Stomach. It is traditionally given for hepatitis: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Hepatitis, jaundice (yellow skin or eyes), dark urine: see your doctor first; this soup does not replace any treatment. A cooling herb: not if you have a cold belly and soft stools. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding (sprouted barley can reduce milk supply). If you take any medication, ask a practitioner for advice.

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop or a pharmacy that stocks Chinese herbs.
From the same place as the capillary wormwood.

etapes.texte: Quickly rinse the wormwood ({yinchen}), the sprouted barley ({maiya}) and the jujubes ({dattes}).
Put them in a pot with the cold water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer over low heat with the lid on.
Strain, keeping the jujubes and discarding the rest. Sweeten lightly ({sucre}) if you like.
Drink half a bowl, warm, twice a day, morning and evening, and eat the jujubes.

notes: Keep the second serving in the fridge and reheat it gently before drinking.

fiches.titre: Spring onion and fermented black soybean soup
fiches.contexte: A kitchen remedy for the very first signs of a cold caught from the cold: chills, clear runny nose, sneezing, with no thirst and no sore throat. It opens the Exterior (the outer layer of the body) to bring on a light sweat and drive out the Cold.
fiches.precautions: Only for a cold from the cold that is just starting. Not if you have a sore throat, a high fever or yellow mucus. Sweat lightly, not heavily. See a doctor if the fever rises, if you have trouble breathing or if it lasts more than 3 days. Miso is salty: go easy if you have high blood pressure.

ingredients.nom: spring onions (the white part, with the roots)

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop (dan dou chi, unsalted). Otherwise, the salted fermented black beans sold in Asian grocery stores, well rinsed.

etapes.texte: Wash the spring onions ({cebette}) well, keeping the roots. Cut the white parts into 3 cm pieces (save the green for another dish). Rinse the fermented soybeans ({douchi}).
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil, add the fermented soybeans and let them simmer.
Add the white parts of the spring onions and simmer briefly to keep their aroma.
Off the heat, dissolve the miso ({miso}) in a ladle of broth, then stir it into the pot: miso should not boil.
Drink it very hot, then cover up (sweater, blanket or comforter) and rest until you sweat lightly. Change your clothes if they're damp and stay out of drafts.

notes: You can have it 2 to 3 times during the day while the chills last; stop as soon as you've sweated a little.

fiches.titre: Lily bulb and sour jujube seed soup
fiches.contexte: An evening soup that nourishes Yin, cools the Heart and calms the mind: for insomnia, restlessness, and menopausal hot flashes with night sweats.
fiches.precautions: Only use lily bulbs sold for cooking or by herbal shops, never bulbs of garden or florist lilies. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have soft stools. Pregnancy, breastfeeding or sleep medication (sleeping pills, anti-anxiety drugs): ask a practitioner for advice.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops. Fresh (vacuum-packed, in the chilled section): use 50 g, no soaking needed.
From a Chinese herbal shop or a specialist pharmacy.

etapes.texte: The day before, soak the lily bulbs ({baihe}) in a bowl of cold water.
Roughly crush the sour jujube seeds ({zaoren}) with a mortar and pestle, or in a bag with a rolling pin.
Put the seeds in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid on.
Strain the decoction through a fine sieve and discard the seeds.
Drain the lily bulbs, add them to the decoction and cook over medium heat until tender.
Drink the decoction warm and eat the bulbs, once a day, about 1 hour before bed.

notes: If you find it a little bitter, add a small piece of rock sugar at the end of cooking.

fiches.contexte: A home remedy for painful periods when the pain eases with warmth (a hot-water bottle on the belly): it warms the lower belly, disperses Cold and relieves pain.

principe.py: Wēn jīng sàn hán zhǐ tòng
principe.fr: Warm the channels, disperse Cold, relieve pain

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: not for heavy, early or bright red periods, nor if you tend to feel hot. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: ask a practitioner for advice. Don't exceed the dose and don't take it continuously. Very painful periods, periods that change, or pain that stops you from living normally need medical advice.

ingredients.note: From a Chinese herbal shop. Buy loose mugwort sold for tea, not moxa sticks.

etapes.texte: Roughly chop the mugwort ({aiye}), or put it in a cloth tea bag so no bits end up in the broth. Slice the ginger ({gingembre}).
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the mugwort and ginger, then gently lower in the eggs ({oeufs}) with a spoon. Cook at a gentle boil.
Take out the eggs, run them under cold water and peel them. Make a few small cuts in the whites so they soak up the flavor.
Put the peeled eggs back in the decoction and let them simmer.
Strain the decoction and sweeten it ({sucre}) if you like. Eat the eggs and drink the decoction very hot.

notes: Have it once a day, 5 days in a row, starting 2 to 3 days before your period is due.
During that time, keep a hot-water bottle on your lower belly and avoid iced drinks.

fiches.titre: Egg in whole cane sugar syrup
fiches.contexte: A warm treat that nourishes Blood, helps it circulate and eases belly cramps: for the 2 or 3 days after your period, for painful periods, or after giving birth.

principe.fr: Nourish Blood and help it circulate

fiches.precautions: Sweet: avoid if you have diabetes. Not during very heavy periods. After giving birth, if you have a fever, bleeding that increases or severe pain: call your midwife or doctor right away.

ingredients.note: Rapadura or muscovado both work.

etapes.texte: Dissolve the sugar ({sucre}) in the water ({eau}), bring to a boil and let it bubble gently.
Beat the egg ({oeuf}) with a fork in a bowl.
Pour the egg in a thin stream into the simmering syrup, stirring gently: it forms ribbons. Let it cook.
Drink it hot, in small sips. Once a day.

notes: The sugar is reduced compared with the traditional recipe (50 g): add a little more if you like it sweeter.
If your belly feels cold, add 2 slices of fresh ginger to the syrup.
You can also poach the whole egg in the syrup (3 minutes) instead of beating it.

fiches.titre: Eggs with jujubes and goji berries
fiches.contexte: A gentle broth that nourishes the Liver and Kidney and calms the mind: for restless nights and nervousness, when the lower back and knees feel weak.

principe.fr: Tonify the Liver and Kidney, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Jujubes are sweet and rich: go easy if you have a bloated belly, mucus or diarrhea. If you take an anticoagulant, ask your doctor (goji can interact with it).

etapes.texte: Rinse the jujubes ({dattes}) and put them in a small pot with the eggs ({oeufs}) and the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then cook at a gentle boil.
Take out the eggs, run them under cold water and peel them.
Put the eggs back in the broth with the rinsed goji berries ({goji}) and let them simmer.
Eat the eggs and jujubes, and drink the broth. Once a day, ideally in the evening.

fiches.contexte: A small evening treat that nourishes Blood and Yin and calms the mind: for insomnia and nights full of dreams.
fiches.precautions: Longan is sweet and warming: go easy if you have a lot of heat (dry mouth, mouth ulcers, constipation), mucus or a bloated belly. Diabetes: in moderation and with no added sugar.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, in bags: a brown, sticky flesh, already pitted.

etapes.texte: Rinse the longan flesh ({longane}) and soak it in a little hot water.
Crack the egg ({oeuf}) into a ramekin without breaking the yolk. Sprinkle the white with sugar ({sucre}).
Steam the ramekin with the lid on until the white starts to set while the yolk is still runny.
Drain the longan and gently press it into the yolk.
Keep steaming until the egg is fully set.
Enjoy it warm, in the evening. Once a day.

notes: No steamer: set the ramekin in a pot with 2 cm of simmering water and cover.
The sugar is kept to a minimum: longan is already very sweet.

fiches.contexte: A light sweet soup that tonifies the Kidney, nourishes Essence and supports the Heart and memory. It's also recommended for high cholesterol: in that case it goes alongside your medical care, never instead of it.
fiches.precautions: Contains sugar: if you have diabetes, make it without the rock sugar. For pregnant women and young children, cook it longer until the egg yolks are fully set.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, as pale golden balls in bags.

etapes.texte: Rinse the tremella ({tremelle}) and soak it in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base, then cut the tremella into small pieces.

Put the tremella in a large heatproof bowl with the cold water ({eau}) and the rock sugar ({sucre}). Steam with the lid on until it's tender and the liquid turns slightly syrupy. Keep an eye on the water level in the steamer.
Crack the quail eggs ({oeufs}) one at a time straight into the hot soup and keep steaming.
Divide among 4 bowls, with 3 eggs each. Enjoy warm.
Rinse the tremella ({tremelle}) and soak it in a large bowl of warm water.
Cut off the hard, yellowish base, then cut the tremella into small pieces.
Put the tremella in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer over low heat with the lid on, stirring now and then.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}) and let it melt, stirring.
Crack the quail eggs ({oeufs}) one at a time into the simmering soup, without stirring.
Divide among 4 bowls, with 3 eggs each. Enjoy warm.

notes: The traditional recipe uses 100 g of rock sugar: 30 g is enough for a lightly sweet soup.
To crack a quail egg, nick the shell with the tip of a knife, then open it over a cup.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently.

fiches.contexte: Purslane clears Heat, eliminates Toxins and drains Dampness: a traditional omelet for sudden, burning, foul-smelling diarrhea.

principe.py: Qīng rè jiě dú zhǐ lì
principe.fr: Clear Heat, eliminate Toxins, stop diarrhea

fiches.precautions: Purslane is cold: not for lingering diarrhea with a cold belly, nor during pregnancy. Drink plenty to replace lost fluids. See a doctor quickly if there's a high fever, blood in the stools, diarrhea lasting more than 2 days, or if a baby or an elderly person is getting dehydrated.

ingredients.note: At markets in summer, or in the garden where it grows on its own. Pick it away from roads and wash it well.

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Wash the purslane ({pourpier}) in plenty of water, drain it well and chop it finely.
Beat the eggs ({oeufs}) with the salt ({sel}), then stir in the purslane.
Heat the oil ({huile}) over medium heat in a frying pan, pour in the mixture and let it set without stirring.
Fold the omelet in half and cook a little longer, until it's set all the way through.
Serve hot, with a bowl of rice or congee.

notes: Outside of bouts of diarrhea, it's also a nice summer omelet, light and refreshing.

fiches.titre: Winter melon soup with dried shrimp
fiches.contexte: A summer soup that cools and drains Dampness: for heavy, hot days, slightly swollen legs, scanty dark urine, and that weighed-down kind of tiredness.
fiches.precautions: Shellfish allergy: replace the shrimp with 4 dried shiitake mushrooms. Rather cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly, soft stools, or if you already urinate a lot. Dried shrimp are salty: use little salt.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, often sold in slices. Peel it thinly or keep the skin, well scrubbed: it boosts the draining effect. Otherwise, use zucchini (10 min of cooking).
In Asian grocery stores, in bags.

etapes.texte: Rinse the dried shrimp ({crevettes}) and soak them in a bowl of warm water. Keep the soaking water.
Remove the seeds and spongy center of the winter melon ({courge}), then cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Put the shrimp, their soaking water, the water ({eau}) and the ginger ({gingembre}) in a pot. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Add the winter melon and simmer with the lid on until it turns translucent and meltingly soft.
Taste before adding salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and add a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}).

notes: For a stronger draining effect, add a handful of Job's tears (yi yi ren), soaked the day before, when you start the broth, and cook 20 minutes longer.

fiches.titre: Chinese cabbage soup with tofu and shiitake
fiches.contexte: A light everyday soup that is kind to the Stomach, replenishes fluids and keeps things moving: ideal after overly rich meals, or when your mouth is dry and your stools a little hard.

principe.fr: Nourish the Stomach, moisten the intestines

fiches.precautions: Rather cooling: if you have a cold belly or soft stools, double the ginger.

ingredients.note: Or 150 g of fresh shiitake, sliced, no soaking needed.

etapes.texte: Soak the shiitake ({shiitake}) in a bowl of hot water.

Drain the shiitake, keeping the water, remove the tough stems and slice the caps. Separate the white ribs of the cabbage ({chou}) from the green leaves and cut everything into strips. Cut the tofu ({tofu}) into cubes.
Put the water ({eau}), the strained soaking water, the shiitake and the ginger ({gingembre}) in a pot. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Add the white cabbage ribs and let them simmer.
Add the tofu and the green leaves, and simmer gently.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}), the spring onion ({cebette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}). Serve hot.

notes: Add a handful of glass noodles or a little rice to the bowl to make it a full meal.

fiches.titre: Scrambled eggs with shrimp and Chinese chives
fiches.contexte: Chinese chives are nicknamed “the herb that lifts Yang”; together with shrimp, they warm the Kidney. A quick dish for a cold lower back, fatigue with a sense of cold, and low libido.

ingredients.nom: Chinese chives (jiu cai), cut into 3 cm (1 in) lengths

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Beat the eggs ({oeufs}) with half the salt ({sel}).
Heat half the oil ({huile}) until very hot, pour in the eggs and stir gently until they set but are still soft. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the ginger ({gingembre}), then the shrimp ({crevettes}). Stir-fry them until they turn pink.
Add the Chinese chives ({ciboule}) and the rest of the salt, and stir-fry over high heat just until they wilt.
Return the eggs to the pan, give it one last stir and serve right away with rice.

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: avoid it if you have signs of Heat (red tongue, thirst, pimples, fever) or a seafood allergy.
notes: You'll find Chinese chives in bunches in Asian grocery stores: flat leaves, with a taste somewhere between garlic and chives. If you can't find them, use very thinly sliced leek or regular chives.

fiches.titre: Fox nut, lotus seed and Chinese yam congee
fiches.contexte: Fox nuts and lotus seeds “tighten”: they help the Kidney hold in what is leaking out (seminal emissions, urine leaks, soft stools). Chinese yam supports the Spleen and Kidney. A mild, nourishing bowl that also calms the mind.

ingredients.nom: dried fox nuts (euryale seeds, qian shi)
fresh Chinese yam (shan yao), diced (or 30 g dried)

etapes.texte: Soak the fox nuts ({qianshi}) and lotus seeds ({lotus}) in cold water, then drain.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the fox nuts and lotus seeds, then let it simmer, covered.
Add the rinsed rice ({riz}), yam ({shanyao}) and jujubes ({dattes}). Let it simmer with the lid slightly ajar, stirring from time to time, until it turns thick and creamy.
Serve hot. Thin it with a little hot water if the congee has gotten too thick.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Soak the fox nuts ({qianshi}) and lotus seeds ({lotus}) in cold water, then drain.

etapes.titre: Put everything in the inner pot
etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}), fox nuts, lotus seeds, yam ({shanyao}), jujubes ({dattes}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot.
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Stir and serve hot.

fiches.precautions: A dish that “tightens”: avoid it if you have dry constipation or a swollen, painful belly.
notes: Fox nuts (small white and red balls) and lotus seeds are sold dried in Asian grocery stores.
You can make a big batch: it keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

fiches.titre: Braised chicken with chestnuts and shiitake mushrooms
fiches.contexte: Chestnut is nicknamed the “Kidney fruit”: it strengthens the lower back and knees. With chicken and ginger, it makes a fall dish that warms the Spleen and Kidney.

principe.fr: Tonify the Kidney, strengthen the Spleen

ingredients.nom: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked for 30 min
water (including the strained shiitake soaking water)

variantes.nom: In a cast-iron casserole pot or saucepan

etapes.texte: Brown the chicken ({poulet}) in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}) and the white parts of the spring onions ({cebette}).
Add the shiitakes ({shiitake}) cut in half, the soy sauce ({soja}) and the water ({eau}). Cover and let it simmer gently.
Add the chestnuts ({chataignes}) and keep cooking uncovered to reduce the sauce.
Sprinkle with the green parts of the spring onions and serve with rice.
On the Sauté setting, if your cooker has one, brown the chicken ({poulet}) in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}) and the white parts of the spring onions ({cebette}).
Add the shiitakes ({shiitake}), chestnuts ({chataignes}), soy sauce ({soja}) and water ({eau}). Simmer or Stew program.
Sprinkle with the green parts of the spring onions and serve with rice.
Brown the chicken ({poulet}) in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}) and the white parts of the spring onions ({cebette}).
Add the shiitakes ({shiitake}), soy sauce ({soja}) and water ({eau}). Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop, add the chestnuts ({chataignes}) and let the sauce reduce uncovered.
Sprinkle with the green parts of the spring onions and serve with rice.

notes: With fresh chestnuts: cut a slit in each one, boil them for 15 minutes and peel them while they're still hot.

fiches.titre: Braised lamb with fennel and fennel seeds
fiches.contexte: Fennel seeds warm the Liver meridian and the lower belly; lamb and ginger warm the Kidney and Spleen. For cold-type pain in the lower belly, periods that come with a feeling of cold, and icy hands and feet.

ingredients.nom: lamb shoulder or neck, cut into pieces

etapes.texte: Brown the lamb ({agneau}) in the oil ({huile}) on all sides.
Add the ginger ({gingembre}), garlic ({ail}) and fennel seeds ({graines}), and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the water ({eau}), add salt ({sel}), cover and let it simmer very gently.
Add the fennel ({fenouil}) and carrots ({carotte}), and keep cooking until everything is meltingly tender.
Serve hot, with rice or millet.
On the Sauté setting, if your cooker has one, brown the lamb ({agneau}) in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}), garlic ({ail}) and fennel seeds ({graines}).
Add the fennel ({fenouil}), carrots ({carotte}), water ({eau}) and salt ({sel}). Simmer or Stew program.
Serve hot, with rice or millet.
Brown the lamb ({agneau}) in the oil ({huile}) with the ginger ({gingembre}), garlic ({ail}) and fennel seeds ({graines}).
Add the fennel ({fenouil}), carrots ({carotte}), water ({eau}) and salt ({sel}). Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own and serve.

fiches.precautions: A very warming dish: not if you have a fever, a red tongue, intense thirst or hot flashes.
notes: Mutton works too; cook it half an hour longer.

fiches.titre: Duck soup with Chinese yam and goji berries
fiches.contexte: Duck nourishes Yin without weighing you down; Chinese yam supports the Spleen, Lung and Kidney, and goji nourishes the Liver and Kidney. For a dry mouth, night sweats, and feeling hot late in the day.

ingredients.nom: fresh Chinese yam (shan yao), cut into chunks (or 40 g dried)

etapes.texte: Drop the duck ({canard}) into boiling water, then drain and rinse: the broth will be clearer and less fatty.
Put the duck back in the cold water ({eau}) with the ginger ({gingembre}) and the white parts of the spring onions ({cebette}). Bring to a simmer and cook covered, skimming off the foam at the start.
Add the yam ({shanyao}) and keep cooking.
Add the goji berries ({goji}) and salt ({sel}).
Skim off the fat if needed and serve with the green parts of the spring onions.
Drop the duck ({canard}) into boiling water, then drain and rinse.
Put the duck, yam ({shanyao}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion whites ({cebette}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot. Soup program.
Add the goji ({goji}) and salt ({sel}), and leave it on Keep Warm.
Skim off the fat if needed and serve.
Drop the duck ({canard}) into boiling water, then drain and rinse.
Put in the duck, yam ({shanyao}), ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion whites ({cebette}) and water ({eau}). Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop, add the goji ({goji}) and salt ({sel}) and let it simmer.
Skim off the fat if needed and serve.

fiches.precautions: Duck is cooling: if you often feel cold or have soft stools, double the ginger.
notes: Once the broth has cooled, it's easy to skim: the fat sets on the surface.

fiches.titre: Pan-fried chicken livers with spinach and goji
fiches.contexte: In Chinese dietary therapy, liver nourishes the Liver: chicken livers, spinach and goji nourish the Blood. For tired eyes, floaters, cramps and brittle nails.

principe.fr: Nourish the Liver, tonify the Blood

etapes.texte: Heat half the oil ({huile}) until very hot and sear the livers ({foies}) with the ginger ({gingembre}): they should stay pink in the middle. Set aside.
In the rest of the oil, fry the garlic ({ail}), then the spinach ({epinards}) until it wilts.
Return the livers to the pan, add the goji ({goji}) and soy sauce ({soja}), and stir over the heat.
Serve right away, with rice.

fiches.precautions: Rich in vitamin A: if you're pregnant, limit organ meats to a small portion now and then, and ask your midwife or doctor for advice.
notes: Overcooked livers turn dry and bitter: take them off the heat as soon as they're browned.

fiches.contexte: Cucumber, tofu and seaweed are cooling and drain Dampness through the urine. A light broth for dark urine, intimate itching, a bitter taste in the mouth, and hot weather.

etapes.texte: Soak the wakame ({wakame}) in cold water, then drain.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a simmer with the ginger ({gingembre}) and soy sauce ({soja}).
Add the tofu ({tofu}), cucumber ({concombre}) and wakame, and let it simmer.
Sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and serve warm.

fiches.precautions: A cooling dish: if you often feel cold or have soft stools, save it for hot weather and add ginger.
notes: You'll find dried wakame in Asian grocery stores or the organic aisle; it swells a lot.

fiches.titre: Stir-fried wood ear mushrooms with celery, garlic and ginger
fiches.contexte: Wood ear mushrooms (mu er) gently get the Blood moving; celery calms Liver Yang. A side dish for fixed pain, periods with clots, high blood pressure and throbbing temples.

principe.fr: Get the Blood moving, clear the vessels

ingredients.nom: celery stalks, sliced on the diagonal

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Soak the wood ear mushrooms ({muer}) in lukewarm water, then rinse them and cut off the hard parts.
Fry the garlic ({ail}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the hot oil ({huile}).
Add the carrot ({carotte}), celery ({celeri}) and mushrooms, and stir-fry over high heat.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}), stir and serve right away.

fiches.precautions: Wood ear mushrooms thin the blood: if you take a blood thinner, are pregnant, or have surgery coming up, ask for advice.
notes: You'll find them dried in Asian grocery stores; 15 g dried makes a big bowlful once they've swollen.

fiches.contexte: A classic kitchen remedy at the very start of a chill-type cold: chills, clear runny nose, stiff neck. Spring onion whites and ginger make you sweat a little, and the rice protects the Stomach.

ingredients.nom: spring onion whites, with their roots, washed

etapes.texte: Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the rinsed rice ({riz}), then let it simmer with the lid slightly ajar.
Add the ginger ({gingembre}) and the spring onion whites ({cebette}), crushed with the flat of a knife. Let it simmer a little longer.
Add salt ({sel}) and have it piping hot, then bundle up so you sweat a little.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot and start the Porridge or Congee program.
Add the ginger ({gingembre}) and the crushed spring onion whites ({cebette}), close the lid and leave on Keep Warm.
Add salt ({sel}) and have it piping hot, then bundle up.

fiches.precautions: Only at the very start of a chill-type cold. If there's a sore throat, a high fever or yellow phlegm, it's no longer the right time.
notes: The aromatics only cook for a few minutes: that's what keeps them effective.

fiches.titre: Beef bone broth with carrots and ginger
fiches.contexte: A long-simmered broth that supports the Kidney, bones and tendons. For tired knees and lower back, recovery after illness, and long winters.

principe.fr: Tonify the Kidney, strengthen the bones

etapes.texte: Cover the bones ({os}) with cold water, bring to a boil, then drain and rinse: the broth will be clearer.
Put the bones back in the cold water ({eau}) with the vinegar ({vinaigre}), ginger ({gingembre}), onion ({oignon}) and star anise ({anis}). Let it barely simmer, covered.
Add the carrots ({carotte}) and jujubes ({dattes}) and keep cooking.
Strain, add salt ({sel}) and serve a hot bowlful. Save the marrow and the shank meat for another meal.
Cover the bones ({os}) with cold water, bring to a boil, then drain and rinse.

Put in the bones, the water ({eau}) up to the inner pot's limit, the vinegar ({vinaigre}), ginger ({gingembre}), onion ({oignon}), star anise ({anis}), carrots ({carotte}) and jujubes ({dattes}). Slow Cook or Long Soup program.
Strain, add salt ({sel}) and serve.
Cover the bones ({os}) with cold water, bring to a boil, then drain and rinse.

Put the bones back in with the water ({eau}) up to the max line, the vinegar ({vinaigre}), ginger ({gingembre}), onion ({oignon}) and star anise ({anis}). Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop, add the carrots ({carotte}) and jujubes ({dattes}) and let it simmer uncovered.
Strain, add salt ({sel}) and serve.

notes: It keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes very well in portions.
Once cooled, it sets into a jelly: that's a good sign.

fiches.titre: Warm oysters with ginger and spring onion
fiches.contexte: Oyster nourishes Yin and Essence and calms the mind; its shell is a classic remedy for holding in Essence and calming. Barely cooked, with ginger to balance their cooling nature.

ingredients.nom: fresh ginger, cut into fine julienne

etapes.texte: Set the oysters ({huitres}) cupped side down in a steamer basket over boiling water and cover: they'll open slightly.
Remove the flat top shell of each oyster with a knife, keeping the juice.
Top each one with a little ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), a drop of soy sauce ({soja}) and sesame oil ({huile}). Serve warm.
Preheat the oven on the broil setting to 220 °C (425 °F).
Set the oysters ({huitres}) cupped side down on a baking sheet, propped up with crumpled foil, and put them in the oven: they'll open slightly.
Open them, then top each one with a little ginger ({gingembre}), spring onion ({cebette}), a drop of soy sauce ({soja}) and sesame oil ({huile}).

fiches.precautions: Throw away any that stay closed after cooking. Not if you have a seafood allergy.
notes: Out of season, frozen shucked oysters can be pan-fried for 1 minute with the ginger.

fiches.contexte: A great classic for the Kidney and Essence: graying or thinning hair, failing memory, dry constipation, tired lower back. Drink it warm at breakfast or as an afternoon snack.

variantes.nom: In a saucepan, with a blender

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the sesame ({sesame}), walnuts ({noix}) and rice ({riz}) in a frying pan, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Blend everything until smooth with the jujubes ({dattes}) and half the water ({eau}).
Pour into a saucepan with the rest of the water and let it thicken over low heat, stirring.
Serve warm and plain: the jujubes are enough to sweeten it.
Dry-toast the sesame ({sesame}), walnuts ({noix}) and rice ({riz}) in a frying pan until fragrant.
Put everything in the blender with the jujubes ({dattes}) and water ({eau}), and start the Smooth Soup or Plant Milk program.
Serve warm.

fiches.precautions: Rich and fatty: if you have soft stools or diarrhea, wait until it passes.
notes: Extra toasted sesame keeps for 2 weeks in a closed jar.

fiches.titre: Braised beef with carrots, jujubes and ginger
fiches.contexte: Beef tonifies Qi and Blood and strengthens the Spleen, tendons and bones; the jujubes and carrot round it out. A deeply nourishing dish for fatigue and recovery after illness.

ingredients.nom: stewing beef (chuck, cheek or shoulder), cubed

variantes.nom: In a cast-iron casserole pot or saucepan

etapes.texte: Brown the beef ({boeuf}) in the oil ({huile}) on all sides.
Add the onion ({oignon}) and ginger ({gingembre}), and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the water ({eau}) and soy sauce ({soja}), then add the star anise ({anis}) and jujubes ({dattes}). Cover and let it simmer very gently.
Add the carrots ({carotte}) and keep cooking until the meat is meltingly tender.
Remove the star anise, taste and serve with rice.
On the Sauté setting, if your cooker has one, brown the beef ({boeuf}) in the oil ({huile}), then the onion ({oignon}) and ginger ({gingembre}).
Add the water ({eau}), soy sauce ({soja}), star anise ({anis}), jujubes ({dattes}) and carrots ({carotte}). Simmer or Stew program.
Remove the star anise and serve with rice.
Brown the beef ({boeuf}) in the oil ({huile}) right in the pressure cooker, then the onion ({oignon}) and ginger ({gingembre}).
Add the water ({eau}), soy sauce ({soja}), star anise ({anis}), jujubes ({dattes}) and carrots ({carotte}). Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own, remove the star anise and serve.

notes: A gelatinous cut (cheek, chuck) makes a more nourishing sauce.

fiches.titre: Stir-fried beef with broccoli and ginger
fiches.contexte: Quick and nourishing: beef tonifies Qi and Blood, and well-cooked broccoli stays easy to digest.

ingredients.nom: quick-cooking beef (sirloin, flank steak), cut into thin strips
slices of ginger, cut into matchsticks
cornstarch, mixed with 3 spoonfuls of water

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Drop the broccoli ({brocoli}) into boiling water, then drain it.
Heat the oil ({huile}) over very high heat and sear the beef ({boeuf}) just until it changes color. Set it aside.
Fry the garlic ({ail}) and ginger ({gingembre}) for a few seconds, then add the broccoli and stir-fry.
Return the beef to the pan, add the soy sauce ({soja}) and the cornstarch mixture ({fecule}), and stir until the sauce coats everything. Serve with rice.

notes: Slice the beef while it's half-frozen: you'll get thinner strips.

fiches.contexte: A winter classic in China: mutton warms Spleen and Kidney Yang, and daikon lightens the dish and helps you digest the meat.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have signs of heat: red tongue, thirst, night sweats, red pimples.

ingredients.nom: mutton or lamb (shoulder, neck), cut into pieces
daikon (white radish), cut into large chunks
stalks of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Drop the mutton ({mouton}) into boiling water, then rinse it: the broth will be clearer and less gamy.
Put the meat, ginger ({gingembre}) and water ({eau}) in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam and let it simmer, covered.
Add the daikon ({radis}) and carrot ({carotte}). Keep cooking until the daikon turns translucent.
Season with salt and pepper ({sel}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).
Drop the mutton ({mouton}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put the meat, ginger ({gingembre}), daikon ({radis}), carrot ({carotte}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot. Soup or Simmer program.
Season with salt and pepper ({sel}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).
Drop the mutton ({mouton}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put the meat, ginger ({gingembre}) and water ({eau}) in the pressure cooker. Start timing once it starts to hiss.
Open it once the pressure has dropped, add the daikon ({radis}) and carrot ({carotte}), and let it simmer with the lid off.
Season with salt and pepper ({sel}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).

notes: Serve the broth piping hot first, then the meat and daikon.

fiches.contexte: The recovery congee: chicken tonifies Qi and gently warms the center, and ginger aids digestion.

ingredients.nom: boneless chicken breast or thigh, cut into thin strips
slices of ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
stalks of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}) and bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}) with half the ginger ({gingembre}). Let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring.
Add the chicken ({poulet}) and the rest of the ginger, stir and let it cook gently.
Add salt ({sel}), then sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and a few drops of sesame oil ({sesame}).

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and half the ginger ({gingembre}) in the inner pot, with water up to the Porridge line. Porridge or Congee program.
Add the chicken ({poulet}) and the rest of the ginger, stir, and leave on Keep Warm or run a short cycle, until the chicken is cooked through.
Add salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and add a drizzle of sesame oil ({sesame}).

notes: Make sure the chicken is cooked through, with no pink in the middle.

fiches.titre: Stir-fried chicken with shiitake mushrooms and ginger
fiches.contexte: Shiitake strengthens Spleen Qi and your defenses, and chicken tonifies Qi: an everyday dish for fatigue and slow digestion.

ingredients.nom: chicken breast or thigh, cut into strips
fresh shiitake mushrooms, sliced (or 8 dried, soaked for 30 min)
slices of ginger, cut into matchsticks

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Brown the chicken ({poulet}) in the oil ({huile}) until cooked through.
Add the garlic ({ail}), ginger ({gingembre}) and shiitakes ({shiitake}), and stir-fry until tender.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}) and spring onion ({cebette}), stir and serve with rice.

notes: Save the soaking water from dried shiitakes for a soup.

fiches.titre: Oyster soup with tofu and ginger
fiches.contexte: Oyster meat nourishes Yin and Blood and calms the mind; tofu is gently cooling. For restless sleep, night sweats, and fatigue with dryness.
fiches.precautions: Cook the oysters thoroughly. Avoid them if you have a seafood allergy, and don't eat them raw during pregnancy.

ingredients.nom: oysters, shucked, with their liquid strained
slices of ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
stalk of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Bring the water ({eau}) to a simmer with the ginger ({gingembre}).
Gently add the tofu ({tofu}).
Add the oysters ({huitres}) and their strained liquid. Take the pan off the heat as soon as their edges curl.
Add pepper ({poivre}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}). Taste before adding salt: the oyster liquid is already salty.

notes: Frozen shucked oysters from Asian grocery stores work too.

fiches.titre: Braised octopus with potatoes and garlic
fiches.contexte: Octopus nourishes Qi and Blood; cooked for a long time, it turns tender and easy to digest. Potatoes support the Spleen.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have a seafood allergy.

ingredients.nom: cleaned octopus (it's more tender if frozen, then thawed)

etapes.texte: Drop the octopus ({poulpe}) into a large pot of boiling water with the bay leaf ({laurier}) and ginger ({gingembre}). Let it simmer, covered, until the tip of a knife goes in easily.
Drain the octopus and cut it into pieces.
Gently fry the onion ({oignon}) and garlic ({ail}) in the oil ({huile}).
Add the potatoes ({pdt}), octopus and water ({eau}). Let it simmer, covered, until the potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper ({sel}).
Put the octopus ({poulpe}), bay leaf ({laurier}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the pressure cooker and add water to come halfway up. Start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop, drain the octopus and cut it into pieces.
In the emptied pressure cooker, gently fry the onion ({oignon}) and garlic ({ail}) in the oil ({huile}).
Add the potatoes ({pdt}), octopus and water ({eau}), and close the lid again.
Season with salt and pepper ({sel}).

fiches.titre: Stir-fried squid with celery and ginger
fiches.contexte: Squid nourishes Yin and Blood, and celery cools the Liver: a light dish when heat rises to your head and your eyes are dry.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have a seafood allergy.

ingredients.nom: celery stalks, sliced on the diagonal
slices of ginger, cut into matchsticks

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: In a very hot pan, sear the squid ({calamar}) in the oil ({huile}) just until it turns white, then set it aside. Overcooked squid gets tough.
Fry the garlic ({ail}) and ginger ({gingembre}), then the celery ({celeri}): it should stay crunchy.
Return the squid to the pan for 30 seconds with the soy sauce ({soja}) and spring onion ({cebette}). Serve with rice.

fiches.titre: Steamed white fish with ginger and spring onion
fiches.contexte: Steaming keeps fish light and easy to digest; ginger and spring onion warm the Stomach. Ideal for a delicate digestion or nausea.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, harmonize the Stomach

ingredients.nom: white fish fillets (cod, sea bass, sea bream…)
slices of ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
stalks of spring onion, cut into thin strips

etapes.texte: Lay the fillets ({poisson}) on a deep plate and scatter half the ginger ({gingembre}) over them.
Set the plate over a pot of simmering water, with the lid on, until the flesh turns opaque.
Pour over the soy sauce ({soja}), then add the rest of the ginger and the spring onion ({cebette}). Drizzle with sizzling-hot oil ({huile}) to bring out the aromas.
Lay the fillets ({poisson}) on a plate that fits in the basket, with half the ginger ({gingembre}).
Put water in the inner pot as the manual says, then use the Steam program. You can cook rice underneath at the same time.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}), the rest of the ginger and the spring onion ({cebette}), then the sizzling-hot oil ({huile}).

notes: A whole fish (sea bass, sea bream) is made the same way: allow a few more minutes.

fiches.contexte: A classic recipe for swelling: fish supports the Spleen, and adzuki beans drain water through the urine. In China, it's made with carp.
fiches.precautions: Swelling (edema) should also be checked by a doctor.

ingredients.nom: carp steaks or firm white fish
ingredients.note: You'll find carp in Asian grocery stores or at the fish counter.

ingredients.nom: dried tangerine peel (or the zest of an organic tangerine)

etapes.texte: Drain the adzuki beans ({azuki}), put them in the water ({eau}) with the peel ({mandarine}), bring to a boil and let it simmer.
Add the fish ({poisson}) and ginger ({gingembre}), and let it simmer gently without stirring.
Add very little salt ({sel}): salt makes the body hold on to water. Drink the broth and eat the beans.
Put the drained adzuki beans ({azuki}), peel ({mandarine}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot. Soup or Simmer program.
Add the fish ({poisson}) and ginger ({gingembre}), and run a short cycle.
Add very little salt ({sel}).

notes: Watch out for carp bones: serve it in large pieces that are easy to pick through.

fiches.titre: Baked salmon with sweet potato and ginger
fiches.contexte: Salmon tonifies Qi and nourishes the Blood, and sweet potato strengthens the Spleen. A simple, complete meal, baked or steamed.

ingredients.nom: stalk of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the sweet potato ({patate}) with the oil ({huile}) and salt ({sel}), spread it on a baking sheet and put it in the oven.
Mix the ginger ({gingembre}) and soy sauce ({soja}), and brush it over the fillets ({saumon}).
Place the salmon on the baking sheet next to the sweet potato and bake until just cooked.
Sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).
Steam the sweet potato ({patate}) until tender.
Brush the fillets ({saumon}) with the ginger ({gingembre}) and soy sauce ({soja}), and add them to the steamer basket.
Drizzle with a little oil ({huile}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).

fiches.titre: Mussels with ginger and spring onion
fiches.contexte: Mussels, slightly warming by nature, nourish the Liver and Kidney, Essence and Blood: for a weak lower back, dizziness and deep-seated fatigue.

principe.py: Bǔ gān shèn yì jīng xuè
principe.fr: Tonify the Liver and Kidney, nourish Essence and Blood

fiches.precautions: Avoid them if you have a seafood allergy. Throw away any mussels that are open before cooking and any that stay closed after.

ingredients.nom: fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
stalks of spring onion, cut into lengths

etapes.texte: In a large pot, gently fry the garlic ({ail}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the oil ({huile}).
Add the mussels ({moules}) and water ({eau}), cover and shake the pot from time to time until they open.
Add the spring onion ({cebette}) and pepper ({poivre}), stir and serve with the juice.

notes: Serve with rice to make the most of the juice.

fiches.contexte: Millet and astragalus (huang qi) strengthen the Spleen and Qi, and help the body clear Dampness. For fatigue, one cold after another, convalescence, the weeks after giving birth, long-lasting soft stools, white vaginal discharge or swollen ankles.

principe.py: Jiàn pí yì qì lì shī
principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, tonify Qi, drain Dampness

fiches.precautions: Astragalus is a Chinese medicinal herb: take it as a 5 to 7 day course, no longer without advice. Avoid it during a cold or an infection with fever, and if you have signs of Heat (thirst, feeling hot, red tongue). Pregnancy, breastfeeding, autoimmune disease or immunosuppressant treatment: ask your doctor or practitioner first.

ingredients.note: In Chinese herbal shops, Asian grocery stores or specialist pharmacies: long, pale yellow slices with a slightly sweet taste.

etapes.texte: Wrap the astragalus ({astragale}) in a square of cheesecloth or a cloth spice bag and tie it tightly.
Put the pouch in a pot with the cold water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer, covered: the astragalus starts releasing its benefits.
Rinse the millet ({millet}) until the water runs clear and add it to the pot. Cook over low heat with the lid ajar, stirring now and then, until the millet bursts and the porridge thickens.
Take out the astragalus pouch, pressing it against the side of the pot with a spoon, then throw it away. Add a little salt ({sel}).
Eat the porridge hot: one bowl in the morning, one bowl in the evening.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Wrap the astragalus ({astragale}) in a square of cheesecloth or a cloth spice bag and tie it tightly.
Put the pouch, rinsed millet ({millet}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot. Let it soak before you start cooking: the astragalus begins to steep.
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Take out the pouch, pressing it, add salt ({sel}) and eat hot, morning and evening.

notes: No cheesecloth? First simmer the astragalus on its own in the water for 20 minutes, strain, then cook the millet in this broth.
You can add 3 jujubes with the millet for a sweeter, more nourishing porridge.

fiches.contexte: Alisma (ze xie) helps the body get rid of excess water and cools the lower belly, while the rice is gentle on the Stomach. It supports medical care for cystitis (burning, urgent need to urinate) and helps with ankles swollen from water retention.
fiches.precautions: A cooling, draining Chinese medicinal herb: 3 to 5 days in a row at most, never as a long course. Not if fatigue comes with abundant, clear urine, or if you often feel cold. Not during pregnancy or breastfeeding, nor with kidney disease or diuretic treatment without medical advice. Cystitis: this congee doesn't replace seeing a doctor; with fever, lower back pain or blood in the urine, see a doctor right away.

ingredients.note: Sold as dried slices in Chinese herbal shops or pharmacies specializing in Chinese herbs: grind them to a fine powder in a coffee or spice grinder. Some herbal shops sell it already ground.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}) and put it in a pot with the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, then let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then, until the grains burst and little craters form on the surface.
Stir the alisma powder ({alisma}) into two spoonfuls of the cooking water to avoid lumps.
Stir it into the congee and cook a little longer over very low heat.
Eat it warm, in two servings: one bowl in the morning, one in the evening.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot.
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Mix the alisma powder ({alisma}) with a little congee, stir it into the rest and leave on Keep Warm with the lid closed.
Eat it warm: one bowl in the morning, one in the evening.

notes: No grinder? Simmer the alisma slices in the water for 30 minutes, strain, then cook the rice in this decoction.
During a bout of cystitis, also drink plenty of water throughout the day.

fiches.contexte: Chinese chives warm the Kidney and support Yang, the body's deep inner fire. For fatigue with feeling cold, thin white discharge, or frequent urination linked to age or the prostate, alongside medical care.

principe.py: Bǔ shèn zhuàng yáng gù jīng
principe.fr: Tonify the Kidney, strengthen Yang, consolidate Essence

fiches.precautions: A warming dish: avoid it if you have signs of Heat (thirst, feeling hot, red tongue, mouth ulcers, spots), night sweats or a sore throat. Urinary problems in men should be checked by a doctor: this congee supports medical care, it doesn't replace it.

ingredients.nom: Chinese chives (jiu cai), washed and cut into 1 cm pieces
ingredients.note: Sold in bunches in Asian grocery stores: flat leaves, a taste between garlic and chives. If you can't find them, use very thinly sliced leek.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}), bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then.
Add the Chinese chives ({ciboule}) and cook just long enough for them to turn tender and bright green.
Add salt ({sel}) and eat hot, ideally for breakfast.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot, then start the Porridge or Congee program.
Add the Chinese chives ({ciboule}), stir, close the lid and leave on Keep Warm.
Add salt ({sel}) and eat hot, ideally for breakfast.

notes: Traditionally, it's eaten for breakfast for about two weeks.
Added at the end, the chives keep their color and aroma.

fiches.contexte: Boiled peanut shells make a mild decoction that supports the Spleen and moistens the Lung. In China, it's recommended for high cholesterol or high blood pressure, alongside medical care, never instead of treatment.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, moisten the Lung

fiches.precautions: Never if you're allergic to peanuts: the shells contain allergens too. Use only raw, organic (untreated) peanut shells that are clean and dry; throw away any stained or moldy shell. Blood pressure or cholesterol: don't change your treatment without your doctor. Diabetes: leave out the rock sugar.

ingredients.nom: shells of raw organic peanuts, untreated
ingredients.note: That's roughly what 250 g of raw peanuts in their shells give you. Keep the nuts for another dish.

etapes.texte: Shell the peanuts and keep the shells ({coques}). Rinse them well, scrubbing them with a brush under running water, then break them up roughly by hand.
Put the shells in a pot with the water ({eau}), bring to a boil, then let it simmer, covered.
Strain the decoction through a fine sieve and throw away the shells. You should have about 1 liter of liquid left; top up with hot water if needed.
Put the decoction back on the heat with the rinsed rice ({riz}). Let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}), let it melt and eat hot, in two servings over the day.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Shell the peanuts and keep the shells ({coques}). Rinse them well, scrubbing them with a brush under running water, then break them up roughly by hand.
Put the shells and water ({eau}) in the inner pot and start the Soup program.
Strain the decoction, throw away the shells, rinse the inner pot and pour the liquid back in.
Add the rinsed rice ({riz}) and start the Porridge or Congee program.
Add the rock sugar ({sucre}), stir and eat hot, in two servings over the day.

notes: The rock sugar is optional: go easy on it, especially if you have high cholesterol.
Non-organic peanut shells may have been treated with chemicals: that's why you only use organic ones.

fiches.contexte: Mint disperses Wind-Heat and clears the head and eyes. For the start of a “hot” cold: scratchy throat, headache, red, stinging eyes.
fiches.precautions: A cooling dish: not for a chill-type cold (shivers, clear runny nose), nor if you're already sweating a lot. Breastfeeding: mint in large amounts can reduce milk supply. Very painful eye, worsening vision or fever lasting more than 3 days: see a doctor.

ingredients.nom: fresh mint, leaves and tender stems (or 10 g dried mint)
ingredients.note: Peppermint is the closest to Chinese mint (bo he). Dried mint is sold in herbal shops or in the herbal tea aisle.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}), bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, bring the mint water ({eau-menthe}) to a boil in a small pot. Add the mint ({menthe}), cover and simmer for 3 minutes, no longer, or its aroma will escape.
Strain and press the leaves well to get all the liquid out.
Add the decoction to the cooked congee with the rock sugar ({sucre}) and cook a moment longer.
Eat it warm, in two servings: one bowl in the morning, one in the evening.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot and start the Porridge or Congee program.
Toward the end of cooking, simmer the mint ({menthe}) in its water ({eau-menthe}) for 3 minutes, covered, in a small pot.
Strain the decoction into the inner pot, add the rock sugar ({sucre}), stir and leave on Keep Warm.
Eat it warm: one bowl in the morning, one in the evening.

notes: The mint cooks only briefly: that's what keeps it effective.
The congee keeps for a day in the fridge; reheat it gently with a little water.

fiches.contexte: Pomelo or grapefruit peel gets Qi moving, soothes the Liver and wakes up the Stomach. For stomach pain and bloating after a heavy meal, or when stress ties your stomach in knots.

principe.py: Shū gān lǐ qì kāi wèi
principe.fr: Soothe the Liver, move Qi, stimulate the appetite

fiches.precautions: Grapefruit and pomelo, peel included, interact with many medicines (for cholesterol, blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, anti-rejection drugs…): if you're on any treatment, ask your pharmacist first. A dispersing dish: not as a long course if fatigue is your main problem. Severe or lasting stomach pain, black stools: see a doctor.

ingredients.nom: organic grapefruit peel (or a quarter of an organic pomelo's peel)
ingredients.note: Organic only: the peel of non-organic citrus fruit is treated.

etapes.texte: The day before, wash and scrub the fruit, then remove the peel ({ecorce}) in large pieces. Let it dry for 24 hours in the open air, on a plate.
Cut the peel into thin strips about 1 cm by 3 cm.
Put the strips in a pot with the water ({eau}) and bring to a boil. Then add the rinsed rice ({riz}).
Let it simmer over low heat with the lid ajar, stirring now and then, until you get a thick congee.
Remove the strips if you find them too bitter. Add salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and eat hot, morning and evening.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: The day before, wash and scrub the fruit, then remove the peel ({ecorce}) in large pieces. Let it dry for 24 hours in the open air, on a plate.
Cut the peel into thin strips and put them in the inner pot with the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}).
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Remove the strips if you find them too bitter. Add salt ({sel}), sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and eat hot, morning and evening.

notes: If you're worried about bitterness, blanch the strips in boiling water for 5 minutes first and throw that water away.
Dried for several days until brittle, the peels keep for months in a closed jar.

fiches.contexte: A mild congee that strengthens Qi while helping drive out the cold. For people who catch one cold after another because they're run down: tired or older people, new mothers after giving birth, children.
fiches.precautions: For young children, cut the grapes into quarters (choking hazard). Sweat lightly without wearing yourself out, and change if your clothes get damp. High fever, fever in a baby or difficulty breathing: see a doctor. Diabetes: reduce or leave out the sugar.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}), bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer with the lid ajar: the congee should stay fairly runny.
When the rice has almost melted, add the apple slices ({pomme}), grapes ({raisin}) and rock sugar ({sucre}). Keep cooking gently.
Eat it piping hot, then snuggle under the duvet: a light sweat helps drive out the cold.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot and start the Porridge or Congee program.
Add the apple ({pomme}), grapes ({raisin}) and rock sugar ({sucre}), stir and run the Soup or Porridge program again for a few minutes.
Eat it piping hot, then rest somewhere warm under the duvet.

notes: The sugar is deliberately reduced compared with the traditional recipe: adjust it to taste.
Out of season, raisins work very well instead of fresh grapes.

fiches.contexte: Poria (fu ling), a mushroom, strengthens the Spleen and helps the body get rid of excess water; the jujubes soften and nourish. For swollen legs or face, water retention, soft stools or difficult urination.
fiches.precautions: Poria is gentle, but it makes you pass water: avoid long courses if you already urinate a lot and your urine is clear, or if your mouth and skin are very dry. Legs that swell suddenly, or on one side only, need to be seen by a doctor.

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops, as a powder or white cubes. The cubes are very hard: grind them to a powder in a spice grinder.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}) and bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}).
Add the jujubes ({dattes}) and let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then.
Stir the poria powder ({fuling}) into half a glass of cold water until there are no lumps left.
Add it to the almost-cooked congee while stirring, then cook a little longer over low heat.
Remove the jujube pits and eat hot.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}), jujubes ({dattes}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot.
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Mix the poria powder ({fuling}) with a little cold water, stir it into the inner pot and leave on Keep Warm.
Remove the jujube pits and eat hot.

notes: Poria has almost no taste: it slips easily into a congee, a soup or pancake batter.
The congee keeps for 2 days in the fridge; reheat it with a little water.

fiches.contexte: Rose soothes the Liver and harmonizes the Stomach: it helps Qi flow when emotions block everything. For irritability, premenstrual syndrome and irregular periods; with hepatitis, alongside medical care.

principe.fr: Soothe the Liver, harmonize the Stomach

fiches.precautions: Rose gets Qi and Blood moving: avoid it during pregnancy and during heavy periods. If you take an anticoagulant, ask your doctor. Never use florist roses: they are treated with chemicals.

ingredients.nom: dried food-grade rosebuds or rose petals (mei gui hua)
ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, herbal shops or the organic herbal tea aisle. In season, three handfuls of fresh petals from an unsprayed garden work too.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}), bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, pull the petals off the rosebuds ({rose}); you can also keep the buds whole.
When the rice has fully melted, add the rose and the rock sugar ({sucre}). Simmer for a few minutes, no longer, to keep the fragrance.
Eat it warm, in the morning or evening.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot and start the Porridge or Congee program.
Add the rose petals or buds ({rose}) and rock sugar ({sucre}), stir and leave on Keep Warm with the lid closed.
Eat it warm, in the morning or evening.

notes: The rock sugar is optional: rose already has a sweet, fragrant taste.
Store dried rosebuds in a closed jar, away from light.

fiches.titre: Chinese yam porridge with flour, onion and ginger
fiches.contexte: A thick, comforting porridge: Chinese yam and wheat strengthen the Spleen and Qi, while onion and ginger warm you up. For fatigue; traditionally also for men with declining sexual vigor or seminal emissions.
fiches.precautions: Ground ginger is warming: use less if you often feel hot, have a dry mouth or mouth ulcers. Contains gluten (wheat flour). Diabetes: leave out the sugar.

ingredients.note: Peel it wearing gloves: its sap makes your skin itch. You'll find it in Asian grocery stores (a long, beige, hairy root).

etapes.texte: Wash and peel the yam ({igname}), cut it into chunks, then crush them into small pieces with the flat of a knife.
In a pot off the heat, whisk the flour ({farine}) while adding the cold water ({eau}) little by little, until there are no lumps. Add the yam.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, then lower the heat and let it thicken gently, stirring often so it doesn't stick.
Add the onion ({oignon}), ground ginger ({gingembre}) and whole cane sugar ({sucre}). Keep cooking until the onion is tender.
Thin with a little hot water if it's too thick and eat hot. You can have it often.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Wash and peel the yam ({igname}), cut it into chunks, then crush them into small pieces with the flat of a knife.
In a bowl, whisk the flour ({farine}) while adding the cold water ({eau}) little by little, until there are no lumps. Transfer to the inner pot and add the yam.
Start the Porridge or Soup program; stir once or twice during cooking if your appliance allows it.
Add the onion ({oignon}), ginger ({gingembre}) and whole cane sugar ({sucre}), stir and keep cooking.
Thin with a little hot water if needed and eat hot.

notes: Gluten-free: replace the wheat flour with the same amount of rice flour.
If onion is hard on your stomach, soften it first for 5 minutes in a spoonful of oil before adding it.

fiches.titre: Glutinous rice congee with jujubes and whole cane sugar
fiches.contexte: Glutinous rice warms the Center (the Spleen and Stomach) and tonifies Qi, jujubes nourish Qi and Blood, and whole cane sugar warms. A comforting bowl for cold days, when you're tired and chilly, or when your belly aches and warmth helps.
fiches.precautions: Glutinous rice is sticky and filling: not if your digestion feels blocked, your belly is bloated, or you have phlegm or a fever. For children and older people, give small, piping-hot portions. Diabetes: avoid it (glutinous rice and sugar raise blood sugar quickly).

ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores (opaque white grains), sometimes sold as sticky rice or sweet rice.

etapes.texte: Rinse the glutinous rice ({riz}) several times, then let it soak in a large bowl of cold water.
Drain the rice and put it in a heavy-bottomed pot with the water ({eau}), jujubes ({dattes}) and ginger ({gingembre}). Bring to a boil.
Let it simmer over low heat with the lid ajar. Stir often, scraping the bottom: glutinous rice sticks quickly.
Remove the ginger, add the whole cane sugar ({sucre}) and stir until it melts.
Eat it hot, ideally in the morning or as an afternoon snack.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Rinse the glutinous rice ({riz}) several times, then let it soak in a large bowl of cold water.
Drain the rice and put it in the inner pot with the water ({eau}), jujubes ({dattes}) and ginger ({gingembre}).
Start the Porridge or Congee program.
Remove the ginger, add the whole cane sugar ({sucre}), stir and eat hot.

notes: For a lighter congee, replace half the glutinous rice with short-grain rice.
It thickens a lot as it cools: reheat it with a little hot water.

fiches.titre: Oat congee with apple and cinnamon
fiches.contexte: A warm, gentle breakfast for the Spleen: oats nourish without weighing you down, cooked apple is easy to digest and cinnamon warms the Stomach. Ideal if you have little appetite in the morning, digest slowly or often feel cold.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, warm the Stomach

fiches.precautions: Cinnamon is warming: use less if you often feel hot, have a dry mouth or mouth ulcers. Gluten intolerance: choose certified gluten-free oats.

ingredients.nom: apple, diced small (skin on if organic)
jujubes (Chinese red dates), pitted and chopped

etapes.texte: Put the water ({eau}), apple ({pomme}), jujubes ({dattes}) and cinnamon ({cannelle}) in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the oats ({avoine}) and salt ({sel}), lower the heat and cook gently, stirring often, until creamy.
Cover off the heat: the oats finish swelling.
Eat hot, thinned with a little hot water if you like it runnier.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the oats ({avoine}), apple ({pomme}), jujubes ({dattes}), cinnamon ({cannelle}), salt ({sel}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot, then stir.
Start the Porridge program.
Stir, thin with a little hot water if needed and eat hot.

notes: With a rice cooker, set a delayed start in the evening: breakfast is ready when you wake up.
Old-fashioned rolled oats hold up better during cooking than instant oats.

fiches.contexte: Corn and millet harmonize the Stomach and gently help clear Dampness by promoting urination. A light congee for times when you feel heavy and a bit bloated, with sluggish digestion or a sticky, coated mouth.
fiches.precautions: Millet is slightly cooling: if your belly often feels cold or your stools are very soft, add 2 slices of fresh ginger while it cooks.

ingredients.note: Or 100 g of fresh or frozen corn kernels, added at the same time as the millet.

etapes.texte: Rinse the millet ({millet}) until the water runs clear. Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil, add the millet and let it simmer.
Sprinkle in the cornmeal ({mais}) while whisking to avoid lumps.
Let it simmer over low heat with the lid ajar, stirring often: the mixture thickens and sticks easily.
Add a little salt ({sel}), thin with hot water if it's too thick and eat hot.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed millet ({millet}), cornmeal ({mais}) and cold water ({eau}) in the inner pot and whisk well.
Start the Porridge or Congee program; stir once halfway through if your appliance allows it.
Add a little salt ({sel}), stir and eat hot.

notes: If you find fresh corn on the cob, first simmer its silk (the fine threads) in the water for 15 minutes, remove it, then cook the millet in that water: it boosts the draining effect.
The congee thickens as it cools; it keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

fiches.titre: Squash and carrot congee with ginger
fiches.contexte: Warm and light, to support the Spleen and settle nausea.

principe.fr: Strengthen the Spleen, harmonize the Stomach

ingredients.note: In a rice cooker, fill up to the Porridge line of the inner pot instead.

ingredients.nom: thin slices of fresh ginger, skin on
stalks of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}) 2 or 3 times, until the water runs almost clear.
Put the rice, water ({eau}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down low and leave the lid ajar. Stir from time to time.
Add the carrots ({carotte}) and squash ({courge}). Let it simmer until the rice grains burst and turn creamy. Add a little hot water if it gets too thick.
Add salt ({sel}). Beat the eggs ({oeuf}) and pour them in a thin stream while stirring, until they set into cooked ribbons.
Sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}) and eat warm.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}) in a strainer, 2 or 3 times.

Put the rice, carrots ({carotte}), squash ({courge}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the inner pot. Add water up to the Porridge or Congee line. If there's no line, use about 8 times the volume of the rice.
Start the Porridge, Congee or Soup program. If there isn't one, use Simmer or Slow Cook. Don't open the lid while it cooks.
Add salt ({sel}). Beat the eggs ({oeuf}) and pour them in a thin stream into the piping-hot congee, stirring with a non-metal spatula.
Sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}). Keep leftovers in the fridge rather than on Keep Warm all night.

notes: Metal utensils damage nonstick inner pots.
To reheat a portion, add a little water, and add the egg at the last minute.
You can swap the squash for peeled chestnuts.

fiches.titre: Millet, sweet potato and jujube congee
fiches.contexte: Millet and sweet potato strengthen the Spleen, and jujubes tonify Qi and Blood. Ideal for breakfast when tiredness takes over.

etapes.texte: Rinse the millet ({millet}) in a fine strainer.
Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the jujubes ({dattes}) and ginger ({gingembre}). Pour in the millet and turn the heat down.
Add the sweet potato ({patate}). Let it simmer, stirring often, until the millet is very soft.
Remove the jujube pits, add a little salt ({sel}) and serve warm.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Rinse the millet ({millet}), then put it in the inner pot with the sweet potato ({patate}), jujubes ({dattes}) and ginger ({gingembre}). Add water up to the Porridge line.
Porridge, Congee or Soup program (otherwise Simmer).
Remove the jujube pits and add a little salt ({sel}).

notes: You'll find millet in organic food stores and Asian grocery stores.
If you can't find jujubes (Chinese red dates), use regular dates: they're sweeter, so use fewer.

fiches.contexte: Chinese yam (shan yao) gently tonifies the Spleen, Lung and Kidney without being heating.

principe.fr: Tonify the Spleen, Lung and Kidney

ingredients.nom: fresh Chinese yam (shan yao), peeled and diced
