ingredients.note: Peel it wearing gloves: its sap makes your skin itch. Or use 30 g of dried shan yao, soaked for 1 h.

etapes.texte: Rinse the rice ({riz}), bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer with the lid ajar.
Add the yam ({igname}) and jujubes ({dattes}). Keep cooking, stirring now and then.
Add the goji berries ({goji}) for the last few minutes, add salt ({sel}) and serve.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed rice ({riz}), yam ({igname}) and jujubes ({dattes}) in the inner pot. Add water up to the Porridge line.
Porridge, Congee or Soup program.
Add the goji berries ({goji}), leave for 5 minutes on Keep Warm, then add salt ({sel}).

notes: You'll find fresh Chinese yam in Asian grocery stores (a long, beige, hairy root), or dried as white slices.

fiches.titre: Chicken broth with astragalus and jujubes
fiches.contexte: Astragalus (Huang Qi) strengthens Qi and your body's barrier against cold. Ideal for preventing colds when you sweat at the slightest effort.

principe.fr: Tonify Qi, strengthen the body's surface

fiches.precautions: Not during a cold or a fever: astragalus “closes” the surface and would keep the illness trapped inside.

etapes.texte: Drop the chicken ({poulet}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put the chicken, astragalus ({huangqi}), jujubes ({dattes}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the cold water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then let it simmer, covered.
Add the carrots ({carotte}) and keep cooking gently.
Remove the astragalus slices, add salt ({sel}) and serve the broth with the meat.
Drop the chicken ({poulet}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put all the ingredients except the salt in the inner pot, with the water ({eau}), without going over the max line.
Soup or Simmer program.
Remove the astragalus and add salt ({sel}).
Drop the chicken ({poulet}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put all the ingredients except the salt in the pressure cooker, filling it no more than two-thirds full. Close the lid and start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own, remove the astragalus and add salt ({sel}).

notes: The astragalus slices aren't meant to be eaten.
You'll find astragalus in Asian grocery stores and Chinese herbal shops.

fiches.titre: Congee with goji berries, jujubes and black sesame
fiches.contexte: Goji, jujubes and black sesame nourish the Blood and the Yin of the Liver and Kidney: good for your eyes, your hair and dry skin.

principe.fr: Nourish the Blood, the Liver and the Kidney

ingredients.nom: black sesame seeds, toasted and ground

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the sesame seeds ({sesame}) in a frying pan for 2 minutes, then grind them.
Rinse the rice ({riz}) and bring it to a boil in the water ({eau}) with the jujubes ({dattes}). Let it simmer with the lid ajar, stirring.
Add the goji berries ({goji}) and the sesame, and cook a few minutes more.
Sweeten with honey if you like ({miel}), once the bowl has cooled a little.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the sesame seeds ({sesame}) for 2 minutes, then grind them.
Put the rinsed rice ({riz}) and jujubes ({dattes}) in the inner pot, with water up to the Porridge line. Porridge or Congee program.
Add the goji ({goji}) and the sesame, then leave 5 minutes on Keep Warm. Add the honey when serving ({miel}).

notes: Honey shouldn't be cooked: stir it into the bowl once it's warm, not hot.

fiches.titre: Spinach and egg soup with sesame
fiches.contexte: Spinach nourishes the Blood and moistens the intestines, and egg nourishes the Blood and Yin. A quick evening soup.
fiches.precautions: Spinach is cooling and loosens the bowels: go easy on it if your stools are very soft.

ingredients.nom: vegetable or chicken broth, or water

etapes.texte: Bring the broth ({bouillon}) to a simmer with the ginger ({gingembre}).
Add the spinach ({epinards}) and let it wilt.
Beat the eggs ({oeuf}) and pour them in a thin stream while stirring.
Add salt ({sel}), drizzle with sesame oil ({sesame}) and serve right away.

fiches.titre: Creamy beet and red lentil soup
fiches.contexte: Beet nourishes the Blood and gets it moving, and red lentils support the Spleen and provide iron.

principe.fr: Nourish the Blood and get it moving

etapes.texte: Gently fry the onion ({oignon}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the oil ({huile}).
Add the beet ({betterave}), carrot ({carotte}), lentils ({lentilles}) and water ({eau}). Let it simmer, covered.
Remove the ginger, blend, add salt ({sel}) and adjust the thickness with a little water.
On the Sauté setting, gently fry the onion ({oignon}) and ginger ({gingembre}) in the oil ({huile}). If you don't have one, just add them in.
Add the beet ({betterave}), carrot ({carotte}), lentils ({lentilles}) and water ({eau}). Soup program.
Remove the ginger, blend and add salt ({sel}).

notes: Your urine and stools may turn pinkish after eating beet: that's normal.

fiches.contexte: Longan nourishes Heart Blood and calms the mind. Drink it in the late afternoon when your sleep is light and your mind is restless.

principe.fr: Nourish the Heart, calm the mind

fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have a lot of bloating or a thick coating on your tongue: longan is sweet and a little heavy.

etapes.texte: Put the longans ({longane}), jujubes ({dattes}) and water ({eau}) in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Add the goji ({goji}), let it steep off the heat, then drink it warm and eat the fruit.

fiches.contexte: Lotus seeds calm the Heart and strengthen the Spleen, and jujubes nourish the Blood. For insomnia, worry and a delicate digestion.

principe.fr: Nourish the Heart, strengthen the Spleen

ingredients.note: Keep the green germ if the tip of your tongue is red (it cools the Heart); otherwise remove it, as it's bitter.

etapes.texte: Drain the lotus seeds ({lotus}), put them in the water ({eau}) with the jujubes ({dattes}), bring to a boil and let it simmer.
Add the rinsed rice ({riz}) and keep cooking over low heat, lid ajar, stirring.
Remove the jujube pits and serve warm, plain or with a little honey.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the drained lotus seeds ({lotus}), rinsed rice ({riz}) and jujubes ({dattes}) in the inner pot. Add water up to the Porridge line.
Porridge or Congee program.

notes: For congee that's ready when you wake up, use your cooker's delay timer.

fiches.titre: Steamed pears with almonds and honey
fiches.contexte: Pear moistens the Lung and soothes a dry cough, and almond helps Lung Qi descend. A dessert that works as a remedy.

principe.fr: Moisten the Lung, calm the cough

fiches.precautions: If your phlegm is white and abundant, choose the daikon soup instead: pear is cooling.

etapes.texte: Cut the tops off the pears ({poire}) and scoop out the core with a teaspoon. Fill with almonds ({amandes}), goji ({goji}) and honey ({miel}). Put the tops back on.
Set them in a bowl over a pot of simmering water, with the lid on.
Eat warm and drink the juice at the bottom of the bowl.
Cut the tops off the pears ({poire}), scoop out the core and fill with almonds ({amandes}), goji ({goji}) and honey ({miel}).
Put water in the inner pot as the manual says, and the pears in a bowl set in the steamer basket. Steam program.

fiches.titre: Snow fungus, lotus seed and goji soup
fiches.contexte: Snow fungus (white fungus, Bai Mu Er) nourishes the Yin of the Lung and Stomach. Lightly sweet, it's enjoyed like a warm dessert.

etapes.texte: Soak the snow fungus ({tremelle}) in lukewarm water until it swells up.
Cut off the hard yellow base, then tear the fungus into small pieces.
Put the snow fungus, lotus seeds ({lotus}), jujubes ({dattes}) and water ({eau}) in a pot. Let it simmer, covered, until the soup turns slightly jelly-like.
Add the goji ({goji}) and sugar ({sucre}), and cook a few minutes more.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Soak the snow fungus ({tremelle}), cut off the hard base and tear it into pieces.
Put everything except the goji in the inner pot. Soup, Porridge or Simmer program.
Add the goji ({goji}), then leave 5 minutes on Keep Warm.

notes: You'll find dried snow fungus in Asian grocery stores (also labeled “white fungus” or “silver ear”).

fiches.titre: Black bean, walnut and black sesame congee
fiches.contexte: Black beans and black sesame nourish the Kidney and Yin, and walnuts gently warm the Kidney. A deeply nourishing dish to eat regularly for a weak lower back, your hair and your memory.

ingredients.nom: black sesame seeds, toasted and ground

etapes.texte: Drain the beans ({haricots}), cover them with the water ({eau}), bring to a boil and let them simmer.
Add the rinsed rice ({riz}) and keep cooking over low heat, stirring, until creamy.
Add the walnuts ({noix}) and sesame ({sesame}), then add salt ({sel}).

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the drained beans ({haricots}) and rinsed rice ({riz}) in the inner pot, with water up to the Porridge line.
Porridge, Beans or Simmer program, on the longest setting.
Add the walnuts ({noix}) and sesame ({sesame}), then add salt ({sel}).
Put the drained beans ({haricots}), rinsed rice ({riz}) and water ({eau}) in the pressure cooker. Start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own, add the walnuts ({noix}) and sesame ({sesame}), then add salt ({sel}).

notes: In a pinch, a store-bought black soybean and Chinese yam powder stirred into hot water works along the same lines. Check for added sugar.

fiches.titre: Braised lamb with Chinese angelica and ginger
fiches.contexte: A classic winter recipe: lamb and ginger warm you up, and Chinese angelica (Dang Gui) nourishes the Blood and gets it moving. For feeling cold, painful periods eased by warmth, and fatigue with a pale complexion.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you have signs of heat (red tongue, thirst, night sweats) or heavy periods, and during pregnancy unless a practitioner says it's OK.

variantes.nom: In a cast-iron casserole pot or saucepan

etapes.texte: Drop the lamb ({agneau}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put in the lamb, angelica ({danggui}), ginger ({gingembre}), onion ({oignon}) and water ({eau}). Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then let it simmer, covered.
Add the carrots ({carotte}) and keep cooking until the meat is meltingly tender.
Remove the angelica, then season with salt and pepper ({sel}).
Drop the lamb ({agneau}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put all the ingredients except the salt in the inner pot. Simmer or Stew program.
Remove the angelica, then season with salt and pepper ({sel}).
Drop the lamb ({agneau}) into boiling water, then rinse it.
Put all the ingredients except the salt in the pressure cooker. Start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own, remove the angelica, then season with salt and pepper ({sel}).

notes: You'll find Chinese angelica in Asian grocery stores or Chinese herbal shops.
Without angelica, it's still a good warming ginger stew.

fiches.titre: Stir-fried shrimp with leeks and walnuts
fiches.contexte: Shrimp, leek and walnuts warm Kidney Yang. A quick dish for fatigue when you feel the cold easily and your lower back feels cold.
fiches.precautions: Avoid it if you're allergic to shellfish, if you have eczema or hives that react to seafood, or if you have signs of heat.

ingredients.nom: slices of ginger, cut into thin matchsticks

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Dry-toast the walnuts ({noix}) in the pan, then set them aside.
Heat the oil ({huile}), fry the ginger ({gingembre}) for a few seconds, then the leek ({poireau}) until it softens.
Add the shrimp ({crevettes}) and sear them until they turn pink.
Add the soy sauce ({soja}) and the walnuts, stir and serve with rice.

fiches.contexte: To warm the center when cold takes over: cold belly, icy hands, periods eased by warmth.
fiches.precautions: Not if you have signs of heat (red tongue, thirst, night sweats, mouth ulcers), and not every day over a long period.

etapes.texte: Put the ginger ({gingembre}), cinnamon ({cannelle}) and water ({eau}) in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Sweeten if you like ({sucre}) and drink hot.

fiches.titre: Pearl barley and adzuki bean congee
fiches.contexte: Chinese pearl barley (Yi Yi Ren) and adzuki beans drain Dampness through the urine: for heaviness, swelling (edema), and oily or weeping skin.
fiches.precautions: Chinese pearl barley (Yi Yi Ren) is not recommended during pregnancy.

ingredients.nom: Chinese pearl barley (Job's tears, Yi Yi Ren)
ingredients.note: In Asian grocery stores, it's sold as “Job's tears”. Regular pearl barley works too.

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed barley ({orge}) and the drained adzuki beans ({azuki}) in the water ({eau}). Bring to a boil and let it simmer.
Add the rinsed rice ({riz}) and keep cooking over low heat, stirring.
Add a little salt ({sel}), or leave it plain for breakfast.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the barley ({orge}), drained adzuki beans ({azuki}) and rice ({riz}) in the inner pot, with water up to the Porridge line.
Porridge, Beans or Simmer program, on the longest setting.
Put everything in the pressure cooker with the water ({eau}). Start timing once it starts to hiss.
Let the pressure drop on its own and add a little salt ({sel}).

fiches.titre: Daikon soup with ginger and tangerine peel
fiches.contexte: Daikon (white radish) makes Qi descend, transforms phlegm and gets digestion moving; tangerine peel dries Dampness.

ingredients.nom: dried tangerine peel (or the zest of an organic tangerine)
stalk of spring onion, finely sliced

etapes.texte: Put the daikon ({radis}), carrot ({carotte}), ginger ({gingembre}), tangerine peel ({mandarine}) and water ({eau}) in a pot. Bring to a boil, then let it simmer until the daikon turns translucent.
Add salt ({sel}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).
Put everything except the salt and spring onion in the inner pot. Soup program.
Add salt ({sel}) and sprinkle with spring onion ({cebette}).

notes: You'll find daikon in Asian grocery stores, and often in the produce section of supermarkets.

fiches.contexte: Tangerine peel (Chen Pi) gets Spleen Qi moving and dries Dampness: for sluggish digestion, bloating and white phlegm.

principe.py: Lǐ qì jiàn pí zào shī
principe.fr: Move Qi, strengthen the Spleen, dry Dampness

ingredients.nom: dried tangerine peel (or the zest of an organic tangerine)

etapes.texte: Put the peel ({mandarine}), ginger ({gingembre}) and water ({eau}) in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then let it simmer.
Drink warm, ideally after a meal.

notes: Dry organic tangerine peels yourself in the open air for a few days: the older they get, the better they are.

fiches.contexte: Mung beans clear Heat and flush out toxins: for summer, thirst, skin that feels hot or red pimples.
fiches.precautions: Cooling: avoid it if you feel the cold easily and have soft stools and a cold belly.

ingredients.nom: whole green mung beans (not bean sprouts)

etapes.texte: Rinse the beans ({mungo}), bring them to a boil in the water ({eau}), then let it simmer. To clear Heat, drink some of this green broth right away.
For a more nourishing soup, keep going until the beans burst.
Sweeten lightly if you like ({sucre}). Drink it warm, or at room temperature in summer.

variantes.nom: In a rice cooker or multicooker

etapes.texte: Put the rinsed beans ({mungo}) and water ({eau}) in the inner pot. Soup or Porridge program.
Sweeten lightly if you like ({sucre}).

fiches.contexte: Chrysanthemum clears the Liver and soothes red or tired eyes, and goji nourishes Liver Yin. Ideal after a day in front of screens.

principe.fr: Clear the Liver, brighten the eyes

fiches.precautions: A little cooling: go easy on it if you have a cold belly and soft stools.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Pour the water ({eau}) over the flowers ({chrysantheme}) and goji ({goji}), cover and let it steep.
Drink warm; you can top up the same flowers with hot water once or twice.

fiches.titre: Stir-fried celery and tofu with ginger
fiches.contexte: Celery calms Liver Yang and clears Heat, and tofu nourishes Yin. A simple dish for headaches at the temples and irritability.

ingredients.nom: celery stalks, sliced on the diagonal
slices of ginger, cut into matchsticks

variantes.nom: In a frying pan or wok

etapes.texte: Brown the tofu ({tofu}) in the oil ({huile}) on all sides, then set it aside.
Fry the ginger ({gingembre}) for a few seconds, then the celery ({celeri}): it should stay a little crunchy.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the soy sauce ({soja}) and spring onion ({cebette}). Serve with rice.

fiches.contexte: Rosebud gets Liver Qi and Blood moving, and orange zest relaxes the belly: for stress, sighing and tension before your period.
fiches.precautions: During pregnancy or if your periods are very heavy, ask for advice first: rose gets the Blood moving.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Pour the water ({eau}) over the rosebuds ({rose}) and zest ({orange}), cover and let it steep.
Drink warm, in a quiet moment.

fiches.contexte: A traditional remedy for the first hours of a chill-type cold: spring onion whites and ginger make you sweat a little and drive out the cold.
fiches.precautions: Only at the very start, with chills and a clear runny nose. Not if you have a sore throat, a high fever or yellow phlegm.

ingredients.nom: spring onion whites with their roots, washed

etapes.texte: Bring the water ({eau}) to a boil with the spring onion ({cebette}) and ginger ({gingembre}), then simmer only very briefly: the active compounds are volatile.
Add the sugar ({sucre}), drink it piping hot and bundle up so you sweat a little.

fiches.contexte: For the start of a heat-type cold: scratchy throat, a slight fever, stinging eyes.

variantes.nom: In a teapot or a bowl

etapes.texte: Pour the water ({eau}) over the mint ({menthe}) and chrysanthemum ({chrysantheme}), cover and let it steep.
Add the honey once it's warm ({miel}) and drink in small sips.

fiches.titre: Warm apple and pear compote with prunes
fiches.contexte: Cooked apple and pear moisten the intestines without chilling them, and prunes keep things moving. For constipation due to dryness.

principe.fr: Moisten the intestines, ease bowel movements

etapes.texte: Put the apples ({pomme}), pears ({poire}), prunes ({pruneaux}), cinnamon ({cannelle}) and water ({eau}) in a saucepan. Cover and let it cook down over low heat.
Mash roughly and eat warm, ideally in the morning.

symptomes.nom: Fatigue during or after cancer treatment
symptomes.syn: fatigue tiredness exhaustion asthenia cancer-related fatigue chemotherapy chemo radiotherapy radiation immunotherapy cancer
symptomes.alerte: Tell your care team about this fatigue: anemia or another side effect of the treatment can be corrected.

symptomes.syn: nausea chemo chemotherapy vomiting throwing up queasy feeling sick
symptomes.alerte: If you vomit several times a day or can no longer drink, contact your care team right away.

symptomes.nom: Dry mouth or small sores in the mouth after treatment
symptomes.syn: mucositis mouth sores mouth ulcers dry mouth saliva chemo radiotherapy radiation loss of taste
symptomes.alerte: If the pain stops you from eating or drinking, tell your care team.

symptomes.nom: Tingling or numbness in the hands and feet after chemotherapy
symptomes.syn: neuropathy peripheral neuropathy pins and needles tingling prickling numbness hands feet chemo oxaliplatin taxol paclitaxel
symptomes.alerte: Tell your oncologist about this tingling: the treatment can be adjusted. No hot-water bottle or moxa on an area with reduced feeling: risk of burns.

symptomes.nom: Hot flashes caused by hormone therapy
symptomes.syn: hormone therapy endocrine therapy tamoxifen aromatase inhibitor hot flashes hot flushes breast cancer prostate cancer
symptomes.alerte: Don't stop your hormone therapy without talking to your oncologist: there are solutions. No soy, red clover, hops or Chinese angelica (dang gui) supplements.

symptomes.nom: Red, dry or burning skin in the radiotherapy area
symptomes.syn: radiation dermatitis radiodermatitis radiation burn radiotherapy radiation red skin dry skin
symptomes.alerte: Don't put anything on the treated area without your radiotherapy team's approval, don't massage it, and keep it out of the sun.

symptomes.syn: thyroid hypothyroidism underactive thyroid hashimoto hashimoto's thyroiditis levothyroxine synthroid high TSH
symptomes.alerte: Keep taking your treatment and having your blood tests: these routines go alongside it, they don't replace it.
symptomes.rappel: Thyroid: no iodine or seaweed supplements without medical advice, and skip the wakame in the recipes.

tableaux.resume: The Heart lacks strength: palpitations on exertion, shortness of breath, tiredness, sweating easily.
tableaux.mecanisme: Heart Qi makes the heart beat and moves the Blood. When it weakens, your heart races on exertion and the slightest activity leaves you out of breath and sweating.
tableaux.consulter: Palpitations should be checked by a doctor (electrocardiogram), especially if they are new or frequent.

items.pourquoi: Opens the chest, regulates the Heart.
Tonifies the Qi of the chest.
Tonifies the Qi of the whole body.

tableaux.privilegier: Grains, jujubes, longans, lotus seeds, chicken, regular meals.
tableaux.eviter: Overwork, too much coffee, strenuous exertion.
conseils: Alternate activity with real breaks during the day.
tableaux.simple: Your heart lacks energy: it races at the slightest effort and you get out of breath quickly.

tableaux.resume: Blood no longer nourishes the mind: palpitations, trouble falling asleep, lots of dreams, poor memory.
causes: A weak Spleen that makes little Blood
tableaux.mecanisme: The mind (Shen) resides in the Heart Blood. Without enough Blood, it loses its anchor: you struggle to fall asleep, dream a lot, and your memory lets you down.

items.pourquoi: Yuan-Source point of the Heart: calms the mind, helps sleep.
Strengthens the Spleen, which makes Blood.

tableaux.privilegier: Jujubes, longans, goji berries, eggs, spinach, grains, lotus seeds.
tableaux.eviter: Screens in the evening, eating dinner too late, coffee in the afternoon.
conseils: Go to bed at the same time every night.
Longan and jujube tea in the late afternoon.
tableaux.simple: Your mind is no longer well nourished: light sleep, a racing heart, a failing memory, vague anxiety.

tableaux.resume: Yin no longer holds the Heart steady: palpitations, restlessness, waking at night, night sweats, dry mouth.
tableaux.mecanisme: Yin calms and cools the Heart. When it runs low, Deficiency Heat stirs the mind at night: waking up, sweating, a racing heart.

items.pourquoi: Nourishes Heart Yin, stops night sweats.

tableaux.privilegier: Snow fungus (white wood ear), lotus seeds, pear, tofu, eggs, sesame, millet.
tableaux.eviter: Coffee, alcohol, spices, intense exercise in the evening, late-night screens.
conseils: Cool, dark bedroom; light dinner.
tableaux.simple: Your heart overheats from exhaustion: restless nights, waking up sweaty, nervousness.

tableaux.resume: Heat agitates the Heart: restlessness, insomnia, ulcers on the tongue, thirst, dark urine.
causes: Too much coffee, alcohol, spicy food
tableaux.mecanisme: Fire rises to the Heart and to the tongue, its “sprout”: red tongue tip, mouth ulcers, a restless mind that can't find sleep.
tableaux.langue: Red, redder and swollen tip, sometimes ulcerated.
tableaux.privilegier: Mung beans, lotus seeds with their green germ, green vegetables, cooked cucumber.
tableaux.eviter: Coffee, alcohol, spices, screens in the evening, overwork.
tableaux.simple: Too much heat agitates the heart and mind: nervousness, sleepless nights, mouth ulcers.

tableaux.resume: Worry wears out the Spleen, which no longer makes enough Blood for the Heart: tiredness, rumination, insomnia, palpitations.
tableaux.mecanisme: Overthinking tires the Spleen, which makes less Blood. A poorly nourished Heart leaves the mind restless: you ruminate, sleep badly and tire quickly.

items.pourquoi: Calms the mind, harmonizes the Stomach.

tableaux.privilegier: Lotus seeds, longans, jujubes, millet, rice, sweet potato, chicken.
tableaux.eviter: Eating while working, skipping meals, too much sugar.
conseils: Write your worries down on paper before bed to set them aside.
tableaux.simple: Too much worry and fatigue: your mind never stops, you sleep badly, you digest badly.

tableaux.resume: Heart Fire is no longer tempered by Kidney Water: insomnia, palpitations, night sweats, weak lower back.
causes: Prolonged overwork and lack of sleep
tableaux.mecanisme: Kidney Water should rise to cool the Heart, and Heart Fire should descend to warm the Kidney. When this exchange breaks down, the top overheats (restlessness, insomnia) and the bottom weakens (lower back, tinnitus).

principe.fr: Restore the exchange between the Heart and Kidney

items.pourquoi: Brings down what rises, grounds you before sleep.

tableaux.resume: Dry autumn air or indoor heating dries out the Lung: dry cough, dry throat and nose, dry skin, with no real heat.

tableaux.mecanisme: The Lung likes moisture. Dry air takes away its fluids: the cough turns dry, and the throat, nose and skin dry out. This is the stage before Yin Deficiency, without marked heat.

tableaux.simple: Dry air irritates your airways: dry cough, itchy throat and nose.

tableaux.resume: The Stomach lacks strength: little appetite, little sense of taste, discomfort in the pit of the stomach, tiredness especially in the morning.
tableaux.mecanisme: The Stomach receives food and “ripens” it. Without enough Qi, it doesn't take food in well: appetite and taste fade, and a dull discomfort sets in after meals.

tableaux.resume: Acute Cold blocks the intestines: sharp belly pain relieved by warmth, loose stools, chills.
causes: A chill caught in the belly
tableaux.mecanisme: Cold makes the intestines contract: the pain is sharp and cramping, and warmth clearly relieves it.
tableaux.moxa: Moxa or a hot-water bottle recommended.

items.pourquoi: Front-Mu point of the Large Intestine.

tableaux.privilegier: Hot broths, rice, ginger, squash.
tableaux.eviter: Anything cold or raw.
conseils: Hot-water bottle on your belly and a hot broth.
tableaux.simple: Cold grips your belly: intestinal cramps and loose stools after catching a chill.

tableaux.resume: The Liver lacks Yin: dry, tired eyes, blurred vision, dizziness, numbness, a slight feeling of heat in the evening.
tableaux.mecanisme: Liver Yin moistens the eyes and tendons and holds Yang in check. When it runs low, the eyes dry out, the tendons go numb and Deficiency Heat appears.
tableaux.langue: Red, especially on the edges, little coating.
tableaux.privilegier: Goji berries, chrysanthemum, black sesame, eggs, tofu, spinach, squid.
tableaux.eviter: Late-night screens, alcohol, spicy food, staying up late.
conseils: Every 20 minutes of screen time, look into the distance for 20 seconds.
tableaux.simple: Your liver is running low on resources: dry eyes, failing eyesight, dizziness, feeling warm in the evening.

tableaux.resume: Heat agitates the Blood: short cycles, heavy bright-red periods, restlessness, thirst.
tableaux.mecanisme: Heat pushes Blood out of the vessels and speeds up the cycle: periods come early, heavy and bright red.
tableaux.consulter: Very heavy periods can lead to anemia: talk to a doctor about it.
tableaux.privilegier: Green vegetables, celery, cooked cucumber, mung beans, tofu.
tableaux.eviter: Spicy food, alcohol, coffee, lamb, fried food.
tableaux.simple: Too much heat in the blood: early, heavy, bright-red periods.

tableaux.resume: Stress and held-in emotions block the free flow of Qi: tension, sighing, a tight throat, changeable mood.
tableaux.mecanisme: The Liver keeps Qi flowing freely. When emotions block it, Qi gets stuck: under the ribs, in the throat, in the breasts before a period, and it upsets your mood.

principe.fr: Free the Liver, get Qi moving

items.pourquoi: With LR 3: the Four Gates, get Qi moving through the whole body.
Yuan-Source point of the Liver: releases stagnation.
Opens the chest, calms the mind.
Front-Mu point of the Liver: relieves the ribs.

tableaux.privilegier: Green vegetables, radish, citrus peel, spring onion, mint, meals eaten in peace.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, too much coffee, fatty food, a sedentary lifestyle.
conseils: Move every day: brisk walking, dancing, sport. Movement frees Liver Qi.
Stretch your sides and let out a real sigh: Qi needs to get out.
tableaux.simple: Stress blocks everything: tension, a tight throat, mood swings, digestion that follows your emotions.

tableaux.resume: Blood no longer nourishes the eyes, tendons and hair enough: blurred vision, floaters, cramps, scanty periods.
causes: A weak Spleen that makes little Blood
tableaux.mecanisme: The Liver stores Blood. When Blood runs low, everything that depends on it dries out: the eyes (blurred vision, floaters), the tendons (cramps, pins and needles), the nails and the hair.
tableaux.langue: Pale, especially on the edges, a little dry.
tableaux.moxa: Gentle moxa is fine on ST 36.

items.pourquoi: Strengthens the Spleen, the source of Blood.

tableaux.privilegier: Goji berries, jujubes, black sesame, spinach, beets, lentils, eggs, a little red meat, bone broths.
tableaux.eviter: Screens late in the evening, staying up late, restrictive diets.
conseils: Rest your eyes every hour: Liver Blood nourishes your eyesight.
In bed before 11 pm: Blood returns to the Liver at night.
A blood test (iron, ferritin, B12) can rule out anemia.
tableaux.simple: There isn't enough blood to nourish your eyes, muscles and hair: blurred vision, cramps, hair loss.

tableaux.resume: Liver Yang rises to the head because Yin no longer holds it back: headaches at the temples, dizziness, tinnitus, irritability.
tableaux.mecanisme: Yin holds Yang in check. When Yin weakens, Liver Yang rises like a flame to the head: tight temples, dizziness, ringing in the ears.

items.pourquoi: Brings Yang down from the head.
Nourishes Kidney Yin, which holds Yang back.

tableaux.privilegier: Celery, chrysanthemum, spinach, tofu, green vegetables, mushrooms.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, coffee, spicy food, brooding over anger, late-night screens.
conseils: Have your blood pressure checked if these headaches keep coming back.
Massage the soles of your feet (KI 1) in the evening to bring down what rises.
tableaux.simple: Pressure rises to your head: headaches at the temples, dizziness, irritability.

tableaux.resume: Intense Liver Heat flares upward: anger, red eyes, bitter taste, violent headaches, restless sleep.
causes: Liver Qi Stagnation that heats up
tableaux.mecanisme: Liver Qi that stays blocked for a long time heats up until it becomes Fire, which rushes up to the eyes, the head and the mouth.
tableaux.langue: Red, redder edges, dry yellow coating.

items.pourquoi: Brings Fire down from the head.

tableaux.privilegier: Celery, chrysanthemum, cooked cucumber, tofu, bean sprouts, mung beans.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, spicy food, fried food, lamb, tobacco.
conseils: Let your anger out in other ways: intense exercise, writing, talking.
tableaux.simple: Intense heat rises to your head: anger, red eyes, violent headaches.

tableaux.nom: Damp-Heat in the Liver and Gallbladder
tableaux.resume: Dampness and Heat stagnate in the Liver and Gallbladder: pain under the ribs, bitter taste, nausea, genital discharge or itching.
tableaux.mecanisme: Damp-Heat blocks the Gallbladder (bitter taste, trouble digesting fat) and flows down along the Liver meridian to the genital area.

principe.py: Qīng lì gān dǎn shī rè
principe.fr: Clear and drain Damp-Heat from the Liver and Gallbladder

tableaux.consulter: Pain under the ribs with fever or jaundice must be seen by a doctor quickly.

items.pourquoi: Frees the Liver, relieves the ribs.
Clears Damp-Heat from the genital area.

tableaux.privilegier: Celery, radish, pearl barley, mung and adzuki beans, cooked green vegetables.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, fatty food, fried food, sugar, spicy food.
tableaux.simple: Dampness and heat clog your liver and gallbladder: bitter mouth, nausea, pain under the ribs.

tableaux.resume: Stress blocks the Liver, which upsets digestion: a belly that bloats and stools that change with your emotions.
tableaux.mecanisme: The blocked Liver “attacks” the Spleen: digestion goes off track in step with your emotions, with bloating and alternating stools.
tableaux.langue: Normal or pale, edges sometimes red.
tableaux.pouls: Wiry on the left, weak on the right.

principe.fr: Free the Liver, strengthen the Spleen

items.pourquoi: Front-Mu point of the Spleen: harmonizes the Liver and Spleen.
Strengthens the Spleen, calms the mind.

tableaux.privilegier: Warm, regular meals, eaten in peace; citrus peel, radish, cooked grains.
tableaux.eviter: Eating fast or while working, coffee on an empty stomach, alcohol.
conseils: Take three slow breaths before each meal.
tableaux.simple: Stress throws your digestion off: a belly that bloats, bowel habits that change with your emotions.

tableaux.resume: The blocked Liver sends Stomach Qi back up: heartburn, belching, nausea, linked to stress.
tableaux.mecanisme: Stuck Liver Qi rises and drags Stomach Qi up with it, when it should go down: heartburn, belching, nausea.

principe.fr: Free the Liver, harmonize the Stomach

tableaux.privilegier: Small warm meals, congee, radish, a little fresh ginger.
tableaux.eviter: Coffee, alcohol, spicy food, sour citrus fruit on an empty stomach, late meals.
tableaux.simple: Stress rises into your stomach: heartburn, belching, nausea.

tableaux.nom: Cold Stagnating in the Liver Meridian
tableaux.resume: Cold blocks the Liver meridian, which circles the genitals: cold lower belly and testicles, a pulling pain toward the groin, relieved by warmth.
causes: Cold reaching the lower body: cold floors, cold-water swimming, clothes that are too light or wet
Underlying Yang that is already weak
tableaux.mecanisme: The Liver meridian runs through the groin, circles the genitals, then rises all the way to the top of the head. Cold contracts and blocks: the scrotum tightens, the pain pulls toward the lower belly, sometimes with pain at the top of the head, and warmth brings relief. In women, it causes cold pain in the lower belly and painful periods.
tableaux.moxa: Moxa recommended on CV 4 and LR 1, or a hot-water bottle on the lower belly.
tableaux.consulter: Sudden, intense pain in a testicle is an emergency: call emergency services (15 or 112 in France). A lump or swelling must be seen by a doctor.

items.pourquoi: Frees Liver Qi and calms the pulling pain.
Crossing point of the three Yin meridians of the leg (Liver, Spleen, Kidney), which all run through the lower belly.
Supports Kidney Yang, the source of warmth.
Warms the Liver meridian at its source.
Warms the lower belly and the Kidney.

tableaux.privilegier: Lamb, fennel seeds, ginger, cinnamon, leek, garlic chives, hot slow-cooked dishes.
tableaux.eviter: Iced drinks, sitting on cold floors, cold-water swimming, staying in wet clothes.
conseils: Keep your lower belly and lower back covered, especially in winter.
A hot-water bottle on your lower belly in the evening often brings relief.
tableaux.simple: Cold settles in your lower belly: pain pulling toward the groin, cold genitals.
reperes: Lower belly pain in the cold

tableaux.nom: Damp-Heat Pouring Down the Liver Meridian
tableaux.py: Gān jīng shī rè xià zhù
tableaux.resume: Hot Dampness builds up in the genital area: damp, itchy private parts, yellow discharge, dark urine, erection or ejaculation problems.
causes: Local heat and moisture: tight or synthetic clothing
Anger and frustration that overheat the Liver
tableaux.mecanisme: The Liver meridian circles the genitals. When Damp-Heat flows down into this area, it weighs it down, irritates and overheats it: dampness and odor, itching, yellow discharge, burning when urinating. It can also get in the way of erections or make ejaculation too quick, without any underlying weakness.
tableaux.langue: Red, greasy yellow coating, especially at the back.

principe.py: Qīng lì gān jīng shī rè
principe.fr: Clear and drain Damp-Heat from the Liver meridian

tableaux.consulter: Burning urination with fever, unusual discharge or sores on the genitals must be seen by a doctor.

items.pourquoi: Luo-Connecting point of the Liver: clears Damp-Heat from the genital area.
Drains Dampness from the lower body.
Front-Mu point of the Bladder: clears Damp-Heat from the lower belly.

tableaux.privilegier: Pearl barley, mung and adzuki beans, cucumber, celery, seaweed, radish, plenty of lukewarm water.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, fried food, very spicy food, sugar, cured and processed meats, tight or synthetic underwear.
conseils: Wear loose cotton and change quickly after exercise.
Wash with lukewarm water, without scented soap.
tableaux.simple: Damp heat in your private parts: itching, odor, yellow discharge, burning.

tableaux.resume: Fear, pressure to “perform” or emotional shock: the desire is there but the erection fades at the wrong moment, your heart races, your sleep becomes restless.
tableaux.mecanisme: In Chinese medicine, fear makes Qi “descend” and affects the Kidney, which governs the sexual sphere. At the same time, the Heart, seat of the mind, becomes agitated. Erections become fragile even though desire is present, often with no other sign of physical weakness.
tableaux.pouls: Weak at the Kidney positions, sometimes rapid and irregular under emotion.

principe.fr: Support the Kidney, calm the mind

tableaux.consulter: If erection problems persist, talk to a doctor: they can also come from circulation, diabetes or a medication.

items.pourquoi: Yuan-Source point of the Heart: calms fear and agitation.
Yuan-Source point of the Kidney: strengthens it.
Anchors Qi in the lower belly.
“Residence of the Will”: strengthens the Kidney and confidence.

tableaux.privilegier: Lotus seeds, jujubes, longans, oysters, walnuts, black sesame, regular meals.
tableaux.eviter: Coffee and stimulants, late-night screens, pressure and comparisons.
conseils: Slow breathing: breathe in for 4 seconds, out for 6 seconds, for 5 minutes before sleep.
Fear of failure keeps the block going: talking about it with your partner often takes away much of the pressure.
tableaux.simple: Stress and fear leave you powerless: the erection fades even though the desire is there.
Your reserves of warmth and coolness run out at the same time: hot flashes then chills, sweating, cold feet, fatigue.
tableaux.resume: The Kidney runs down on both sides at once: you feel hot then cold, sweat at night yet have icy feet, your lower back is weak. The most typical pattern of menopause.
causes: Age and the natural decline of the Kidney's reserves
tableaux.mecanisme: The Kidney holds both Yin, which cools, and Yang, which warms. Around menopause, both decline together: Yin no longer tempers heat (hot flashes, sweating), and Yang no longer warms the lower body (cold feet, urinating at night). Hence these signs that seem contradictory.
tableaux.langue: Pale or slightly red, little coating.
tableaux.pouls: Deep, thready and weak, especially at the Kidney positions.

principe.fr: Balance and tonify Kidney Yin and Yang

tableaux.moxa: Gentle moxa is fine on CV 4 when your feet are cold, never during a hot flash.
tableaux.consulter: Bleeding after menopause, very troublesome hot flashes, persistent sadness or bone pain should be discussed with a doctor.

items.pourquoi: Yuan-Source point of the Kidney: supports both Yin and Yang.
Nourishes Yin, calms heat and helps sleep.
Crossing point of the three Yin meridians: nourishes Blood and Yin.

tableaux.privilegier: Black beans, black sesame, walnuts, Chinese yam, goji berries, duck, fish, slow-cooked soups, regular meals.
tableaux.eviter: Coffee, alcohol, very spicy food, late and heavy meals, late-night screens.
conseils: Keep your feet warm but your head cool: socks and a well-aired bedroom.
A daily walk and a regular bedtime often ease hot flashes.

tableaux.resume: Energy and Blood are both lacking: deep tiredness, paleness, dizziness, shortness of breath, palpitations.
tableaux.mecanisme: Qi makes Blood and moves it along, and Blood nourishes Qi. When one runs low, the other follows: you wear out, turn pale, your head spins.
tableaux.moxa: Gentle moxa is fine on ST 36 and CV 6.

items.pourquoi: Strengthens the Spleen, the source of Qi and Blood.

tableaux.privilegier: Broths, jujubes, goji berries, eggs, meat in small amounts, grains, legumes.
tableaux.eviter: Restrictive diets, overwork, skipping meals.
conseils: A blood test (iron, ferritin, B12) can rule out anemia.
tableaux.simple: Your body lacks both energy and blood: deep tiredness, paleness, dizziness.

tableaux.resume: The Liver and Kidney lack Yin: dry eyes, dizziness, tinnitus, weak lower back, feeling warm in the evening.
tableaux.mecanisme: The Liver and Kidney share the same source. When their Yin drops, the eyes and head dry out and heat up, and the lower body weakens.
tableaux.privilegier: Goji berries, black sesame, black beans, snow fungus (tremella), eggs, pear, chrysanthemum.
tableaux.eviter: Late-night screens, spicy food, alcohol, staying up late.
tableaux.simple: Deep exhaustion: dry eyes, dizziness, tinnitus, weak lower back, feeling warm in the evening.

tableaux.resume: Cold reaches your digestion and the depths of your body: diarrhea at dawn, cold belly and lower back, swelling (edema).
tableaux.mecanisme: Kidney Yang lights the fire that lets the Spleen digest. When both weaken, the whole lower body cools down and water stagnates.
tableaux.privilegier: Slow-cooked dishes, ginger, cinnamon, leek, walnuts, lamb, rice, squash.
tableaux.eviter: Anything cold or raw, ice cream, sodas.
conseils: Hot-water bottle on your belly and lower back in the evening.
tableaux.simple: Your body lacks warmth: diarrhea on waking, cold belly and lower back, swollen legs.

tableaux.resume: Spleen and Lung weak together: tiredness, clear phlegm, poor appetite, one cold after another.
causes: A weak Spleen that no longer nourishes the Lung
tableaux.mecanisme: The Spleen (Earth) nourishes the Lung (Metal). When the Spleen weakens, the Lung follows: you digest poorly and catch colds easily.

principe.fr: Tonify the Lung, strengthen the Spleen

tableaux.privilegier: Chinese yam, rice, millet, chicken, mushrooms, cooked vegetables.
tableaux.eviter: Dairy, sugar, raw food, cold food.
tableaux.simple: Weak defenses and weak digestion together: you catch everything, get out of breath, digest poorly.

tableaux.resume: Blood circulates poorly and congeals: fixed, stabbing pain, painful periods with clots, dark complexion, purplish tongue.
tableaux.mecanisme: “Where Qi goes, Blood follows.” If Qi stagnates or cold congeals it, Blood slows down and comes to a standstill: the pain becomes fixed and stabbing, and periods fill with clots.
tableaux.langue: Purplish or with dark spots, swollen veins under the tongue.

items.pourquoi: Gets Blood moving in the lower belly.
With LR 3, gets Qi and Blood moving.
Frees Qi, which carries Blood along.

tableaux.privilegier: Daily movement, beets, onion, chives, rosebuds, turmeric, a little rice vinegar.
tableaux.eviter: Cold, a sedentary lifestyle, sitting for hours.
conseils: Move every day: stasis dissolves with movement.
tableaux.simple: Your blood circulates poorly: fixed, stabbing pain, periods with clots, dull complexion.
reperes: Aftermath of a fall or blow

tableaux.resume: Cold congeals Blood in the lower belly: very painful periods relieved by warmth, clots, long cycles.
causes: A chill caught in the belly during a period
tableaux.mecanisme: Cold contracts and congeals the Blood of the Uterus: periods become painful, late, with clots, and warmth clearly brings relief.
tableaux.moxa: Moxa or a hot-water bottle recommended, except when periods are heavy.

items.pourquoi: Gets Blood moving in the lower belly.

tableaux.privilegier: Ginger, cinnamon, lamb, slow-cooked dishes, hot drinks.
tableaux.eviter: Cold drinks, ice cream, swimming in cold water during your period.
conseils: Hot-water bottle on your lower belly during your period.
Start the points a few days before your period.
tableaux.simple: Cold has settled in your belly: very painful periods, eased by a hot-water bottle.

tableaux.nom: Wind Bi: pain that moves around
tableaux.resume: Wind dominates: joint pain moves from one place to another from day to day.
causes: Not enough Blood to nourish the joints
tableaux.mecanisme: Wind is mobile: it makes the pain travel from one joint to another.

items.pourquoi: Unblocks the area that hurts today.
“To treat Wind, first treat the Blood.”
Nourishes Blood and gets it moving.

tableaux.privilegier: Warm dishes, foods that nourish Blood.
tableaux.eviter: Drafts, air conditioning blowing on you.
tableaux.simple: Joint pain that moves around from one day to the next.

tableaux.nom: Cold Bi: sharp pain relieved by warmth
tableaux.resume: Cold blocks a joint: sharp, fixed pain, clearly relieved by warmth, worse in cold weather.
tableaux.mecanisme: Cold contracts and blocks: the pain is intense, localized, and melts away with warmth.
tableaux.moxa: Moxa recommended on the painful area.
tableaux.privilegier: Ginger, cinnamon, slow-cooked dishes, lamb, hot baths.
tableaux.eviter: Cold, damp, iced drinks.
conseils: Alternate a brief cold bath with a long hot bath if it brings you relief, and always finish with hot.
tableaux.simple: A joint blocked by cold: sharp pain, relieved by warmth.

tableaux.resume: Dampness weighs down the joints: swelling, heaviness, numbness, worse in damp weather.
causes: A weak Spleen that produces Dampness
tableaux.mecanisme: Dampness is heavy and sticky: it builds up in the joint, which swells and feels heavy.

items.pourquoi: Strengthens the Spleen, which transforms Dampness.

tableaux.privilegier: Pearl barley, adzuki beans, ginger, cooked grains.
tableaux.eviter: Dairy, sugar, fatty food, damp places.
tableaux.simple: Heavy, swollen joints, worse in damp weather.

tableaux.resume: The joint is red, hot, swollen and very painful, sometimes with fever.
tableaux.mecanisme: Heat inflames the joint: redness, heat, swelling and sharp pain.
tableaux.consulter: A red, hot, swollen joint must be seen by a doctor quickly, especially with fever.
tableaux.privilegier: Mung beans, celery, green vegetables, pearl barley.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, spicy food, red meat, local heat.
conseils: Don't massage the inflamed joint directly.
tableaux.simple: A red, hot, swollen joint that is very painful.

tableaux.resume: Wind and Heat agitate the skin: red patches that appear and disappear quickly, intense itching.
tableaux.mecanisme: Wind makes the patches mobile and sudden; Heat makes them red and itchy.

principe.py: Shū fēng qīng rè zhǐ yǎng
principe.fr: Expel Wind, clear Heat, calm itching

tableaux.privilegier: Mung beans, cooked cucumber, green vegetables, water.
tableaux.eviter: Seafood, alcohol, spicy food, foods that have already triggered a reaction in you.
tableaux.simple: Itchy red patches that come and go quickly.

tableaux.resume: Dampness and Heat rise to the skin: weeping eczema, redness, itching, sometimes small blisters.
tableaux.mecanisme: Dampness makes the skin weep; Heat makes it red and itchy: the skin becomes moist and inflamed.
tableaux.privilegier: Pearl barley, mung and adzuki beans, cooked green vegetables.
tableaux.eviter: Sugar, dairy, alcohol, fried food, spicy food.
conseils: Don't scratch: pat the skin or apply gentle cold.
tableaux.simple: The skin weeps, turns red and itches.

tableaux.resume: Blood no longer nourishes the skin: dry skin that itches, especially in the evening, without much redness.
tableaux.mecanisme: Blood moistens the skin. When it runs low, the skin dries out and an “internal Wind” makes it itch.

principe.py: Yǎng xuè rùn zào qū fēng

tableaux.privilegier: Sesame, goji berries, jujubes, eggs, spinach, good oils.
tableaux.eviter: Long, hot showers, harsh soaps.
conseils: Take short, lukewarm showers and moisturize your skin right after.
tableaux.simple: Your skin is dry and itchy, especially in the evening, without much redness.

tableaux.nom: Blood Heat: acne and red spots
tableaux.resume: Heat in the Blood comes out through the skin: red spots, sometimes with pus, skin that feels hot.
tableaux.mecanisme: Heat carried by the Blood rises to the face and upper back and breaks out as red spots.
tableaux.privilegier: Green vegetables, mung beans, celery, cooked cucumber, water.
tableaux.eviter: Sugar, fried food, chocolate, spicy food, alcohol, dairy.
conseils: Don't squeeze your spots.
tableaux.simple: Heat in the blood comes out on the skin: red spots, sometimes with pus.

tableaux.resume: The Lung lacks the strength to breathe, speak and protect you from the cold: short breath, weak voice, one cold after another.
causes: A weak Spleen that no longer nourishes the Lung
Chronic coughs or the tail end of a long illness
Poorly treated colds that let Cold settle in
Long hours hunched over a desk, with cramped breathing
tableaux.mecanisme: The Lung governs breathing and protective Qi. When its Qi runs low, you get short of breath on exertion, your voice weakens and the surface of the body lets wind and cold in: you sweat easily and catch everything going around.
tableaux.langue: Pale or normal, thin white coating.
tableaux.pouls: Empty and weak, especially at the Lung position (right wrist, thumb side).
tableaux.moxa: Moxa is fine (hot-water bottle or moxa on CV 6 and ST 36).

items.pourquoi: Yuan-Source point of the Lung: directly tonifies its Qi.
Tonifies Lung Qi and restores its downward movement; useful when a cough lingers after a cold.
Tonifies the Spleen and Stomach: “Earth nourishes Metal.”
Sea of Qi: tonifies the Qi of the whole body.
Back-Shu point of the Lung: tonifies its Qi.
Back-Shu point of the Spleen: strengthens the source of Qi.
Gentle warmth to build up Qi.

tableaux.privilegier: Warm, cooked dishes, grains, Chinese yam, chicken, mushrooms, a little ginger and onion.
tableaux.eviter: Cold and raw food, too much dairy, tobacco, staying hunched over for long periods.
conseils: Breathe slowly and deeply for 5 minutes a day, shoulders relaxed.
Cover your neck and chest as soon as it turns cool.
tableaux.simple: Weak breath and weak defenses: soft voice, shortness of breath, one cold after another.

tableaux.resume: Lung Qi Deficiency with cold on top: you feel the cold easily, your upper back is cold, the phlegm is clear, and the slightest draft gives you a cold.
causes: The same causes as Lung Qi Deficiency, over a longer time
Repeated exposure to cold (light clothing, cold drinks)
tableaux.mecanisme: The cold comes from a lack of Yang: the Lung no longer warms the chest and upper back, and fluids stagnate as clear phlegm.
tableaux.pouls: Weak, especially at the right thumb position.

items.pourquoi: Yuan-Source point of the Lung: tonifies its Qi.
Tonifies the Lung and helps Qi descend.
Regulates the Qi of the center (digestion) and spreads Yang.
Expels Wind-Cold and tonifies Lung Qi.

tableaux.privilegier: Warm, slow-cooked dishes, ginger, cinnamon, leek, onion, walnuts.
tableaux.eviter: Iced drinks, raw food, tropical fruit in winter, going out with wet hair.
conseils: Keep your upper back covered: a scarf is often enough.
In the morning, rub your upper back against a warm wall or with a hot towel.
tableaux.simple: Weak, cold Lung: you feel the cold, clear runny nose, one cold after another.

tableaux.resume: The Lung lacks fluids: dry cough, dry throat, hoarse voice, a little heat toward the end of the day.
causes: A cough or illness that has dragged on
tableaux.mecanisme: Yin moistens and cools. When the Lung runs short of it, the airways dry out and a mild Deficiency Heat appears in the evening and at night.
tableaux.langue: Red and dry, little or no coating, sometimes cracked at the front.
tableaux.moxa: No moxa: the heat would dry you out even more.

items.pourquoi: With KI 6: opens the Ren Mai and moistens the throat.
Tonifies Lung Yin in chronic conditions.

tableaux.privilegier: Pear, snow fungus (tremella), almonds, honey, sesame, tofu, Chinese yam, soups and stewed fruit.
tableaux.eviter: Strong spices, grilled food, alcohol, tobacco, coffee, overly dry air.
conseils: Humidify the air in your bedroom.
Go to bed before 11 pm: Yin rebuilds itself at night.
tableaux.simple: Your airways lack moisture: a dry cough that lingers, hoarse voice, feeling warm in the evening.

tableaux.resume: Sadness and worry lock Qi in the chest and throat: tight throat, sighing, a feeling of pressure in the chest.
causes: Sadness, grief or worry held inside
Staying hunched over for long periods, breath held back
tableaux.mecanisme: Emotions knot Lung Qi so it no longer flows freely: it gets stuck in the throat (feeling of a lump) and in the chest.
tableaux.langue: Normal or slightly red on the sides of the front part.
tableaux.pouls: Slightly wiry at the Lung position.

items.pourquoi: Frees Lung Qi and releases emotions held inside.
Gathering point of the Qi of the chest.
Transforms the Phlegm clogging the throat.

tableaux.privilegier: Regular meals, citrus zest, radish, spring onion, rose tea.
tableaux.eviter: Eating while brooding, sitting hunched over for hours.
conseils: Walk, sing, breathe deeply: breath gets Lung Qi moving.
Talk about what weighs on you: sadness held inside tightens the throat.
tableaux.simple: Sadness tightens the chest and throat: lump in the throat, sighing, heavy chest.

tableaux.resume: The start of a cold caught from the cold: chills, clear runny nose, sneezing, stiff neck, no sweating.
tableaux.mecanisme: Wind-Cold blocks the surface of the body: the pores close, you shiver without sweating, and the Lung can no longer spread Qi outward, hence the runny nose and the cough.

items.pourquoi: Restores the Lung's spreading function and expels Wind.
Releases the surface and the head.

tableaux.privilegier: Hot drinks, ginger, spring onion, broths; bundle up so you sweat a little.

items.pourquoi: Releases the surface, relieves the throat and head.

tableaux.eviter: Spices, fried food, alcohol, sugar.

tableaux.simple: An infection coming on with heat: sore throat, fever, yellow nasal discharge.

causes: A weak Spleen that produces Dampness
tableaux.mecanisme: “The Spleen produces Phlegm, the Lung stores it.” Dampness that isn't transformed rises and builds up in the Lung.
tableaux.langue: Swollen, with a thick, greasy white coating.

items.pourquoi: Makes Lung Qi descend and transforms phlegm.
Strengthens the Spleen so it stops producing Phlegm.

tableaux.privilegier: White radish (daikon), mandarin peel, ginger, pearl barley, cooked grains.
tableaux.eviter: Dairy, sugar, fried food, bananas, cold drinks.
conseils: Cut out dairy for 2 to 3 weeks and notice the difference.
tableaux.simple: Lots of white phlegm clogs the airways.

tableaux.resume: Thick, sticky yellow phlegm, often after a poorly treated cold or in smokers.
causes: A heat-type cold that never cleared up
tableaux.mecanisme: Heat cooks the Lung's fluids and turns them into thick yellow phlegm that makes breathing harder.
tableaux.langue: Red, with a greasy yellow coating.
tableaux.consulter: If the fever climbs, if breathing becomes difficult or if you cough up blood, see a doctor right away.

items.pourquoi: Front-Mu point of the Lung: frees the chest.

tableaux.privilegier: Pear, white radish, watercress, mushrooms, light broths.
tableaux.eviter: Tobacco, fried food, spices, dairy, sugar, alcohol.
conseils: This is the right time to quit smoking: your Lung is telling you so.
tableaux.simple: Thick yellow phlegm clogs the airways.

tableaux.resume: The Spleen has trouble transforming food: tired after meals, bloating, loose stools, poor appetite.
causes: Irregular meals, eaten on the go or in front of a screen
Too much raw food, cold food, sugar
Worry and long hours of mental work
tableaux.mecanisme: The Spleen extracts Qi from food and distributes it. When it weakens, digestion slows down, the whole body runs short of Qi and Dampness starts to build up.
tableaux.langue: Pale, swollen, with tooth marks on the edges.
tableaux.moxa: Moxa is fine on ST 36 and CV 12.

items.pourquoi: Front-Mu point of the Stomach: tonifies the center (digestion).

tableaux.privilegier: Warm, cooked, regular meals: rice, millet, squash, sweet potato, carrot, dates, chicken.
tableaux.eviter: Raw and cold food, sugar, dairy, snacking, eating in front of a screen.
conseils: Chew thoroughly and put down your fork between bites.
Walk for 10 minutes after lunch.
tableaux.simple: Your digestion lacks strength: you don't absorb what you eat well, so you feel tired and bloated.

tableaux.resume: Spleen Qi Deficiency with cold on top: cold belly, you feel the cold easily, very loose stools, sometimes swelling (edema).
causes: Cold food and drinks every day
tableaux.mecanisme: Without Yang, the Spleen can no longer “cook” food: the belly is cold, the stools contain undigested food and fluids stagnate as swelling (edema).

principe.fr: Warm the center, strengthen the Spleen

items.pourquoi: Warms and tonifies the Spleen and Stomach.

tableaux.privilegier: Ginger, cinnamon, leek, squash, rice, cooked oatmeal, broths, lamb in winter.
tableaux.eviter: Cold drinks, ice cream, raw fruit, salads, walking barefoot on tiled floors.
conseils: Put a hot-water bottle on your belly in the evening.
Start your day with a hot drink.
tableaux.simple: Weak, cold digestion: cold belly, very loose stools, you feel the cold easily.

tableaux.resume: The Spleen no longer has the strength to hold the organs in place: heaviness, organ prolapse, hemorrhoids, chronic diarrhea.
causes: Carrying heavy loads, standing for long periods
tableaux.mecanisme: Spleen Qi naturally moves upward and holds things in place. When it sinks, everything tends to drop: organs, stools, veins.

principe.fr: Tonify the center and raise Qi

tech: Gentle pressure, clockwise rotation, without pressing hard

tableaux.privilegier: As for Spleen Qi Deficiency, plus astragalus (Huang Qi) cooked in broth.
tableaux.eviter: Carrying heavy loads, standing for long periods, straining hard on the toilet.
conseils: Strengthen your pelvic floor: ask your doctor or a midwife for suitable exercises.
tableaux.simple: Your body no longer has the strength to hold things up: a feeling that everything is dropping, organ prolapse, hemorrhoids.

tableaux.resume: A weak Spleen no longer keeps Blood inside the vessels: easy bruising, minor bleeding, heavy periods.
tableaux.mecanisme: Spleen Qi “holds” Blood inside the vessels. When it runs low, Blood escapes: bruises, nosebleeds or bleeding gums, heavy periods.
tableaux.consulter: Unusual bleeding or bruises that appear for no reason call for a blood test: see a doctor.
tableaux.privilegier: Cooked grains, dates, chicken, eggs, cooked vegetables.
tableaux.eviter: Raw and cold food, overwork.
tableaux.simple: Your vessels leak easily: bruises at the slightest bump, minor bleeding, heavy periods.

tableaux.resume: Cold Dampness weighs down digestion: heavy body, full belly, bland, pasty taste in the mouth, little thirst.
causes: Living or working in a damp place
Too much cold and raw food
tableaux.mecanisme: Dampness is heavy and sticky: it blocks the Spleen, weighs down the body and head, and clogs the tongue with a thick coating.
tableaux.privilegier: Pearl barley, adzuki beans, ginger, mandarin peel, radish, rice.
tableaux.eviter: Dairy, sugar, fatty food, too much white bread, cold drinks, damp places.
conseils: Air out and heat your bedroom if it is damp.
tableaux.simple: Heavy, clogged digestion: full belly, pasty mouth, heavy body.

tableaux.nom: Damp-Heat in the Spleen and Stomach
tableaux.resume: Dampness heats up: full belly, nausea, sticky, foul-smelling stools, pasty mouth, sometimes oily skin.
tableaux.mecanisme: Dampness that has been stuck for a long time produces Heat: everything becomes sticky, yellow and smelly.
tableaux.langue: Red, with a greasy yellow coating.
tableaux.privilegier: Pearl barley, mung and adzuki beans, celery, radish, cooked cucumber, rice.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, fried food, sugar, fatty meat, strong spices, dairy.
tableaux.simple: Damp heat in the belly: nausea, sticky, foul-smelling stools, oily skin.

tableaux.resume: The Stomach lacks fluids: hungry but no desire to eat, dry mouth, mild burning pain, tongue cracked in the center.
causes: Meals eaten late at night or in a rush
tableaux.mecanisme: Stomach Yin keeps digestion moist. When it runs low, the Stomach dries out: it burns a little, you feel hungry but can't eat much, and the center of the tongue loses its coating.
tableaux.langue: Red, no coating in the center, crack along the midline.

items.pourquoi: Calms the Stomach, soothes hiccups and nausea.

tableaux.privilegier: Soups, congee, Chinese yam, snow fungus (tremella), pear, tofu, eggs, sesame. Eat at set times.
tableaux.eviter: Spices, coffee, alcohol, grilled food, eating late at night or while working.
conseils: Have dinner before 8 pm, light and warm.
tableaux.simple: Your stomach is dried out: you feel hungry but don't want to eat, dry mouth, a slight burning.

tableaux.resume: Heat burns the Stomach: excessive hunger, thirst for cold drinks, sore gums, bad breath.
causes: Spices, alcohol, grilled meat, fried food
tableaux.mecanisme: Stomach Heat burns through food too fast (constant hunger) and rises along the meridian to the gums and mouth.
tableaux.langue: Red, with a dry yellow coating.

items.pourquoi: Clears Stomach Heat, relieves the gums.

tableaux.privilegier: Green vegetables, cucumber, pear, tofu, mung beans, whole grains, room-temperature water.
tableaux.eviter: Spices, alcohol, coffee, fried food, grilled food, lamb, too much red meat.
tableaux.simple: Your stomach is on fire: excessive hunger, thirst, sore gums, bad breath.

tableaux.resume: Cold blocks the Stomach, often after iced drinks: sharp pain relieved by warmth, nausea, vomiting of clear fluid.
causes: Iced drinks, ice cream, raw food
tableaux.mecanisme: Cold contracts and freezes things in place: the Stomach cramps up, the pain is sharp and eases with warmth.

items.pourquoi: Makes Stomach Qi descend, calms nausea.

tableaux.privilegier: Fresh ginger, hot broths, rice, leek.
tableaux.eviter: Iced drinks, ice cream, raw food, cold fruit.
conseils: A hot-water bottle on your stomach brings quick relief.
tableaux.simple: Your stomach is gripped by cold: sharp pain after an iced drink.

tableaux.resume: Eating too much or too fast: full, painful stomach, sour belching, bad breath, restless sleep.
causes: Meals that are too big or eaten too fast
tableaux.mecanisme: Food stays stuck in the Stomach: Qi no longer descends, it rises as belching and even disturbs sleep.

principe.fr: Aid digestion and make things move down

tableaux.privilegier: Skip a meal or eat light (broth, congee), radish, mandarin peel.
tableaux.eviter: Lying down right after eating, heavy dinners.
conseils: Massage your belly clockwise after meals.
tableaux.simple: Eating too much or too fast: full stomach, belching, digestion at a standstill.
reperes: Upset stomach after a rich meal

tableaux.resume: Stomach Qi rises instead of descending: nausea, hiccups, belching, vomiting.
tableaux.mecanisme: Stomach Qi is supposed to descend. If it is blocked or weakened, it rises: that is the nausea, hiccups and belching.

principe.fr: Harmonize the Stomach, make Qi descend

tableaux.privilegier: Fresh ginger, congee, small warm meals.
tableaux.eviter: Fatty food, big meals, lying down right after eating.
conseils: If you feel nauseous, PC 6 on its own, at any time, often brings quick relief.
tableaux.simple: Your stomach sends things back up instead of digesting: nausea, hiccups, belching, vomiting.

tableaux.resume: The body's underlying fire is weakening: cold in the lower back and legs, abundant clear urine, deep fatigue.
tableaux.mecanisme: Kidney Yang warms the whole body and keeps fluids working. When it drops, the lower body cools down, urine flows clear and abundant, and your underlying energy runs short.
tableaux.pouls: Deep and weak, especially at the Kidney positions.

items.pourquoi: Tonifies the Qi of the whole body.
Warms the Kidney and the lower belly.

tableaux.privilegier: Walnuts, lamb, shrimp, leek, cinnamon, ginger, black beans, chestnuts, slow-cooked dishes.
tableaux.eviter: Cold and raw food, iced drinks, overwork, staying up late, sitting on cold floors.
conseils: Rub your lower back with your palms every evening until it feels warm.
Keep your lower back and feet warm.
tableaux.simple: The body's underlying fire is weakening: cold lower back, abundant urine, deep tiredness.

tableaux.resume: The body's deep fluids are running out: night sweats, hot flashes, tinnitus, weak lower back, dry mouth at night.
causes: Overwork and lack of sleep over many years
tableaux.mecanisme: Kidney Yin is the basis of all the Yin in the body. When it runs out, Deficiency Heat appears in the evening and at night, and the lower body weakens.
tableaux.privilegier: Black beans, black sesame, goji berries, snow fungus (tremella), Chinese yam, eggs, tofu, pear.
tableaux.eviter: Spicy food, alcohol, coffee, sauna, intense exercise in the evening, staying up late.
conseils: Yin rebuilds itself at night: go to bed before 11 pm.
tableaux.simple: Your reserves are running out: night sweats, hot flashes, tinnitus, weak lower back.

tableaux.resume: The Kidney no longer “closes”: frequent urges to urinate, leaks, dribbling urine, white discharge.
tableaux.mecanisme: Kidney Qi keeps the lower gates of the body closed. When it weakens, urine and discharges escape.
tableaux.privilegier: Chinese yam, walnuts, black beans, lotus seeds, chestnuts.
tableaux.eviter: Cold drinks, carrying heavy loads, drinking a lot in the evening.
conseils: Pelvic floor rehabilitation (physical therapy) gives very good results: talk to your doctor about it.
tableaux.simple: Your body doesn't hold things in well anymore: urinary leaks, getting up at night, discharge.
reperes: Getting up at night to urinate

tableaux.resume: The Kidney no longer draws the breath downward: chronic shortness of breath, short breathing, asthma that lingers.
tableaux.mecanisme: The Lung breathes in, and the Kidney “receives” the breath and anchors it low down. When the Kidney weakens, the in-breath stays short and breathlessness sets in.

principe.fr: Tonify the Kidney so it can receive the breath

tableaux.consulter: Chronic shortness of breath must be followed up by a doctor.
tableaux.privilegier: Walnuts, Chinese yam, black beans, chicken, hot dishes.
tableaux.eviter: Tobacco, cold, sudden exertion.
conseils: Belly breathing: breathe in through your nose, letting your belly swell, then breathe out slowly through your mouth.
tableaux.simple: Your breath no longer goes all the way down: chronic shortness of breath, asthma that lingers.

tableaux.resume: Your deep essence is running out: premature aging, early gray hair, poor memory, declining hearing.
tableaux.mecanisme: Jing is our deep reserve, inherited and then maintained. It nourishes the bones, brain, ears and hair: when it declines, everything ages faster.
tableaux.langue: Variable, often pale, or red with no coating.
tableaux.privilegier: Black sesame, black beans, walnuts, goji berries, eggs, bone broths, seaweed.
tableaux.eviter: Overwork, short nights, excess of any kind.
conseils: Jing is easier to preserve than to rebuild: regular sleep, nourishing meals, no excess.
tableaux.simple: Your deep reserves are running out: premature aging, gray hair, declining memory and hearing.

tableaux.resume: Dampness and Heat move down into the Bladder: burning when urinating, frequent and urgent urges, dark urine.
causes: Cold and damp that heat up
tableaux.mecanisme: Damp-Heat blocks the Bladder: urine becomes scanty, dark, burning and urgent.
tableaux.langue: Greasy yellow coating at the back.

principe.py: Qīng lì páng guāng shī rè
principe.fr: Clear and drain Damp-Heat from the Bladder

tableaux.consulter: Burning urination must be seen by a doctor: a urinary tract infection is quick to treat. Go to the emergency room if you have fever, chills, pain in your lower back, or if you are pregnant.
tableaux.privilegier: Drinking plenty of water, mung and adzuki beans, pearl barley, celery, cooked cucumber.
tableaux.eviter: Alcohol, spicy food, coffee, sugar, holding in your urine.
tableaux.simple: Heat and dampness in the bladder: burning when urinating, urgent urges.

tableaux.resume: Dampness and Heat in the intestines: urgent, burning, foul-smelling diarrhea, sometimes with mucus, with belly pain.
tableaux.mecanisme: Damp-Heat blocks the Large Intestine: stools become urgent, burning and foul-smelling.
tableaux.consulter: Blood in the stools, a high fever, signs of dehydration or diarrhea lasting more than 3 days mean you must see a doctor.

items.pourquoi: Front-Mu point of the Large Intestine.
Lower He-Sea point of the Large Intestine.

tableaux.privilegier: Rice, broths, cooked carrot, pearl barley. Drink often, in small sips.
tableaux.eviter: Fatty food, dairy, alcohol, spicy food, raw fruit during the attack.
tableaux.simple: Damp heat in the intestine: urgent, burning, foul-smelling diarrhea.

tableaux.resume: The intestines lack fluids: dry, hard stools that are difficult to pass, dry mouth.
causes: Diet that is too dry, not enough water
tableaux.mecanisme: Without fluids, stools dry out and no longer slide along: this is a “dry” constipation, without sharp pain.
tableaux.langue: Dry, pale, or red with no coating.

principe.fr: Moisten the intestines, ease bowel movements

tableaux.privilegier: Prunes, pear, stewed apple, sesame, almonds, walnuts, spinach, sweet potato, enough water.
tableaux.eviter: Spicy food, grilled food, too much coffee, holding it in when you need to go.
conseils: Massage your belly clockwise for 5 minutes in the morning.
Rest your feet on a small stool when you're on the toilet.
tableaux.simple: Your intestine lacks moisture: dry, hard stools.

tableaux.resume: The intestines lack strength: you feel the urge but struggle to pass stools, you're tired after straining, stools aren't necessarily hard.
causes: Age, the aftermath of an illness
tableaux.mecanisme: Qi pushes the stools along. When it runs low, they move poorly even if they aren't dry, and straining wears you out.
tableaux.privilegier: Sweet potato, cooked grains, prunes, stewed fruit, cooked vegetables.
tableaux.eviter: Raw and cold food, a sedentary lifestyle.
conseils: Go to the toilet at a set time, ideally in the morning after a hot drink.
tableaux.simple: Your intestine lacks strength: the urge is there but passing stools is hard.
